    if n == 0 || length(prediction) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Welford accumulators provide stable variances and covariance in one pass.
    mean_y = zero(L)
    mean_p = zero(L)
    m2_y = zero(L)
    m2_p = zero(L)
    covariance = zero(L)
    target_energy = zero(L)
    squared_error = zero(L)

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        y = L(dataset.y[i])
        p = L(prediction[i])
        if !isfinite(y) || !isfinite(p)
            return L(Inf)
        end

        residual = p - y
        squared_error = muladd(residual, residual, squared_error)
        target_energy = muladd(y, y, target_energy)

        count = L(i)
        delta_y = y - mean_y
        delta_p = p - mean_p
        mean_y += delta_y / count
        mean_p += delta_p / count

        m2_y = muladd(delta_y, y - mean_y, m2_y)
        m2_p = muladd(delta_p, p - mean_p, m2_p)
        covariance = muladd(delta_p, y - mean_y, covariance)
    end

    # Preserve an exact zero optimum even if unrelated moment sums overflow.
    if squared_error == zero(L)
        return zero(L)
    end

    if !isfinite(squared_error) || !isfinite(target_energy) ||
       !isfinite(m2_y) || !isfinite(m2_p) || !isfinite(covariance)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Normalization preserves relative accuracy across differently scaled tasks.
    normalizer = target_energy > zero(L) ? target_energy : L(n)
    normalized_mse = squared_error / normalizer
    if !isfinite(normalized_mse)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # This equals the normalized residual of the best affine fit a*p + b.
    shape_loss = zero(L)
    if m2_y > zero(L)
        shape_loss = one(L)
        if m2_p > zero(L)
            correlation = covariance / sqrt(m2_p) / sqrt(m2_y)
            if !isfinite(correlation)
                return L(Inf)
            end
            bounded_correlation = min(abs(correlation), one(L))
            shape_loss = one(L) - bounded_correlation * bounded_correlation
        end
    end

    # Direct fidelity remains dominant; the shape term supplies early guidance.
    loss_value = L(0.85) * log1p(normalized_mse) + L(0.15) * shape_loss
    return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(loss_value) : L(Inf)
end

niche_crowding_survival_gen3_1.name: niche_crowding_survival_gen3_1
niche_crowding_survival_gen3_1.code:
"""
Niche-crowding survival ("structural fitness sharing").

Motivation: standard age-regularized survival (replace the oldest member) treats every
population slot as interchangeable, so once a particular *family* of expressions (e.g.
everything built from `sin`/`cos`/division) becomes locally competitive, its offspring
tend to dominate the population purely by out-breeding rarer structural forms (like ones
using `exp`, `sqrt`, or `log`) even though those rarer forms might be closer to the true
functional form. This causes the search to get trapped refining constants inside one
functional family instead of trying qualitatively different shapes -- exactly the pattern
seen when the Pareto front repeatedly re-derives sin/cos/rational combinations but never
discovers an `exp(-x^2/2)`-like structure.

This operator implements a lightweight "niching"/fitness-sharing scheme:

1. Compute a coarse structural signature for every population member by checking, on its
   printed expression string, which basic operator/function "flavors" appear
   (`+`,`-`,`*`,`/`,`sin`,`cos`,`exp`,`sqrt`,`log`,`square`/`^`). This avoids depending on
   any internal tree-node API and only uses the public `string` representation.
2. Group all eligible members (i.e. not in `exclude_indices`) by this signature into niches.
3. Find the largest niche -- the structural family currently overrepresented in the
   population.
4. Within that dominant niche, evict the oldest member (age-regularized), mirroring the
   default policy but scoped to the crowded niche only. This leaves small/rare niches
   (including singleton novel structures) untouched, giving them time to be explored and
   refined, while still recycling stale members of overpopulated families.
5. Safety net: if the oldest member in the dominant niche is also the best-cost member of
   the *entire* population, skip it and evict the next-oldest member in that niche instead,
   so we never accidentally discard the current best solution just because it happens to
   share a niche signature with many other members.
"""
function niche_crowding_survival_gen3_1(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Collect eligible indices (not excluded)
    eligible = [i for i in 1:(pop.n) if !(i in exclude_indices)]

    # Fallback: if nothing eligible (shouldn't normally happen), just return oldest overall
    if isempty(eligible)
        BT = typeof(first(pop.members).birth)
        births = [pop.members[i].birth for i in 1:(pop.n)]
        return argmin_fast(births)
    end

    # Step 1: compute a coarse structural signature per eligible member
    function structural_signature(member)::Tuple
        s = string(member.tree)
        return (
            occursin("sin", s),
            occursin("cos", s),
            occursin("exp", s),
            occursin("sqrt", s),
            occursin("log", s),
            occursin("square", s) || occursin("^", s),
            occursin("/", s),
            occursin("*", s),
            occursin("+", s) || occursin("-", s),
        )
    end

    # Step 2: group eligible indices by signature
    niches = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Int}}()
    for i in eligible
        sig = structural_signature(pop.members[i])
        if haskey(niches, sig)
            push!(niches[sig], i)
        else
            niches[sig] = [i]
        end
    end

    # Step 3: find the dominant (largest) niche
    dominant_group = eligible
    max_size = -1
    for (_, group) in niches
        if length(group) > max_size
            max_size = length(group)
            dominant_group = group
        end
    end

    # Step 4: within the dominant niche, pick the oldest member to evict
    # Sort candidates in the dominant niche by birth (ascending -> oldest first)
    sorted_group = sort(dominant_group; by=i -> pop.members[i].birth)

    # Step 5: safety net -- never evict the global best-cost member if an alternative exists
    global_best_idx = argmin_fast([pop.members[i].cost for i in 1:(pop.n)])
    for candidate in sorted_group
        if candidate != global_best_idx
            return candidate
        end
    end

    # If every candidate in the dominant niche happens to be the global best (only possible
    # if the niche has size 1 and equals the best), just return the oldest overall eligible one
    return sorted_group[1]
end

pareto_niche_lineage_survival_gen3_0.name: pareto_niche_lineage_survival_gen3_0
pareto_niche_lineage_survival_gen3_0.code:
"""
    pareto_niche_lineage_survival_gen3_0(pop, options; exclude_indices=Int[])

Select a replacement victim using ecological niches in the loss-complexity plane.
The population is divided into rank-based objective cells so that densely sampled
trade-offs experience more turnover than rare ones. Members receive additional
replacement pressure when they are Pareto-dominated, have poor penalized cost,
are old, or belong to an overrepresented sibling lineage. Unique best-loss and
minimum-complexity endpoints are mildly protected to retain useful stepping
stones without making them immortal.

The method assumes lower loss, cost, and complexity are preferable, birth values
increase over time, and nonpositive parent references denote founders or unknown
parents. Nonfinite losses and costs are treated as worst possible values.
"""
function pareto_niche_lineage_survival_gen3_0(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = pop.n
    n > 0 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot select a survivor from an empty population"))

    # Build an eligibility mask so crossover cannot select the same slot twice.
    eligible = trues(n)
    for i in exclude_indices
        if 1 <= i <= n
            eligible[i] = false
        end
    end
    any(eligible) || throw(ArgumentError("all population indices are excluded"))

    losses = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    costs = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    births = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)

    for i in 1:n
        member = pop.members[i]

        loss = Float64(member.loss)
        cost = Float64(member.cost)
        losses[i] = isfinite(loss) ? loss : Inf
        costs[i] = isfinite(cost) ? cost : Inf

        complexities[i] = Int(compute_complexity(member, options))
        births[i] = Float64(member.birth)
    end

    # Map equal objective values to the same quantile bin. Rank-based bins are
    # insensitive to the often enormous scale differences between benchmark losses.
    rank_bins = function (values, number_of_bins::Int)
        bins = Vector{Int}(undef, length(values))
        order = sortperm(values)
        m = length(values)
        p = 1

        while p <= m
            q = p
            value = values[order[p]]
            while q < m && isequal(values[order[q + 1]], value)
                q += 1
            end

            # Use the tied group's midpoint rank to avoid separating duplicates.
            bin = fld((p + q - 2) * number_of_bins, 2 * m) + 1
            bin = clamp(bin, 1, number_of_bins)
            for k in p:q
                bins[order[k]] = bin
            end
            p = q + 1
        end

        return bins
    end

    # Roughly sqrt(n) bins retain resolution while ensuring meaningful occupancy.
    number_of_bins = max(2, round(Int, sqrt(n / 2)))
    loss_bins = rank_bins(losses, number_of_bins)
    complexity_bins = rank_bins(complexities, number_of_bins)

    cell_counts = Dict{Tuple{Int,Int},Int}()
    for i in 1:n
        key = (loss_bins[i], complexity_bins[i])
        cell_counts[key] = get(cell_counts, key, 0) + 1
    end

    # Mark members dominated in the two objectives (complexity, raw loss).
    # Sorting by complexity makes this O(n log n), rather than comparing all pairs.
    dominated = falses(n)
    objective_order = sortperm(
        collect(1:n);
        by=i -> (complexities[i], losses[i]),
    )

    best_loss_at_lower_complexity = Inf
    p = 1
    while p <= n
        q = p
        complexity = complexities[objective_order[p]]
        while q < n && complexities[objective_order[q + 1]] == complexity
            q += 1
        end

        best_loss_in_group = Inf
        for k in p:q
            best_loss_in_group = min(
                best_loss_in_group,
                losses[objective_order[k]],
            )
        end

        for k in p:q
            i = objective_order[k]
            loss = losses[i]

            # Equal loss at strictly lower complexity dominates; within an equal
            # complexity group, domination requires strictly lower loss.
            dominated[i] =
                best_loss_at_lower_complexity <= loss ||
                best_loss_in_group < loss
        end

        best_loss_at_lower_complexity = min(
            best_loss_at_lower_complexity,
            best_loss_in_group,
        )
        p = q + 1
    end

    # Convert penalized cost to a tied fractional rank in [0, 1].
    cost_rank = zeros(Float64, n)
    cost_order = sortperm(costs)
    p = 1
    while p <= n
        q = p
        value = costs[cost_order[p]]
        while q < n && isequal(costs[cost_order[q + 1]], value)
            q += 1
        end

        midpoint_rank = ((p - 1) + (q - 1)) / 2
        rank_fraction = midpoint_rank / max(n - 1, 1)
        for k in p:q
            cost_rank[cost_order[k]] = rank_fraction
        end
        p = q + 1
    end

    # Repeated offspring from one parent are a useful proxy for a locally
    # over-exploited search basin. Ignore founder/unknown parent references.
    sibling_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for member in pop.members
        if member.parent > 0
            sibling_counts[member.parent] =
                get(sibling_counts, member.parent, 0) + 1
        end
    end

    oldest_birth = minimum(births)
    newest_birth = maximum(births)
    birth_span = newest_birth - oldest_birth

    best_loss = minimum(losses)
    best_loss_count = count(x -> isequal(x, best_loss), losses)
    minimum_complexity = minimum(complexities)
    minimum_complexity_count = count(==(minimum_complexity), complexities)

    # Frequency-aware tournaments already provide some complexity diversity, so
    # reduce—but do not remove—the independent objective-niche pressure.
    density_weight = options.use_frequency_in_tournament ? 0.90 : 1.25
    maximum_size = max(Int(options.maxsize), 1)

    best_index = findfirst(eligible)
    best_score = -Inf

    for i in 1:n
        eligible[i] || continue

        member = pop.members[i]
        cell_size = cell_counts[(loss_bins[i], complexity_bins[i])]
        oldness = birth_span > 0 ? (newest_birth - births[i]) / birth_span : 0.0

        sibling_count = member.parent > 0 ?
            get(sibling_counts, member.parent, 1) : 1

        score =
            density_weight * log1p(cell_size - 1) +
            (dominated[i] ? 1.50 : 0.0) +
            0.65 * cost_rank[i] +
            0.55 * oldness +
            0.35 * log1p(sibling_count - 1)

        # High complexity is only weakly penalized here, and only when already
        # dominated, so potentially necessary complex stepping stones can survive.
        if dominated[i]
            relative_complexity = clamp(
                complexities[i] / Float64(maximum_size),
                0.0,
                1.0,
            )
            score += 0.25 * relative_complexity
        end

        # Protect objective endpoints most strongly when they are unique; duplicate
        # endpoints receive little protection and can still be recycled.
        if isequal(losses[i], best_loss)
            score -= 1.25 / sqrt(best_loss_count)
        end
        if complexities[i] == minimum_complexity
            score -= 0.40 / sqrt(minimum_complexity_count)
        end

        if score > best_score
            best_score = score
            best_index = i
        end
    end

    return best_index
end

mse_safe_loss_gen3_4.name: mse_safe_loss_gen3_4
mse_safe_loss_gen3_4.code:
"""
Custom Loss: mse_safe_loss_gen3_4
==========================
Core idea: keep the parent's per-sample MSE objective (no complexity
penalty, no reweighting), but harden it against two failure modes that slip
through the `completed` flag returned by `eval_tree_array`:

1. **Silent non-finite predictions.** Some operators (e.g. `pow`, `log`,
   `div`) can produce `NaN`/`Inf` outputs on certain rows while still
   reporting `completed = true` (the "completed" flag only tracks internal
   overflow guards during evaluation, not the final numeric values). The
   parent would happily square and sum these, letting `NaN` propagate into
   the loss and silently poisoning the Pareto front / tournament selection.
   Here we explicitly check for non-finite predictions and reject such
   trees with `L(Inf)`, matching the treatment of outright evaluation
   failures.
2. **Allocation overhead.** The parent materializes a temporary `diff`
   vector before reducing. We instead use a single-pass `mapreduce`, which
   avoids the extra allocation and touches memory once instead of twice —
   this matters because loss evaluation is the hot path of the search.

No complexity penalty is introduced; the returned value is still a plain
per-sample MSE, so `loss_to_cost` and the Pareto frontier behave exactly as
they do for the parent, just with more robust handling of degenerate
predictions and a slightly cheaper reduction.
"""
function mse_safe_loss_gen3_4(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    # Reject outright evaluation failures immediately, as in the parent.
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = length(prediction)
    # Guard against degenerate empty predictions (shouldn't happen, but avoid div-by-zero).
    if n == 0
        return L(Inf)
    end

    y = dataset.y
    # Single-pass accumulation of squared error and a finiteness check,
    # avoiding the allocation of an intermediate `diff` vector.
    total = zero(L)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = prediction[i]
        # Any non-finite prediction (NaN/Inf) marks the tree as unusable,
        # even if `eval_tree_array` reported `completed = true`.
        if !isfinite(p)
            return L(Inf)
        end
        d = p - y[i]
        total += abs2(d)
    end

    return L(total / n)
end

pareto_niche_age_regularized_survival_ge.name: pareto_niche_age_regularized_survival_gen3_5
pareto_niche_age_regularized_survival_ge.code:
"""
    pareto_niche_age_regularized_survival_gen3_5(
        pop::Population{T,L,N},
        options::AbstractOptions;
        exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
    )::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}

Synthesized multi-objective survival operator combining Age-Regularized Evolution
(Parent 1) with Pareto Dominance Shielding, Complexity-Niche De-duplication, and
Numerical Sanitation (Parent 2).

# Core Idea
Standard age-regularized evolution (Parent 1) guarantees steady evolutionary turnover
by evicting the oldest individual, but is oblivious to whether that individual is a vital
Pareto stepping-stone or a bloated, sub-optimal duplicate. Parent 2 introduces multi-objective
eviction based on Pareto dominance and complexity crowding.

This operator synthesizes the two into an adaptive survival policy that:
1. **Sanitizes Population Instantly**: Prioritizes immediate eviction of non-finite (NaN/Inf)
   solutions before evaluating valid candidates.
2. **Eliminates Redundant Clones & Taylor-Series Bloat**: Detects near-identical loss duplicates
   and heavily penalizes redundant sub-optimal copies within the same or higher complexity tiers,
   preventing population stagnation in polynomial bloat traps.
3. **Shields the Empirical Pareto Frontier**: Protects non-dominated solutions across all
   complexity niches from premature eviction, preserving vital structural stepping stones.
4. **Smoothly Degenerates to Age-Regularized Evolution**: For non-dominated, uniquely distributed
   individuals across complexity bins, dominance, crowding, and duplicate penalties vanish to
   zero, reducing the selection strictly to age-based turnover (argmin birth) as in Parent 1.

# Steps
1. Filter out `exclude_indices` and check for invalid numbers for immediate replacement.
2. Extract complexities, losses, and birth orders across all population members.
3. Identify numerical duplicates (near-identical losses at equal or higher complexity).
4. Compute Pareto dominance counts (how many population members strictly dominate candidate `i`).
5. Measure intra-bin loss gap and density for complexity-niche crowding.
6. Calculate a composite eviction priority score and replace the highest-priority member.

# Returns
- `Int`: The 1-based index of the population member chosen for replacement.
"""
function pareto_niche_age_regularized_survival_gen3_5(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = pop.n
    n <= 0 && return 1

    # Safe fallback index respecting exclusion constraints
    fallback_idx = 1
    for i in 1:n
        if !(i in exclude_indices)
            fallback_idx = i
            break
        end
    end

    # Pre-allocate feature vectors for fast vectorised evaluation
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    losses = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    births = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    is_invalid = Vector{Bool}(undef, n)

    min_birth = typemax(Int)
    max_birth = typemin(Int)

    # Step 1: Feature extraction & immediate sanitation of non-finite solutions
    for i in 1:n
        member = pop.members[i]
        comp = compute_complexity(member, options)
        loss = Float64(member.loss)
        cost = Float64(member.cost)
        birth = member.birth

        complexities[i] = comp
        losses[i] = loss
        births[i] = birth

        # Detect numerical anomalies (NaN / Inf in loss or cost)
        invalid = isnan(loss) || isinf(loss) || isnan(cost) || isinf(cost)
        is_invalid[i] = invalid

        if !(i in exclude_indices)
            # Immediate eviction of invalid members to keep population healthy
            invalid && return i

            if birth < min_birth
                min_birth = birth
            end
            if birth > max_birth
                max_birth = birth
            end
        end
    end

    # Degenerate case: all valid members excluded
    if min_birth > max_birth
        return fallback_idx
    end

    birth_span = max(1, max_birth - min_birth)

    # Step 2: Detect duplicate solutions (near-identical loss with >= complexity)
    # Penalizes redundant clones that clog the search space
    is_duplicate = zeros(Float64, n)
    for i in 1:n
        (i in exclude_indices || is_invalid[i]) && continue
        loss_i = losses[i]
        comp_i = complexities[i]
        for j in 1:n
            (j == i || is_invalid[j]) && continue
            loss_j = losses[j]
            comp_j = complexities[j]

            # Relative numerical tolerance check for identical loss evaluation
            tol = 1e-10 * (max(abs(loss_i), abs(loss_j)) + 1e-8)
            if abs(loss_i - loss_j) <= tol
                # If j has lower complexity, or equal complexity but is younger/preferred, i is redundant
                if comp_j < comp_i || (comp_j == comp_i && (loss_j < loss_i || (loss_j == loss_i && births[j] > births[i])))
                    is_duplicate[i] = 1.0
                    break
                end
            end
        end
    end

    # Step 3: Compute Pareto Dominance Counts
    # Solution j strictly dominates solution i if (comp_j <= comp_i && loss_j <= loss_i)
    # with at least one strict inequality.
    dom_counts = zeros(Int, n)
    max_dom = 0
    for i in 1:n
        (i in exclude_indices || is_invalid[i]) && continue
        comp_i = complexities[i]
        loss_i = losses[i]
        d_count = 0
        for j in 1:n
            (j == i || is_invalid[j]) && continue
            comp_j = complexities[j]
            loss_j = losses[j]
            if (comp_j <= comp_i && loss_j <= loss_i) && (comp_j < comp_i || loss_j < loss_i)
                d_count += 1
            end
        end
        dom_counts[i] = d_count
        if d_count > max_dom
            max_dom = d_count
        end
    end

    # Step 4: Compute Complexity-Niche Crowding Penalty
    # Computes relative sub-optimality of candidate i within its complexity niche
    crowding_scores = zeros(Float64, n)
    for i in 1:n
        (i in exclude_indices || is_invalid[i]) && continue
        comp_i = complexities[i]
        loss_i = losses[i]

        bin_count = 0
        min_bin_loss = loss_i
        max_bin_loss = loss_i

        for j in 1:n
            is_invalid[j] && continue
            if complexities[j] == comp_i
                bin_count += 1
                if losses[j] < min_bin_loss
                    min_bin_loss = losses[j]
                end
                if losses[j] > max_bin_loss
                    max_bin_loss = losses[j]
                end
            end
        end

        # Crowding applies when multiple members share the same complexity niche
        if bin_count > 1
            loss_gap = max_bin_loss - min_bin_loss
            intra_rank = loss_gap > 1e-12 ? ((loss_i - min_bin_loss) / loss_gap) : 0.5
            density_factor = bin_count / n
            crowding_scores[i] = intra_rank * density_factor
        end
    end

    # Step 5: Multi-Objective Eviction Priority Synthesis
    # Combines Age turnover (Parent 1) with Dominance shielding, niche crowding,
    # and duplicate pruning (Parent 2).
    #
    # Weights balance exploration turnover vs. stepping-stone preservation:
    w_age   = 0.35   # Base aging turnover pressure (Parent 1)
    w_dom   = 0.35   # Pareto dominance penalty (preserves non-dominated front)
    w_crowd = 0.20   # Niche crowding penalty (clears redundant intra-bin clutter)
    w_dup   = 0.10   # Exact/near duplicate penalty (combats stagnation bloat)

    best_eviction_score = -Inf
    best_idx = fallback_idx

    for i in 1:n
        (i in exclude_indices) && continue

        # Normalized age: 1.0 for oldest member, 0.0 for youngest member
        norm_age = (max_birth - births[i]) / birth_span

        # Normalized dominance: 0.0 for empirical Pareto-optimal stepping stones
        norm_dom = max_dom > 0 ? (dom_counts[i] / max_dom) : 0.0

        # Crowding and duplicate penalties
        norm_crowd = crowding_scores[i]
        norm_dup = is_duplicate[i]

        # Composite eviction score: higher value indicates higher priority for eviction
        eviction_score = (w_age * norm_age) +
                         (w_dom * norm_dom) +
                         (w_crowd * norm_crowd) +
                         (w_dup * norm_dup)

        if eviction_score > best_eviction_score
            best_eviction_score = eviction_score
            best_idx = i
        end
    end

    return best_idx
end

algebraic_canonicalizing_refactor_mutati.code:
"""
    algebraic_canonicalizing_refactor_mutation_gen3_6(tree, options, nfeatures, rng)

A *semantics-preserving* structural mutation that rewrites an expression with
elementary algebraic identities instead of perturbing it randomly.

Motivation (unchanged from the parent): PySR's built-in mutations are strictly *local*
edits, so two algebraically identical but structurally distant forms — e.g.
`x1*x2 + x1*x3` vs. `x1*(x2 + x3)`, or `(2*x1)*3` vs. `x1*6` — are separated by many
individually-deleterious steps. Ground-truth expressions in SRBench/Feynman-style
benchmarks are written in compact, factored, constant-folded form, so a population that
has already found the right *semantics* in a bloated form sits on a complexity plateau
it cannot descend gradually. This operator performs that algebraic "jump" in one move:
loss is (nearly) unchanged while complexity usually drops, so it behaves as a neutral
drift / simplification operator that both compresses good expressions and re-shapes them
so that later local mutations explore a different neighbourhood.

Algorithm:
1. Locate `+ - * /` (identity comparison) and, by *base name* (stripping the `safe_`
   prefix PySR adds), `^` plus the unary ops `exp, log, sqrt, square, ...`.
2. Traverse the whole tree once and collect every applicable rewrite site as
   `(node, freshly-built replacement subtree, weight, is_expansion)`. Replacements are
   built exclusively from `copy`s of grandchildren, so in-place `set_node!` can never
   create aliasing (this also handles `node === tree`, i.e. the root, for free).
3. With small probability take a single *expanding* rewrite (distribution); otherwise
   run a short *cascade* of non-expanding rewrites (rescanning after each application,
   stopping stochastically) so that a single mutation call can fully simplify a tree.

Rewrite catalogue (weights in parentheses; the sampler additionally multiplies the
weight by `1 + 0.6 * (nodes_removed)` so genuinely compressing moves dominate):
* constant folding of binary and unary nodes (5) — new;
* neutral/absorbing elements `a+0, a-0, a*1, a*0, a/1, 0/a, a^1, a^0, a-a, a/a` (5) — new;
* exact sum cancellation `(a±b)∓b -> a`, `a-(a-b) -> b` (5);
* multiplicative cancellation `(a*b)/a -> b`, `(a/b)*b -> a`, `(a*k)/(b*k) -> a/b`,
  `a/(b*a) -> 1/b` (4–5) — last two are new;
* factoring `a*b ± a*c -> a*(b±c)` (3), plus the new implicit-coefficient variants
  `a*b ± a -> a*(b±1)` and `a + a -> 2*a` (2), which expose a coefficient to the
  constant optimizer;
* common denominator `a/c ± b/c -> (a±b)/c` (3);
* transcendental fusion `log a + log b -> log(ab)`, `log a - log b -> log(a/b)`,
  `exp a * exp b -> exp(a+b)`, `exp a / exp b -> exp(a-b)`, `√a*√b -> √(ab)` (3) — new;
* inverse unary-pair cancellation `exp(log x) -> x`, `atan(tan x) -> x`, ... (4) — new;
* constant-chain merging `(a±k1)±k2 -> a+k`, `(a*k1)/k2 -> a*k`, ... (4) — new;
* canonical constant placement `k+a -> a+k`, `k*a -> a*k` (1.5) — new, size-neutral but
  it is what lets the merging rules above fire;
* division folding/lifting `(a/b)/c -> a/(b*c)`, `a/(b/c) -> (a*c)/b` (2);
* expansions (rare, only if they fit in `options.maxsize`): `a*(b±c) -> a*b ± a*c` and
  the new `(b±c)/a -> b/a ± c/a`, kept because they are sometimes the precursor that
  lets a later factoring discover a *different* common factor.

What changed vs. the parent: (i) many more rules — constant folding, identities,
constant-chain merging, log/exp/sqrt fusion, inverse-unary cancellation, quotient-level
cancellation and implicit-coefficient factoring; (ii) a *cascade* driver that can apply
several simplifications in one call instead of exactly one rewrite, which is what turns
a bloated-but-accurate tree into its canonical form in a single mutation; (iii) weights
now depend on the measured node reduction rather than being fixed per rule;
(iv) expansions are separated out and drawn only with probability 0.15, and (v) the
operator no longer bails out when `*`/`/` are absent, since folding/identity rules still
apply. Cancellation rules assume the cancelled subtree is non-zero (generic-position
assumption); any rewrite that does change the loss is still filtered by PySR's usual
accept/reject step.
"""
function algebraic_canonicalizing_refactor_mutation_gen3_6(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    tree.degree == 0 && return tree

    binops = options.operators.binops
    unaops = options.operators.unaops

    # ---- operator lookup -------------------------------------------------------
    plus_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (+), binops)
    minus_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (-), binops)
    times_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (*), binops)
    div_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (/), binops)

    # PySR wraps many operators (`log` -> `safe_log`, `^` -> `safe_pow`, ...), so we
    # match on the *base* name rather than on the function object.
    function base_name(f)
        s = string(f)
        startswith(s, "safe_") && (s = s[6:end])
        return s
    end
    pow_idx = findfirst(op -> base_name(op) in ("^", "pow", "pow_abs"), binops)

    # name of each unary operator, for the fusion / inverse-pair rules
    una_names = ntuple(i -> base_name(unaops[i]), length(unaops))
    find_una(nm) = findfirst(i -> una_names[i] == nm, 1:length(una_names))
    exp_idx = find_una("exp")
    log_idx = find_una("log")
    sqrt_idx = find_una("sqrt")

    # f(g(x)) -> x for these ordered (outer, inner) name pairs
    inv_pairs = (
        ("exp", "log"),
        ("log", "exp"),
        ("sqrt", "square"),
        ("square", "sqrt"),
        ("sin", "asin"),
        ("asin", "sin"),
        ("tan", "atan"),
        ("atan", "tan"),
        ("sinh", "asinh"),
        ("asinh", "sinh"),
        ("tanh", "atanh"),
        ("atanh", "tanh"),
        ("neg", "neg"),
        ("inv", "inv"),
    )
    function is_inverse_pair(outer_op::Integer, inner_op::Integer)
        (outer_op <= length(una_names) && inner_op <= length(una_names)) || return false
        return (una_names[outer_op], una_names[inner_op]) in inv_pairs
    end

    # ---- structural (syntactic) equality of two subtrees ------------------------
    function trees_equal(a::N, b::N)
        a.degree == b.degree || return false
        if a.degree == 0
            a.constant == b.constant || return false
            return a.constant ? (a.val == b.val) : (a.feature == b.feature)
        end
        a.op == b.op || return false
        for i in 1:(a.degree)
            trees_equal(get_child(a, i), get_child(b, i)) || return false
        end
        return true
    end

    # ---- cheap predicates / constructors ---------------------------------------
    is_plus(t) = t.degree == 2 && plus_idx !== nothing && t.op == plus_idx
    is_minus(t) = t.degree == 2 && minus_idx !== nothing && t.op == minus_idx
    is_sum(t) = is_plus(t) || is_minus(t)
    is_times(t) = t.degree == 2 && times_idx !== nothing && t.op == times_idx
    is_div(t) = t.degree == 2 && div_idx !== nothing && t.op == div_idx
    is_pow(t) = t.degree == 2 && pow_idx !== nothing && t.op == pow_idx

    bin(op, a, b) = constructorof(N)(; op=op, children=(a, b))
    una(op, a) = constructorof(N)(; op=op, children=(a,))
    cst(v) = constructorof(N)(T; val=convert(T, v))

    isconstleaf(t) = t.degree == 0 && t.constant
    is_val(t, v) = isconstleaf(t) && t.val == v

    # numeric folding helpers: reject failures, non-finite and absurdly large results
    function ok_value(y)
        yy = try
            convert(T, y)
        catch
            return nothing
        end
        isfinite(yy) || return nothing
        (abs(yy) < 1e12) || return nothing
        return yy
    end
    function try_bin(i, a, b)
        y = try
            binops[i](a, b)
        catch
            return nothing
        end
        return ok_value(y)
    end
    function try_una(i, a)
        y = try
            unaops[i](a)
        catch
            return nothing
        end
        return ok_value(y)
    end

    # ---- candidate site bookkeeping --------------------------------------------
    sites = Tuple{N,N}[]
    weights = Float64[]
    expands = Bool[]

    function add_site!(node, repl, w; expand::Bool=false)
        if !expand
            # reward rewrites that actually delete nodes
            d = count_nodes(node) - count_nodes(repl)
            w *= 1.0 + 0.6 * max(0, d)
        end
        push!(sites, (node, repl))
        push!(weights, w)
        push!(expands, expand)
        return nothing
    end

    maxsize = hasproperty(options, :maxsize) ? options.maxsize : 30

    # ---- one full scan of the tree, filling `sites` -----------------------------
    function scan!()
        empty!(sites)
        empty!(weights)
        empty!(expands)
        total = count_nodes(tree)

        # `any(f, tree)` visits every node as long as we keep returning `false`
        any(tree) do t
            if t.degree == 1
                c = get_child(t, 1)
                # (U1) fold a constant under a unary operator
                if isconstleaf(c)
                    v = try_una(t.op, c.val)
                    v === nothing || add_site!(t, cst(v), 5.0)
                end
                # (U2) cancel an inverse unary pair: exp(log x) -> x, etc.
                if c.degree == 1 && is_inverse_pair(t.op, c.op)
                    add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c, 1)), 4.0)
                end

            elseif t.degree == 2
                c1 = get_child(t, 1)
                c2 = get_child(t, 2)

                # (B0) constant folding
                if isconstleaf(c1) && isconstleaf(c2)
                    v = try_bin(t.op, c1.val, c2.val)
                    v === nothing || add_site!(t, cst(v), 5.0)
                end

                # (B1) neutral / absorbing elements and self-cancellation
                if is_plus(t)
                    is_val(c2, 0) && add_site!(t, copy(c1), 5.0)
                    is_val(c1, 0) && add_site!(t, copy(c2), 5.0)
                elseif is_minus(t)
                    is_val(c2, 0) && add_site!(t, copy(c1), 5.0)
                    trees_equal(c1, c2) && add_site!(t, cst(zero(T)), 5.0)
                elseif is_times(t)
                    is_val(c2, 1) && add_site!(t, copy(c1), 5.0)
                    is_val(c1, 1) && add_site!(t, copy(c2), 5.0)
                    (is_val(c1, 0) || is_val(c2, 0)) && add_site!(t, cst(zero(T)), 5.0)
                elseif is_div(t)
                    is_val(c2, 1) && add_site!(t, copy(c1), 5.0)
                    is_val(c1, 0) && add_site!(t, cst(zero(T)), 5.0)
                    trees_equal(c1, c2) && add_site!(t, cst(one(T)), 5.0)
                elseif is_pow(t)
                    is_val(c2, 1) && add_site!(t, copy(c1), 5.0)
                    is_val(c2, 0) && add_site!(t, cst(one(T)), 5.0)
                end

                # (B2) exact cancellation inside sums
                if is_minus(t)
                    if is_plus(c1)
                        trees_equal(get_child(c1, 2), c2) &&
                            add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), 5.0)
                        trees_equal(get_child(c1, 1), c2) &&
                            add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 2)), 5.0)
                    end
                    # a - (a - b) -> b
                    if is_minus(c2) && trees_equal(c1, get_child(c2, 1))
                        add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c2, 2)), 5.0)
                    end
                elseif is_plus(t)
                    if is_minus(c1) && trees_equal(get_child(c1, 2), c2)
                        add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), 5.0)
                    end
                    if is_minus(c2) && trees_equal(get_child(c2, 2), c1)
                        add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c2, 1)), 5.0)
                    end
                end

                # (B3) factor a shared multiplicative term out of a sum
                if is_sum(t) && times_idx !== nothing
                    if is_times(c1) && is_times(c2)
                        # a*b ± a*c -> a*(b±c) (any of the four factor orderings)
                        for i in 1:2, j in 1:2
                            if trees_equal(get_child(c1, i), get_child(c2, j))
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        times_idx,
                                        copy(get_child(c1, i)),
                                        bin(
                                            t.op,
                                            copy(get_child(c1, 3 - i)),
                                            copy(get_child(c2, 3 - j)),
                                        ),
                                    ),
                                    3.0,
                                )
                                break  # one factoring per node is enough
                            end
                        end
                    elseif is_times(c1)
                        # a*b ± a -> a*(b±1): exposes an explicit coefficient
                        for i in 1:2
                            if trees_equal(get_child(c1, i), c2)
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        times_idx,
                                        copy(c2),
                                        bin(t.op, copy(get_child(c1, 3 - i)), cst(one(T))),
                                    ),
                                    2.0,
                                )
                                break
                            end
                        end
                    elseif is_times(c2)
                        # a ± a*b -> a*(1±b)
                        for j in 1:2
                            if trees_equal(get_child(c2, j), c1)
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        times_idx,
                                        copy(c1),
                                        bin(t.op, cst(one(T)), copy(get_child(c2, 3 - j))),
                                    ),
                                    2.0,
                                )
                                break
                            end
                        end
                    elseif is_plus(t) && trees_equal(c1, c2)
                        # a + a -> 2*a (gives the constant optimizer something to tune)
                        add_site!(t, bin(times_idx, cst(one(T) + one(T)), copy(c1)), 2.0)
                    end
                end

                # (B4) common denominator: a/c ± b/c -> (a±b)/c
                if is_sum(t) &&
                    is_div(c1) &&
                    is_div(c2) &&
                    trees_equal(get_child(c1, 2), get_child(c2, 2))
                    add_site!(
                        t,
                        bin(
                            div_idx,
                            bin(t.op, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), copy(get_child(c2, 1))),
                            copy(get_child(c1, 2)),
                        ),
                        3.0,
                    )
                end

                # (B5) cancellations and restructurings around a quotient
                if is_div(t)
                    if is_times(c1)
                        # (a*b)/a -> b and (a*b)/b -> a
                        if trees_equal(get_child(c1, 1), c2)
                            add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 2)), 5.0)
                        elseif trees_equal(get_child(c1, 2), c2)
                            add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), 5.0)
                        end
                    end
                    if is_times(c1) && is_times(c2)
                        # (a*k)/(b*k) -> a/b
                        for i in 1:2, j in 1:2
                            if trees_equal(get_child(c1, i), get_child(c2, j))
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        div_idx,
                                        copy(get_child(c1, 3 - i)),
                                        copy(get_child(c2, 3 - j)),
                                    ),
                                    4.0,
                                )
                                break
                            end
                        end
                    end
                    if is_times(c2)
                        # a/(b*a) -> 1/b
                        for j in 1:2
                            if trees_equal(get_child(c2, j), c1)
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        div_idx, cst(one(T)), copy(get_child(c2, 3 - j))
                                    ),
                                    3.0,
                                )
                                break
                            end
                        end
                    end
                    # fold nested divisions: (a/b)/c -> a/(b*c)
                    if is_div(c1) && times_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            bin(
                                div_idx,
                                copy(get_child(c1, 1)),
                                bin(times_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 2)), copy(c2)),
                            ),
                            2.0,
                        )
                    end
                    # lift an inner division: a/(b/c) -> (a*c)/b
                    if is_div(c2) && times_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            bin(
                                div_idx,
                                bin(times_idx, copy(c1), copy(get_child(c2, 2))),
                                copy(get_child(c2, 1)),
                            ),
                            2.0,
                        )
                    end
                end

                # (B6) multiplicative cancellation: (a/b)*b -> a and b*(a/b) -> a
                if is_times(t)
                    if is_div(c1) && trees_equal(get_child(c1, 2), c2)
                        add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), 5.0)
                    elseif is_div(c2) && trees_equal(get_child(c2, 2), c1)
                        add_site!(t, copy(get_child(c2, 1)), 5.0)
                    end
                end

                # (B7) transcendental fusion (all strictly size-reducing)
                if log_idx !== nothing &&
                    c1.degree == 1 &&
                    c2.degree == 1 &&
                    c1.op == log_idx &&
                    c2.op == log_idx
                    if is_plus(t) && times_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            una(
                                log_idx,
                                bin(
                                    times_idx,
                                    copy(get_child(c1, 1)),
                                    copy(get_child(c2, 1)),
                                ),
                            ),
                            3.0,
                        )
                    elseif is_minus(t) && div_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            una(
                                log_idx,
                                bin(
                                    div_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), copy(get_child(c2, 1))
                                ),
                            ),
                            3.0,
                        )
                    end
                end
                if exp_idx !== nothing &&
                    c1.degree == 1 &&
                    c2.degree == 1 &&
                    c1.op == exp_idx &&
                    c2.op == exp_idx
                    if is_times(t) && plus_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            una(
                                exp_idx,
                                bin(
                                    plus_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), copy(get_child(c2, 1))
                                ),
                            ),
                            3.0,
                        )
                    elseif is_div(t) && minus_idx !== nothing
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            una(
                                exp_idx,
                                bin(
                                    minus_idx,
                                    copy(get_child(c1, 1)),
                                    copy(get_child(c2, 1)),
                                ),
                            ),
                            3.0,
                        )
                    end
                end
                if sqrt_idx !== nothing &&
                    is_times(t) &&
                    c1.degree == 1 &&
                    c2.degree == 1 &&
                    c1.op == sqrt_idx &&
                    c2.op == sqrt_idx
                    add_site!(
                        t,
                        una(
                            sqrt_idx,
                            bin(times_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), copy(get_child(c2, 1))),
                        ),
                        3.0,
                    )
                end

                # (B8) merge two constants living in the same +/- or */ chain
                if plus_idx !== nothing &&
                    isconstleaf(c2) &&
                    (is_plus(t) || is_minus(t)) &&
                    (is_plus(c1) || is_minus(c1)) &&
                    isconstleaf(get_child(c1, 2))
                    k1 = get_child(c1, 2).val
                    k2 = c2.val
                    s1 = is_plus(c1) ? one(T) : -one(T)
                    s2 = is_plus(t) ? one(T) : -one(T)
                    kk = ok_value(s1 * k1 + s2 * k2)
                    kk === nothing || add_site!(
                        t, bin(plus_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), cst(kk)), 4.0
                    )
                end
                if times_idx !== nothing &&
                    isconstleaf(c2) &&
                    (is_times(t) || is_div(t)) &&
                    (is_times(c1) || is_div(c1)) &&
                    isconstleaf(get_child(c1, 2))
                    k1 = get_child(c1, 2).val
                    k2 = c2.val
                    raw = if is_times(c1) && is_times(t)
                        k1 * k2                       # (a*k1)*k2
                    elseif is_times(c1) && is_div(t)
                        k2 == 0 ? nothing : k1 / k2   # (a*k1)/k2
                    elseif is_div(c1) && is_times(t)
                        k1 == 0 ? nothing : k2 / k1   # (a/k1)*k2
                    else
                        (k1 == 0 || k2 == 0) ? nothing : one(T) / (k1 * k2)  # (a/k1)/k2
                    end
                    if raw !== nothing
                        kk = ok_value(raw)
                        kk === nothing || add_site!(
                            t, bin(times_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), cst(kk)), 4.0
                        )
                    end
                end

                # (B9) canonical constant placement for the commutative ops; size-neutral
                # but it is what enables (B8) to fire on the next cascade pass.
                if (is_plus(t) || is_times(t)) && isconstleaf(c1) && !isconstleaf(c2)
                    add_site!(t, bin(t.op, copy(c2), copy(c1)), 1.5)
                end

                # (B10) distribution a*(b±c) -> a*b ± a*c  (size-increasing)
                if is_times(t)
                    for k in 1:2
                        s = get_child(t, k)        # candidate sum
                        m = get_child(t, 3 - k)    # factor that gets duplicated
                        if is_sum(s)
                            nm = count_nodes(m)
                            # keep the duplicated factor tiny and respect the budget
                            if nm <= 3 && total + nm + 1 <= maxsize
                                add_site!(
                                    t,
                                    bin(
                                        s.op,
                                        bin(times_idx, copy(m), copy(get_child(s, 1))),
                                        bin(times_idx, copy(m), copy(get_child(s, 2))),
                                    ),
                                    1.0;
                                    expand=true,
                                )
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end

                # (B11) split a quotient over a sum: (b±c)/a -> b/a ± c/a (size-increasing)
                if is_div(t) && is_sum(c1)
                    nd = count_nodes(c2)
                    if nd <= 3 && total + nd + 1 <= maxsize
                        add_site!(
                            t,
                            bin(
                                c1.op,
                                bin(div_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 1)), copy(c2)),
                                bin(div_idx, copy(get_child(c1, 2)), copy(c2)),
                            ),
                            1.0;
                            expand=true,
                        )
                    end
                end
            end
            return false  # never short-circuit: we want a complete traversal
        end
        return nothing
    end

    # weighted choice restricted to the indices in `idxs`
    function pick(idxs)
        wsum = 0.0
        for i in idxs
            wsum += weights[i]
        end
        r = rand(rng) * wsum
        acc = 0.0
        for i in idxs
            acc += weights[i]
            r <= acc && return i
        end
        return idxs[end]
    end

    scan!()
    isempty(sites) && return tree  # no identity applies -> leave the tree untouched

    # Occasionally take a single *expanding* step: it is sometimes the precursor that
    # lets a later factoring discover a different common factor.
    exp_ids = findall(expands)
    if !isempty(exp_ids) && rand(rng) < 0.15
        node, repl = sites[exp_ids[rand(rng, 1:length(exp_ids))]]
        set_node!(node, repl)  # `repl` is built from copies -> in-place is safe
        return tree
    end

    # Otherwise: a short cascade of non-expanding rewrites. Rescanning after each
    # application keeps all node references valid and lets simplifications chain
    # (e.g. factor -> cancel -> fold constants) inside a single mutation.
    for pass in 1:8
        pass > 1 && scan!()
        idxs = findall(!, expands)
        isempty(idxs) && break
        node, repl = sites[pick(idxs)]
        set_node!(node, repl)
        # stop early most of the time so the operator stays a comparatively local move
        rand(rng) < 0.45 && break
    end

    return tree
end

marginal_information_bridge_selection_ge.name: marginal_information_bridge_selection_gen3_7
marginal_information_bridge_selection_ge.code:
"""
    marginal_information_bridge_selection_gen3_7(pop, running_search_statistics, options)

Selects parents by favoring sampled expressions that form useful “bridges” on the
loss-complexity frontier rather than merely having the lowest penalized cost. It
computes each candidate's marginal log-loss improvement over the best strictly
simpler candidate, so large explanatory jumps are rewarded while tiny improvements
from added complexity are suppressed. Complexity frequencies are locally smoothed
to discourage bloated families from evading parsimony by spreading across adjacent
sizes. A near-frontier scout term preserves young alternative structures, while
sibling dilution reduces repeated selection from a single parent lineage. The
heuristic assumes nonnegative losses and treats ratios of losses as more meaningful
than absolute loss differences across tasks.
"""
function marginal_information_bridge_selection_gen3_7(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = min(max(options.tournament_selection_n, 1), pop.n)
    sample = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, n; replace=false)

    if n == 1
        return sample[1]
    end

    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    log_losses = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    valid = Vector{Bool}(undef, n)

    # Log loss measures multiplicative progress and is less task-scale dependent.
    for i in 1:n
        complexities[i] = max(1, compute_complexity(sample[i], options))
        loss_i = Float64(sample[i].loss)
        valid[i] = isfinite(loss_i) && loss_i >= 0.0
        log_losses[i] = valid[i] ? log(max(loss_i, floatmin(Float64))) : Inf
    end

    # Fall back to ordinary cost selection if the whole tournament is numerically invalid.
    if !any(valid)
        costs = Vector{L}(undef, n)
        for i in 1:n
            costs[i] = sample[i].cost
        end
        return sample[argmin_fast(costs)]
    end

    # Identify the lower envelope in the two objectives (complexity, raw loss).
    on_frontier = copy(valid)
    for i in 1:n
        if !valid[i]
            continue
        end
        for j in 1:n
            if i != j && valid[j] &&
               complexities[j] <= complexities[i] &&
               log_losses[j] <= log_losses[i] &&
               (complexities[j] < complexities[i] ||
                log_losses[j] < log_losses[i])
                on_frontier[i] = false
                break
            end
        end
    end

    min_birth = minimum(member.birth for member in sample)
    max_birth = maximum(member.birth for member in sample)
    birth_span = max(Float64(max_birth) - Float64(min_birth), 1.0)

    p = clamp(Float64(options.tournament_selection_p), 0.0, 1.0)
    scaling = abs(Float64(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling))
    scaling = isfinite(scaling) ? scaling : 0.0
    maxsize_f = Float64(max(options.maxsize, 1))
    frequencies = running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies

    scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)

    for i in 1:n
        if !valid[i]
            scores[i] = 0.0
            continue
        end

        complexity_i = complexities[i]
        loss_i = log_losses[i]

        # Find the preceding point on the sampled lower envelope.
        predecessor_loss = Inf
        predecessor_complexity = 0
        best_upto_loss = loss_i
        for j in 1:n
            if !valid[j]
                continue
            end

            if complexities[j] <= complexity_i
                best_upto_loss = min(best_upto_loss, log_losses[j])
            end

            if complexities[j] < complexity_i &&
               (log_losses[j] < predecessor_loss ||
                (log_losses[j] == predecessor_loss &&
                 complexities[j] > predecessor_complexity))
                predecessor_loss = log_losses[j]
                predecessor_complexity = complexities[j]
            end
        end

        # Reward information gain per added node; cap it so one lucky member
        # cannot completely eliminate structural exploration.
        marginal_gain = 0.0
        if isfinite(predecessor_loss) && loss_i < predecessor_loss
            complexity_step = max(complexity_i - predecessor_complexity, 1)
            marginal_gain = (predecessor_loss - loss_i) / sqrt(Float64(complexity_step))
            marginal_gain = min(marginal_gain, 12.0)
        end

        # Keep imperfect alternative structures if they remain reasonably close
        # to the best loss attainable at no greater sampled complexity.
        frontier_deficit = max(loss_i - best_upto_loss, 0.0)
        near_frontier = exp(-min(frontier_deficit, 50.0) / 2.0)

        # Smooth occupancy across adjacent sizes so bloat cannot escape pressure
        # merely by moving from size c to c+1.
        local_frequency = 0.0
        local_weight = 0.0
        if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            for offset in -1:1
                size = complexity_i + offset
                if 1 <= size <= min(options.maxsize, length(frequencies))
                    weight = offset == 0 ? 2.0 : 1.0
                    frequency = Float64(frequencies[size])
                    if isfinite(frequency) && frequency > 0.0
                        local_frequency += weight * frequency
                    end
                    local_weight += weight
                end
            end
        end
        if local_weight > 0.0
            local_frequency /= local_weight
        end
        rarity = 1.0 / (1.0 + scaling * local_frequency)

        # Dilute sibling swarms while leaving independently created roots alone.
        sibling_count = 1
        parent_i = sample[i].parent
        if parent_i > 0
            sibling_count = 0
            for j in 1:n
                sibling_count += sample[j].parent == parent_i ? 1 : 0
            end
            sibling_count = max(sibling_count, 1)
        end
        lineage_factor = inv(sqrt(Float64(sibling_count)))

        # Slight recency pressure helps new structural motifs survive long enough
        # to be mutated, without overwhelming demonstrated fitness.
        relative_age = (Float64(sample[i].birth) - Float64(min_birth)) / birth_span
        recency_factor = 0.75 + 0.5 * relative_age

        # This mild prior only separates otherwise similar high-complexity scouts.
        simplicity_factor = inv(sqrt(1.0 + Float64(complexity_i) / maxsize_f))

        bridge_term = on_frontier[i] ? 0.15 + marginal_gain : 0.0
        scout_term = (0.12 + 0.28 * (1.0 - p)) * near_frontier
        exploitation = 0.75 + 1.25 * p

        scores[i] = (
            0.06 + exploitation * bridge_term + scout_term
        ) * rarity * lineage_factor * recency_factor * simplicity_factor
    end

    total_score = sum(scores)
    if !(isfinite(total_score) && total_score > 0.0)
        costs = Vector{L}(undef, n)
        for i in 1:n
            costs[i] = sample[i].cost
        end
        return sample[argmin_fast(costs)]
    end

    weights = StatsBase.Weights(scores, total_score)
    return sample[StatsBase.sample(weights)]
end

residual_matching_pursuit_boost_gen3_8.name: residual_matching_pursuit_boost_gen3_8
residual_matching_pursuit_boost_gen3_8.code:
"""
    residual_matching_pursuit_boost_gen3_8(tree::N, dataset, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}

A data-aware mutation operator inspired by 1D Matching Pursuit and Gradient Boosting.
It evaluates the current expression tree on the dataset to compute residuals, calculates the
optimal 1D least-squares orthogonal projection of the residuals onto each input feature (and
a constant bias term), and injects the most predictive linear term into the expression.

# Key Steps:
1. **Residual Evaluation**: Evaluates `tree` on `dataset.X` and computes residuals `r = y - y_pred`.
   If evaluation fails, target is missing, or residual variance is negligible, returns `tree` unchanged.
2. **Matching Pursuit Scoring**: Computes the optimal scale `β_j = <X_j, r> / ||X_j||^2` and the
   corresponding squared error reduction `Score_j = <X_j, r>^2 / ||X_j||^2` for each feature `j`,
   as well as for a constant offset `j = 0` (`β_0 = mean(r)`).
3. **Stochastic Selection**: Selects a candidate term, with 70% probability picking the top-scoring
   feature and 30% sampling among competitive candidates to preserve population diversity.
4. **Term Construction**: Creates the optimal linear term `(β * x_j)` or constant `β`.
5. **Structural Integration**:
   - Updates existing constants when a pure bias term is selected.
   - For large trees (bloat control), replaces low-impact leaves or constants with the new term.
   - Otherwise, prepends the boosted term to the tree root via addition or subtraction.
"""
function residual_matching_pursuit_boost_gen3_8(
    tree::N,
    dataset,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # 1. Safety and prerequisite checks
    dataset.y === nothing && return tree
    n = dataset.n
    n < 2 && return tree
    nfeatures < 1 && return tree

    # Look up available arithmetic binary operators
    add_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (+), options.operators.binops)
    sub_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (-), options.operators.binops)
    mul_idx = findfirst(op -> op == (*), options.operators.binops)

    # We need at least addition or subtraction to perform boosting
    add_idx === nothing && sub_idx === nothing && return tree

    # 2. Evaluate current tree predictions on training data
    y_pred, ok = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options.operators)
    !ok && return tree

    # Compute prediction residuals
    all(isfinite, y_pred) || return tree
    residual = dataset.y .- y_pred
    all(isfinite, residual) || return tree

    # Compute baseline residual statistics
    tot_ss = 0.0
    sum_r = 0.0
    for i in 1:n
        ri = Float64(residual[i])
        sum_r += ri
        tot_ss += ri * ri
    end

    # If residuals are already negligible, no mutation needed
    tot_ss <= 1e-12 * n && return tree

    # 3. Compute 1D Orthogonal Projections (Matching Pursuit)
    # Index 1 corresponds to candidate 0 (constant bias)
    # Indices 2:(nfeatures + 1) correspond to features 1:nfeatures
    scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, nfeatures + 1)
    betas = Vector{Float64}(undef, nfeatures + 1)

    # Bias candidate (constant offset)
    scores[1] = (sum_r * sum_r) / n
    betas[1] = sum_r / n

    # Feature candidates
    for j in 1:nfeatures
        acc_xr = 0.0
        acc_xx = 0.0
        for i in 1:n
            xi = Float64(dataset.X[j, i])
            ri = Float64(residual[i])
            acc_xr += xi * ri
            acc_xx += xi * xi
        end

        if acc_xx > 1e-12 && isfinite(acc_xr) && isfinite(acc_xx)
            scores[j + 1] = (acc_xr * acc_xr) / acc_xx
            betas[j + 1] = acc_xr / acc_xx
        else
            scores[j + 1] = 0.0
            betas[j + 1] = 0.0
        end
    end

    max_score = maximum(scores)
    # If no candidate explains meaningful residual variance, return unchanged
    if max_score <= 1e-9 * tot_ss || !isfinite(max_score)
        return tree
    end

    # 4. Stochastic Candidate Selection
    chosen_idx = if rand(rng) < 0.70
        argmax(scores)
    else
        threshold = 0.25 * max_score
        valid_indices = findall(s -> s >= threshold, scores)
        isempty(valid_indices) ? argmax(scores) : rand(rng, valid_indices)
    end

    chosen_beta = betas[chosen_idx]
    cand_id = chosen_idx - 1  # 0 for constant bias, 1:nfeatures for features
    !isfinite(chosen_beta) && return tree

    # 5. Determine combining operator and construct the boosting subtree
    combine_op = add_idx !== nothing ? add_idx : sub_idx
    eff_beta = (add_idx === nothing && sub_idx !== nothing) ? -chosen_beta : chosen_beta

    if cand_id == 0
        # Constant bias term
        term_node = constructorof(N)(T; val=T(eff_beta))
    else
        # Feature term: scale * x_j (or just x_j / -x_j if multiplication is unavailable)
        feat_node = constructorof(N)(T; feature=cand_id)
        if mul_idx !== nothing && abs(eff_beta - 1.0) > 1e-4
            const_node = constructorof(N)(T; val=T(eff_beta))
            term_node = constructorof(N)(; op=mul_idx, children=(const_node, feat_node))
        elseif eff_beta < 0.0 && sub_idx !== nothing && combine_op == add_idx
            # Feature with negative weight: change combine operator to subtraction
            combine_op = sub_idx
            term_node = feat_node
        else
            term_node = feat_node
        end
    end

    # 6. Integrate the term into the tree
    # Case A: Tree is a single constant leaf
    if tree.degree == 0 && tree.constant
        if cand_id == 0
            tree.val += T(eff_beta)
            return tree
        elseif abs(tree.val) < eps(T)
            return term_node
        else
            return constructorof(N)(; op=combine_op, children=(copy(tree), term_node))
        end
    end

    # Case B: Tree root is already an addition and candidate is a bias term
    if cand_id == 0 && combine_op == add_idx && (tree.degree == 2 && tree.op == add_idx)
        for c in 1:2
            child = get_child(tree, c)
            if child.degree == 0 && child.constant
                child.val += T(eff_beta)
                return tree
            end
        end
    end

    # Case C: Bloat management for large trees (replace unneeded leaves/constants)
    if count_nodes(tree) >= 10
        if has_constants(tree) && rand(rng) < 0.40
            const_leaf = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=t -> t.degree == 0 && t.constant))
            set_node!(const_leaf, term_node)
            return tree
        elseif rand(rng) < 0.30
            leaf = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=t -> t.degree == 0))
            set_node!(leaf, term_node)
            return tree
        end
    end

    # Case D: Default prepending at root
    return constructorof(N)(; op=combine_op, children=(copy(tree), term_node))
end

symmetric_motif_duplication_gen4_9.name: symmetric_motif_duplication_gen4_9
symmetric_motif_duplication_gen4_9.code:
"""
    symmetric_motif_duplication_gen4_9(tree::N, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}

A structural mutation operator that identifies, replicates, and recombines modular subexpressions
(motifs) with optional feature-space permutations or direct coupling.

# Motivation & Core Idea
Physical and mathematical expressions commonly exhibit symmetries, repeated structural motifs
(e.g., Euclidean distances `(x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2`, coupled harmonic terms `sin(x1) + sin(x2)`,
or rational envelopes `u / (1 + u^2)`), and multilinear interactions. Standard point mutations
require exponentially many lucky mutations to replicate an evolved subexpression across other
variables. This operator extracts an existing subtree, systematically permutes its feature indices
(or keeps them identical for self-interaction), and couples or grafts the transformed motif back
into the expression tree.

# Steps & Heuristics
1. Sample a donor subtree from the existing expression tree.
2. Deep-copy the donor into an independent motif.
3. If features are present and `nfeatures > 1`, apply one of three feature-space transformations:
   - Cyclic feature permutation (e.g., `x_i -> x_{i+k}`), preserving relational sub-structures.
   - Targeted single-feature substitution (`x_a -> x_b`), useful for asymmetric couplings.
   - Identity mapping (no change), enabling polynomial powers (e.g. `u * u`) and rational forms.
4. Integrate the transformed motif into the tree via either:
   - Binary operator coupling: wraps a target node and the motif under a random binary operator.
   - Homologous grafting: replaces a target node in the tree with the evolved motif.
"""
function symmetric_motif_duplication_gen4_9(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # Local helper: recursively collect all active feature indices in a subtree
    function _collect_features!(node, feats::Vector{Int})
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant
                push!(feats, node.feature)
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _collect_features!(get_child(node, i), feats)
            end
        end
        return feats
    end

    # Local helper: apply a cyclic shift to all feature leaves in a subtree
    function _shift_features!(node, shift::Int, num_features::Int)
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant
                node.feature = mod1(node.feature + shift, num_features)
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _shift_features!(get_child(node, i), shift, num_features)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    # Local helper: substitute occurrences of a specific feature index with another
    function _remap_feature!(node, from_f::Int, to_f::Int)
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant && node.feature == from_f
                node.feature = to_f
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _remap_feature!(get_child(node, i), from_f, to_f)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    # Fallback: if no binary operators are configured, wrap with a unary operator if possible
    if options.nops[2] == 0
        if options.nops[1] > 0
            node = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
            new_node = constructorof(N)(;
                op=rand(rng, 1:options.nops[1]),
                children=(copy(node),),
            )
            set_node!(node, new_node)
        end
        return tree
    end

    # Step 1: Select a donor subtree motif to duplicate
    donor = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
    donor_clone = copy(donor)

    # Step 2: Extract active features and apply feature-space symmetry transformation
    feats = _collect_features!(donor_clone, Int[])
    if !isempty(feats) && nfeatures > 1
        strategy_roll = rand(rng)
        if strategy_roll < 0.45
            # Cyclic permutation: shifts all variable indices by a fixed offset
            shift = rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1))
            _shift_features!(donor_clone, shift, nfeatures)
        elseif strategy_roll < 0.70
            # Targeted substitution: pick one variable present in the motif and remap it
            f_old = rand(rng, feats)
            valid_targets = [f for f in 1:nfeatures if f != f_old]
            if !isempty(valid_targets)
                f_new = rand(rng, valid_targets)
                _remap_feature!(donor_clone, f_old, f_new)
            end
        else
            # Identity: keep exact features to foster powers (e.g. u*u) or rational self-coupling
        end
    end

    # Step 3: Integrate the transformed motif back into the expression
    total_nodes = count_nodes(tree)
    # Use grafting if the tree has sufficient depth/size, otherwise couple via binary operator
    if total_nodes > 3 && rand(rng) < 0.35
        # Homologous Grafting: replace a randomly chosen node with the evolved motif
        target = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
        set_node!(target, donor_clone)
    else
        # Binary Coupling: pair target node with the motif under a binary operator
        target = rand(rng, Bool) ? donor : rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
        target_copy = copy(target)
        bin_op = rand(rng, 1:options.nops[2])

        # Randomize operand ordering for non-commutative operations (subtraction, division)
        children_tuple = rand(rng, Bool) ? (target_copy, donor_clone) : (donor_clone, target_copy)
        new_node = constructorof(N)(;
            op=bin_op,
            children=children_tuple,
        )
        set_node!(target, new_node)
    end

    return tree
end

fit_rational_pole_mutation_gen4_3.name: fit_rational_pole_mutation_gen4_3
fit_rational_pole_mutation_gen4_3.code:
"""
    fit_rational_pole_mutation_gen4_3(tree, dataset, options, nfeatures, rng)

A data-aware mutation that converts a *polynomial-looking* expression into a
**rational (pole-bearing) expression** by fitting the denominator with least squares.

Motivation: plain genetic search very often approximates a rational law such as
`y = N / (1 - u/3)` by its Taylor series (`N*(1 + u/3 + u^2/9 + ...)`), which
produces long, ever-growing polynomial trees that never cross over to the compact
rational form (this is visible on tasks such as `feynman_II_11_27`). This mutation
provides that jump in one step. Given the current tree `p(x)` (interpreted as a
candidate *numerator*) it searches for a "pole driver" subexpression `q(x)` and
proposes

    p(x)  ->  a * p(x) / (1 + b * q(x)),

where the pair `(a, b)` is obtained in closed form: the condition
`y * (1 + b*q) ≈ a * p` is **linear** in `(a, b)`, so a 2x2 weighted normal-equation
solve yields the optimal coefficients without any nonlinear optimization.

Steps: (1) evaluate the tree on `dataset.X`; (2) collect candidate `q`'s — a random
handful of subtrees of the tree, plus a random feature leaf and a random
product-of-two-features (cheap way to discover denominators like `x0*x1` that are
not yet in the tree); (3) for each candidate solve the 2x2 least-squares system for
`(a, b)`; (4) reject candidates whose fitted denominator `1 + b*q` changes sign or
comes close to zero anywhere on the training data (that would place a pole inside
the data range), or whose `b` is numerically negligible; (5) score surviving
candidates by their *actual* weighted MSE and accept the best one only if it
improves the current MSE by at least 10% (the wrap costs ~4-6 nodes, so we demand a
real gain) and respects `options.maxsize`. Otherwise the tree is returned unchanged.

Assumptions/heuristics: requires `+`, `*`, `/` among the binary operators and a
single-output dataset; constants `a`, `b` are inserted as ordinary constant leaves
so downstream constant optimization can refine them further.
"""
function fit_rational_pole_mutation_gen4_3(
    tree::N,
    dataset,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    y = dataset.y
    y === nothing && return tree            # multi-output: nothing to fit against
    X = dataset.X
    n = dataset.n
    n < 8 && return tree                    # too few points to trust a 2-parameter fit

    # We need +, * and / to be able to express a*p/(1 + b*q)
    binops = options.operators.binops
    i_add = findfirst(op -> op === (+), binops)
    i_mul = findfirst(op -> op === (*), binops)
    i_div = findfirst(op -> op === (/), binops)
    (i_add === nothing || i_mul === nothing || i_div === nothing) && return tree

    # ---- current predictions (the candidate "numerator") -------------------
    p, ok = eval_tree_array(tree, X, options.operators)
    ok || return tree
    all(isfinite, p) || return tree

    w = dataset.weights
    _wmean(v) = w === nothing ? mean(v) : sum(w .* v) / sum(w)

    base_mse = Float64(_wmean(abs2.(y .- p)))
    (!isfinite(base_mse) || base_mse <= 0) && return tree   # nothing to gain

    # ---- assemble candidate pole-drivers q --------------------------------
    subtrees = N[]
    any(tree) do t
        # keep operator nodes and variable leaves; constants make useless denominators
        if t.degree > 0 || !t.constant
            push!(subtrees, t)
        end
        return false                       # never short-circuit: visit all nodes
    end

    cands = N[]
    if !isempty(subtrees)
        # sample a small random handful (duplicates are harmless, just redundant work)
        for _ in 1:min(length(subtrees), 6)
            push!(cands, subtrees[rand(rng, 1:length(subtrees))])
        end
    end
    # a bare feature, and a random pairwise product: cheap "new" denominators
    push!(cands, constructorof(N)(T; feature=rand(rng, 1:nfeatures)))
    if nfeatures >= 2
        f1 = rand(rng, 1:nfeatures)
        f2 = rand(rng, 1:nfeatures)
        push!(
            cands,
            constructorof(N)(;
                op=i_mul,
                children=(
                    constructorof(N)(T; feature=f1), constructorof(N)(T; feature=f2)
                ),
            ),
        )
    end
    isempty(cands) && return tree

    # ---- evaluate every candidate, keep the best rational wrap ------------
    best_mse = base_mse
    best_q = nothing
    best_a = 1.0
    best_b = 0.0

    for q in cands
        qv, qok = eval_tree_array(q, X, options.operators)
        qok || continue
        all(isfinite, qv) || continue
        sq = Float64(std(qv))
        (!isfinite(sq) || sq <= 1e-12) && continue        # constant q ⇒ no new structure

        # Weighted normal equations for  min_{a,b} || y + b*(y*q) - a*p ||^2
        S11 = 0.0; S12 = 0.0; S22 = 0.0; r1 = 0.0; r2 = 0.0
        @inbounds for k in 1:n
            wk = w === nothing ? 1.0 : Float64(w[k])
            yk = Float64(y[k])
            pk = Float64(p[k])
            uk = yk * Float64(qv[k])       # column for b
            S11 += wk * uk * uk
            S12 += wk * uk * pk
            S22 += wk * pk * pk
            r1 += wk * uk * yk
            r2 += wk * pk * yk
        end
        D = S11 * S22 - S12 * S12
        (!isfinite(D) || abs(D) <= 1e-12 * max(1.0, S11 * S22)) && continue

        b = (S12 * r2 - r1 * S22) / D
        a = (S11 * r2 - r1 * S12) / D
        (!isfinite(a) || !isfinite(b)) && continue
        abs(b) * sq < 1e-6 && continue      # denominator would be ~1: no real change
        abs(a) < 1e-12 && continue

        # Pole safety: 1 + b*q must stay away from zero and keep a fixed sign on data
        dmin = Inf
        dmax = -Inf
        @inbounds for k in 1:n
            dk = 1.0 + b * Float64(qv[k])
            dmin = min(dmin, dk)
            dmax = max(dmax, dk)
        end
        (dmin <= 0.1 && dmax >= -0.1) && continue   # straddles / hugs zero ⇒ reject

        # Score the *actual* candidate prediction (not the linearized objective)
        acc = 0.0
        wsum = 0.0
        bad = false
        @inbounds for k in 1:n
            dk = 1.0 + b * Float64(qv[k])
            predk = a * Float64(p[k]) / dk
            if !isfinite(predk)
                bad = true
                break
            end
            wk = w === nothing ? 1.0 : Float64(w[k])
            resid = Float64(y[k]) - predk
            acc += wk * resid * resid
            wsum += wk
        end
        (bad || wsum <= 0) && continue
        mse = acc / wsum
        if isfinite(mse) && mse < best_mse
            best_mse = mse
            best_q = q
            best_a = a
            best_b = b
