   improvements of roughly one percent, plus the current best-loss member.

Compared with the parent, this removes coarse redundancy, neighboring-complexity
bands, lineage counts, separate best-cost elitism, and multiple frontier-strength
heuristics. Exact niches retain structural diversity, while the sparse frontier
preserves meaningful stepping stones without protecting every tiny improvement
and encouraging expression bloat. Protections decay with age so elites can
eventually turn over. Non-finite members receive dominant deletion pressure.
"""
function sparse_pareto_niche_survival_gen15_6(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = pop.n
    n <= 1 && return 1

    excluded = falses(n)
    for idx in exclude_indices
        1 <= idx <= n && (excluded[idx] = true)
    end
    all(excluded) && return 1

    # Gather the statistics used by all subsequent signals.
    comp = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    lossf = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    costf = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    births = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    broken = falses(n)

    for i in 1:n
        member = pop.members[i]
        raw_loss = Float64(member.loss)
        raw_cost = Float64(member.cost)

        comp[i] = compute_complexity(member, options)
        broken[i] = !isfinite(raw_loss) || !isfinite(raw_cost)
        lossf[i] = isfinite(raw_loss) ? raw_loss : Inf
        costf[i] = isfinite(raw_cost) ? raw_cost : Inf
        births[i] = Float64(member.birth)
    end

    # Birth counters are monotonic, so range normalization is sufficient for age.
    oldest_birth = minimum(births)
    newest_birth = maximum(births)
    birth_span = newest_birth - oldest_birth
    age_score = birth_span > 0.0 ?
        (newest_birth .- births) ./ birth_span :
        fill(0.5, n)

    # Cost ranks avoid dependence on the numerical scale of the objective.
    cost_rank = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    cost_order = sortperm(costf)
    rank_denom = Float64(max(1, n - 1))
    for (rank, idx) in enumerate(cost_order)
        cost_rank[idx] = (rank - 1) / rank_denom
    end

    # Use one redundancy resolution and retain the best, simplest tie-breaker:
    # lowest true loss, then cost, then newest member.
    signatures = Vector{Tuple{Int,Float64}}(undef, n)
    signature_counts = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()
    representative = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()

    for i in 1:n
        rounded_loss = isfinite(lossf[i]) ?
            round(lossf[i]; sigdigits=7) : Inf
        signature = (comp[i], rounded_loss)
        signatures[i] = signature
        signature_counts[signature] = get(signature_counts, signature, 0) + 1

        old = get(representative, signature, 0)
        if old == 0 ||
           lossf[i] < lossf[old] ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[old] && costf[i] < costf[old]) ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[old] && costf[i] == costf[old] &&
            births[i] > births[old])
            representative[signature] = i
        end
    end

    # Exact-complexity occupancy supplies a lightweight diversity signal.
    complexity_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for c in comp
        complexity_counts[c] = get(complexity_counts, c, 0) + 1
    end
    max_complexity_count = maximum(values(complexity_counts))

    # Build a sparse Pareto frontier. Tiny improvements accumulate until they
    # exceed the threshold, rather than each receiving individual protection.
    pareto_landmark = falses(n)
    pareto_order = sortperm(1:n; by=i -> (comp[i], lossf[i], costf[i]))
    best_seen_loss = Inf
    last_protected_loss = Inf

    for idx in pareto_order
        current_loss = lossf[idx]
        if isfinite(current_loss) && current_loss < best_seen_loss
            if isinf(last_protected_loss)
                pareto_landmark[idx] = true
                last_protected_loss = current_loss
            else
                improvement = last_protected_loss - current_loss
                threshold = 0.01 * max(abs(last_protected_loss), 1.0e-12)
                if improvement > threshold
                    pareto_landmark[idx] = true
                    last_protected_loss = current_loss
                end
            end
            best_seen_loss = current_loss
        end
    end

    # Keep one current loss champion; ties favor simpler and newer expressions.
    best_loss_idx = 0
    for i in 1:n
        broken[i] && continue
        if best_loss_idx == 0 ||
           lossf[i] < lossf[best_loss_idx] ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[best_loss_idx] &&
            comp[i] < comp[best_loss_idx]) ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[best_loss_idx] &&
            comp[i] == comp[best_loss_idx] &&
            births[i] > births[best_loss_idx])
            best_loss_idx = i
        end
    end

    # The largest score identifies the member to replace.
    best_choice = 0
    best_score = -Inf

    for i in 1:n
        excluded[i] && continue

        is_duplicate = representative[signatures[i]] != i
        crowding = max_complexity_count > 1 ?
            (complexity_counts[comp[i]] - 1) /
            Float64(max_complexity_count - 1) : 0.0

        # Crowding primarily removes weak members from an occupied complexity.
        quality_gate = 0.30 + 0.70 * cost_rank[i]

        score =
            1.05 * age_score[i] +
            0.75 * cost_rank[i] +
            1.20 * (is_duplicate ? 1.0 : 0.0) +
            0.50 * quality_gate * crowding

        # Invalid members dominate all ordinary candidates.
        broken[i] && (score += 6.0)

        # Age-decayed protection avoids permanently freezing stale elites.
        if pareto_landmark[i]
            score -= 1.05 * (1.0 - 0.55 * age_score[i])
        end
        if i == best_loss_idx
            score -= 0.70 * (1.0 - 0.60 * age_score[i])
        end

        # Break near-ties without materially changing clear score differences.
        score += 0.005 * rand()

        if score > best_score
            best_score = score
            best_choice = i
        end
    end

    return best_choice == 0 ? 1 : best_choice
end

context_aware_crowding_niche_tournament_.name: context_aware_crowding_niche_tournament_gen15_8
context_aware_crowding_niche_tournament_.code:
"""
    context_aware_crowding_niche_tournament_gen15_8(pop, running_search_statistics, options)

Tournament selection that suppresses clone-heavy lineages while preserving
underrepresented complexity niches without substantially increasing ordinary
tournament selection pressure.

Steps:
 1. Sample the usual `tournament_selection_n` eligible candidates plus a small
    context-only set. Context members provide better evidence of population
    crowding but cannot win directly.
 2. Compute adaptive-parsimony-adjusted costs in a stable signed-log
    representation. This preserves the ordering of multiplicatively adjusted
    costs while avoiding overflow from the frequency exponent.
 3. Compare each member with better context members. Repeated reference IDs,
    structurally equal trees, equal-complexity/equal-loss solutions, siblings,
    and direct parent-child relations contribute progressively weaker crowding
    evidence. The accumulated penalty is capped so a dense but useful lineage is
    discouraged rather than eliminated.
 4. Apply a mild rank-independent youth bonus based on birth time within the
    sampled context.
 5. Occasionally choose the rarest valid complexity among the best half of the
    eligible candidates. This quality gate prevents rare-niche exploration from
    selecting arbitrarily poor or out-of-range expressions.
 6. Otherwise apply the configured geometric tournament ladder to only the usual
    number of eligible candidates.

Compared with the parent operator, the enlarged sample is used only as crowding
context, so it does not silently strengthen every tournament. Structural equality
and reference identity improve clone detection, lineage evidence is graded and
capped, frequency arithmetic is overflow-safe, and rare-niche selection is
quality-gated and excludes invalid complexity sizes. Equal complexity plus nearly
equal loss remains a deliberately weak proxy for semantic redundancy.
"""
function context_aware_crowding_niche_tournament_gen15_8(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Mild tunables: diversity pressure should redirect search, not erase fitness.
    context_scale = 1.5
    clone_penalty = 1.30
    crowding_cap = 4.0
    loss_rtol = 1e-5
    loss_atol = 1e-12
    youth_discount = 0.04
    p_rare_niche = 0.10
    niche_quality_fraction = 0.50

    n_candidates = min(pop.n, max(1, options.tournament_selection_n))
    context_size = min(
        pop.n,
        max(n_candidates, ceil(Int, context_scale * n_candidates)),
    )

    # Sampling is unordered, so the first n_candidates remain an unbiased
    # ordinary tournament; the remainder are crowding witnesses only.
    pool = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, context_size; replace=false)
    n = length(pool)

    # softplus(x) = log(1 + exp(x)), evaluated without overflow.
    softplus = function (x::Float64)
        return x > 0.0 ? x + log1p(exp(-x)) : log1p(exp(x))
    end

    # This encoding is a strictly increasing transform of a signed adjusted cost:
    # sign(z) * log(1 + abs(z)). It permits multiplicative adjustments in log space.
    encode_cost = function (cost_sign::Int8, log_magnitude::Float64)
        if cost_sign > 0
            return softplus(log_magnitude)
        elseif cost_sign < 0
            return -softplus(log_magnitude)
        else
            return 0.0
        end
    end

    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    cost_signs = Vector{Int8}(undef, n)
    base_log_magnitudes = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    base_scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)

    raw_scaling = Float64(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling)
    adaptive_parsimony_scaling = isfinite(raw_scaling) ? raw_scaling : 0.0
    normalized_frequencies = running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies

    # Compute frequency-adjusted costs without explicitly evaluating exp(scaling*f).
    for i in 1:n
        member = pool[i]
        complexity = compute_complexity(member, options)
        complexities[i] = complexity

        frequency = 0.0
        if options.use_frequency_in_tournament &&
           0 < complexity <= options.maxsize &&
           complexity <= length(normalized_frequencies)
            raw_frequency = Float64(normalized_frequencies[complexity])
            frequency = isfinite(raw_frequency) ? max(raw_frequency, 0.0) : 0.0
        end
        frequency_term = adaptive_parsimony_scaling * frequency

        cost = Float64(member.cost)
        if !isfinite(cost)
            # Invalid numerical results should never gain a selection advantage.
            cost_signs[i] = Int8(1)
            base_log_magnitudes[i] = Inf
            base_scores[i] = Inf
        elseif cost > 0.0
            cost_signs[i] = Int8(1)
            base_log_magnitudes[i] = log(cost) + frequency_term
            base_scores[i] = encode_cost(cost_signs[i], base_log_magnitudes[i])
        elseif cost < 0.0
            # Negative costs are unusual, but this exactly preserves the default
            # multiplicative ordering and supports sign-safe later penalties.
            cost_signs[i] = Int8(-1)
            base_log_magnitudes[i] = log(-cost) + frequency_term
            base_scores[i] = encode_cost(cost_signs[i], base_log_magnitudes[i])
        else
            cost_signs[i] = Int8(0)
            base_log_magnitudes[i] = -Inf
            base_scores[i] = 0.0
        end
    end

    # Better members act as witnesses against redundant worse members.
    order = sortperm(base_scores)
    redundancy = zeros(Float64, n)
    for a in 2:n
        i = order[a]
        li = Float64(pool[i].loss)
        crowding = 0.0

        for b in 1:(a - 1)
            j = order[b]
            isfinite(base_scores[j]) || continue

            # Strongest evidence first; each pair contributes only once.
            same_reference =
                pool[i].ref != 0 && pool[i].ref == pool[j].ref
            same_tree = isequal(pool[i].tree, pool[j].tree)

            lj = Float64(pool[j].loss)
            same_loss = false
            if isfinite(li) && isfinite(lj)
                tolerance =
                    loss_atol + loss_rtol * max(abs(li), abs(lj))
                same_loss = abs(li - lj) <= tolerance
            end
            same_objective_niche =
                complexities[i] == complexities[j] && same_loss

            same_parent =
                pool[i].parent != 0 &&
                pool[i].parent == pool[j].parent

            directly_related =
                (pool[i].parent != 0 && pool[i].parent == pool[j].ref) ||
                (pool[j].parent != 0 && pool[j].parent == pool[i].ref)

            if same_reference
                crowding += 1.25
            elseif same_tree
                crowding += 1.0
            elseif same_objective_niche
                # Equal size and loss can be coincidental, so this is weaker than
                # actual structural equality.
                crowding += 0.65
            elseif same_parent
                crowding += 0.30
            elseif directly_related
                crowding += 0.15
            end
        end

        # Avoid making every representative of a dominant but promising lineage
        # effectively unselectable when its best witness is context-only.
        redundancy[i] = min(crowding, crowding_cap)
    end

    # Estimate recency within the context. The bonus is intentionally too small
    # to rescue a substantially worse expression by itself.
    birth_min = pool[1].birth
    birth_max = pool[1].birth
    for i in 2:n
        birth = pool[i].birth
        birth_min = min(birth_min, birth)
        birth_max = max(birth_max, birth)
    end
    birth_span = max(birth_max - birth_min, 1)

    penalized_scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    log_clone_penalty = log(clone_penalty)
    for i in 1:n
        recency =
            Float64(pool[i].birth - birth_min) / Float64(birth_span)

        # Positive log_factor means worse. log1p keeps the small youth term stable.
        log_factor =
            redundancy[i] * log_clone_penalty +
            log1p(-youth_discount * recency)

        sign = cost_signs[i]
        adjusted_log_magnitude = if sign > 0
            base_log_magnitudes[i] + log_factor
        elseif sign < 0
            # Dividing a negative cost by factor makes it worse, matching the
            # parent's sign-safe inflation rule.
            base_log_magnitudes[i] - log_factor
        else
            base_log_magnitudes[i]
        end
        penalized_scores[i] = encode_cost(sign, adjusted_log_magnitude)
    end

    # Only the ordinary tournament-sized prefix is eligible to win.
    candidate_scores = penalized_scores[1:n_candidates]
    candidate_order = sortperm(candidate_scores)

    # Explicit niche recovery is restricted to candidates already in the better
    # half of this tournament, preventing unconstrained selection of poor rarities.
    if rand() < p_rare_niche
        quality_count = max(
            1,
            ceil(Int, niche_quality_fraction * n_candidates),
        )
        best_niche_idx = 0
        best_niche_frequency = Inf
        best_niche_score = Inf

        for rank in 1:quality_count
            i = candidate_order[rank]
            complexity = complexities[i]

            # Out-of-range expressions are not legitimate "rare niches".
            if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize &&
               complexity <= length(normalized_frequencies)
                raw_frequency = Float64(normalized_frequencies[complexity])
                frequency =
                    isfinite(raw_frequency) ? max(raw_frequency, 0.0) : Inf

                if frequency < best_niche_frequency ||
                   (frequency == best_niche_frequency &&
                    candidate_scores[i] < best_niche_score)
                    best_niche_idx = i
                    best_niche_frequency = frequency
                    best_niche_score = candidate_scores[i]
                end
            end
        end

        best_niche_idx != 0 && return pool[best_niche_idx]
    end

    # Geometric rank selection over exactly n_candidates preserves the configured
    # tournament pressure despite the enlarged crowding context.
    p = Float64(options.tournament_selection_p)
    chosen_idx = if !isfinite(p) || p >= 1.0
        candidate_order[1]
    elseif p <= 0.0
        # A nonpositive geometric parameter has no valid weights; uniform rank
        # selection is the least-assumptive fallback.
        candidate_order[rand(1:n_candidates)]
    else
        probabilities = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_candidates)
        remaining = 1.0
        for rank in 1:n_candidates
            probabilities[rank] = p * remaining
            remaining *= 1.0 - p
        end
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(probabilities, sum(probabilities))
        winner_rank = StatsBase.sample(weights)
        candidate_order[winner_rank]
    end

    return pool[chosen_idx]
end

affine_shape_bounded_relative_tail_loss_.name: affine_shape_bounded_relative_tail_loss_gen15_0
affine_shape_bounded_relative_tail_loss_.code:
"""
    affine_shape_bounded_relative_tail_loss_gen15_0(tree, dataset, options)

Two-pass shape-first loss combining efficient affine calibration with robust
relative-error uniformity. The primary score is the normalized RMSE remaining
after the best least-squares affine recalibration `a * prediction + b`, evaluated
from fitted residuals directly to retain precision near exact structural matches.

The second pass also measures affine-calibrated pointwise relative error using
the bounded ratio

    |fitted - y| / (|fitted - y| + |y| + target_rms / 8).

Bounding each sample before aggregation prevents overflow and limits the influence
of extreme or near-zero targets. Its L2 norm rewards uniformly accurate fits,
while an L4 soft-tail norm detects localized Padé-like approximation failures
without the noise sensitivity of a hard maximum. A small bounded raw-NMSE term
selects the correctly scaled and shifted representative among affine-equivalent
expressions.

For effectively constant targets, where affine shape is undefined, the same
second-pass budget is used for a scale-normalized bounded raw RMSE instead.
Welford moments, direct residual evaluation, and simple uncompensated sums keep
the cost to one tree evaluation and two linear passes. No complexity penalty is
included.
"""
function affine_shape_bounded_relative_tail_loss_gen15_0(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = dataset.n
    if n <= 0 || length(prediction) != n || length(dataset.y) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    zero_l = zero(L)
    one_l = one(L)
    n_l = L(n)

    # First pass: stable moments for the affine least-squares fit.
    mean_p = zero_l
    mean_y = zero_l
    m2_p = zero_l
    m2_y = zero_l
    cov_py = zero_l
    max_abs_p = zero_l
    max_abs_y = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        max_abs_p = max(max_abs_p, abs(p))
        max_abs_y = max(max_abs_y, abs(y))

        k = L(i)
        delta_p = p - mean_p
        delta_y = y - mean_y

        mean_p += delta_p / k
        mean_y += delta_y / k

        # The covariance update uses the newly updated target mean.
        cov_py += delta_p * (y - mean_y)
        m2_p += delta_p * (p - mean_p)
        m2_y += delta_y * (y - mean_y)
    end

    if !(isfinite(mean_p) && isfinite(mean_y) &&
         isfinite(m2_p) && isfinite(m2_y) && isfinite(cov_py) &&
         isfinite(max_abs_p) && isfinite(max_abs_y))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Roundoff can make Welford sums microscopically negative.
    m2_p = max(m2_p, zero_l)
    m2_y = max(m2_y, zero_l)

    relative_tolerance = sqrt(eps(L))
    target_rms = sqrt(m2_y / n_l)
    prediction_rms = sqrt(m2_p / n_l)

    target_is_variable =
        target_rms > relative_tolerance * max_abs_y
    prediction_is_variable =
        prediction_rms > relative_tolerance * max_abs_p

    if !target_is_variable
        # Shape carries no information for a constant target, so promote the
        # scale-normalized raw error instead of returning only a tiny tie-breaker.
        target_scale = max(one_l, max_abs_y)
        raw_sum = zero_l

        @inbounds for i in 1:n
            residual = L(prediction[i]) - L(dataset.y[i])
            normalized = residual / target_scale
            raw_sum += normalized * normalized
        end

        bounded_raw = if isfinite(raw_sum) && raw_sum >= zero_l
            raw_mse = raw_sum / n_l
            raw_mse <= one_l ?
                raw_mse / (one_l + raw_mse) :
                one_l / (one_l + one_l / raw_mse)
        else
            one_l
        end

        loss_value = sqrt(max(bounded_raw, zero_l))
        return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(loss_value) : L(Inf)
    end

    target_norm = sqrt(m2_y)
    if !(isfinite(target_norm) && target_norm > zero_l)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # A nearly constant prediction is treated as a constant rather than allowing
    # an unstable, extremely large affine slope.
    slope = zero_l
    intercept = mean_y
    if prediction_is_variable
        slope = cov_py / m2_p
        intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_p
        if !(isfinite(slope) && isfinite(intercept))
            return L(Inf)
        end
    end

    # Relative damping remains small enough to expose low-|y| regions while
    # preventing target zero-crossings from dominating the loss.
    relative_floor = target_rms / L(8)

    affine_sum = zero_l
    relative_square_sum = zero_l
    relative_fourth_sum = zero_l
    raw_sum = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        # Raw error is only a bounded calibration tie-breaker; overflow is
        # allowed to propagate to raw_sum and is saturated after the loop.
        raw_normalized = (p - y) / target_norm
        raw_sum += raw_normalized * raw_normalized

        fitted = prediction_is_variable ? muladd(slope, p, intercept) : mean_y
        affine_residual = fitted - y
        affine_normalized = affine_residual / target_norm
        affine_term = affine_normalized * affine_normalized

        if !(isfinite(fitted) && isfinite(affine_residual) &&
             isfinite(affine_normalized) && isfinite(affine_term))
            return L(Inf)
        end
        affine_sum += affine_term

        # Compute a/(a+d) without forming a+d, which could overflow.
        residual_magnitude = abs(affine_residual)
        relative_denominator = abs(y) + relative_floor
        bounded_relative = if residual_magnitude == zero_l
            zero_l
        elseif residual_magnitude <= relative_denominator
            ratio = residual_magnitude / relative_denominator
            ratio / (one_l + ratio)
        else
            inverse_ratio = relative_denominator / residual_magnitude
            one_l / (one_l + inverse_ratio)
        end

        relative_square = bounded_relative * bounded_relative
        relative_square_sum += relative_square
        relative_fourth_sum += relative_square * relative_square
    end

    if !(isfinite(affine_sum) &&
         isfinite(relative_square_sum) && isfinite(relative_fourth_sum))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # The affine optimum cannot be worse than predicting mean(y).
    shape_term = sqrt(clamp(affine_sum, zero_l, one_l))

    # L2 measures typical relative accuracy; L4 is a smooth, robust soft peak
    # that gives localized structural errors more influence.
    relative_l2 = sqrt(max(relative_square_sum / n_l, zero_l))
    relative_l4 = sqrt(sqrt(max(relative_fourth_sum / n_l, zero_l)))

    bounded_raw = if isfinite(raw_sum) && raw_sum >= zero_l
        raw_nmse = raw_sum
        raw_nmse <= one_l ?
            raw_nmse / (one_l + raw_nmse) :
            one_l / (one_l + one_l / raw_nmse)
    else
        one_l
    end

    relative_weight = one_l / L(4)
    tail_weight = one_l / L(16)
    calibration_weight = one_l / L(256)

    loss_value =
        shape_term +
        relative_weight * relative_l2 +
        tail_weight * relative_l4 +
        calibration_weight * bounded_raw

    return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(max(loss_value, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
end

streamlined_affine_shape_loss_gen15_2.name: streamlined_affine_shape_loss_gen15_2
streamlined_affine_shape_loss_gen15_2.code:
"""
    streamlined_affine_shape_loss_gen15_2(tree, dataset, options)

Measure the functional shape of candidate expressions using the normalized affine
residual (the minimum root-mean-square error obtainable by any linear transformation
`a * prediction + b`), augmented with a bounded raw-error calibration tie-breaker.

# Steps:
1. Pass 1: Compute the means of the prediction and target vectors.
2. Pass 2: Accumulate sample variances, covariance, and raw residual sum of squares.
3. Shape Evaluation: Compute normalized affine RMSE via the correlation coefficient
   `sqrt(1 - r^2)`, which equals the residual error of optimal least-squares affine fitting.
4. Calibration Tie-breaker: Compute normalized raw error bounded by `x / (1 + x)` so that
   correctly calibrated expressions are favored without masking uncalibrated shapes.

# Simplifications relative to parent:
- Replaced the multi-variable Welford moment accumulation and fitted-residual re-evaluation
  with two clean, unbranched passes that enable vectorization and SIMD optimization.
- Removed Kahan compensated summation, error-tracking accumulators, and overflow guards.
- Replaced the redundant branch in the saturation function (which computed algebraically
  identical expressions on both sides) with a single smooth rational bound.
- Unified constant-target and constant-prediction edge cases into simple, robust guards.
"""
function streamlined_affine_shape_loss_gen15_2(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    # Evaluate the expression tree on the dataset features
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = dataset.n
    if n <= 0 || length(prediction) != n || length(dataset.y) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    zero_l = zero(L)
    one_l = one(L)
    n_l = L(n)

    # Pass 1: compute means
    sum_p = zero_l
    sum_y = zero_l
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])
        if !(isfinite(p) && isfinite(y))
            return L(Inf)
        end
        sum_p += p
        sum_y += y
    end

    mean_p = sum_p / n_l
    mean_y = sum_y / n_l

    if !(isfinite(mean_p) && isfinite(mean_y))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Pass 2: compute centered second moments and raw squared error
    var_p = zero_l
    var_y = zero_l
    cov_py = zero_l
    raw_sq = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])
        dp = p - mean_p
        dy = y - mean_y
        dr = p - y

        var_p += dp * dp
        var_y += dy * dy
        cov_py += dp * dy
        raw_sq += dr * dr
    end

    if !(isfinite(var_p) && isfinite(var_y) && isfinite(cov_py) && isfinite(raw_sq))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Guard against constant targets
    eps_l = eps(L)
    if var_y <= eps_l
        target_scale = max(one_l, abs(mean_y))
        raw_rmse = sqrt(max(zero_l, raw_sq / n_l)) / target_scale
        return isfinite(raw_rmse) ? L(raw_rmse) : L(Inf)
    end

    # Shape term: normalized affine RMSE = sqrt(1 - r^2)
    shape_term = if var_p <= eps_l
        one_l
    else
        denom_sq = var_p * var_y
        r_sq = (cov_py * cov_py) / denom_sq
        r_sq_clamped = clamp(r_sq, zero_l, one_l)
        sqrt(max(zero_l, one_l - r_sq_clamped))
    end

    # Calibration term: bounded normalized raw error
    raw_nmse = max(zero_l, raw_sq / var_y)
    bounded_raw = raw_nmse / (one_l + raw_nmse)

    # Combine shape loss with calibration tie-breaker (weight = 1/256 ≈ 0.0039)
    calibration_weight = one_l / L(256)
    loss_value = shape_term + calibration_weight * bounded_raw

    return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(max(loss_value, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
end

age_anchored_niche_survival_gen15_4.name: age_anchored_niche_survival_gen15_4
age_anchored_niche_survival_gen15_4.code:
"""
    age_anchored_niche_survival_gen15_4(pop, options; exclude_indices=Int[])

Age-regularized survival with bounded quality/diversity corrections.

Core synthesis
--------------
Parent 2 (`age_regularized_survival`) simply deletes the oldest member. That
rule is robust: it guarantees turnover, prevents any lineage from becoming
immortal, and is the strategy that PySR's default configuration is tuned
around. Parent 1 replaces age with a rich multi-criteria score (redundancy,
complexity crowding, family crowding, Pareto and elite protection), which adds
useful selection pressure but can also override age entirely and freeze parts of
the population.

This operator keeps age-regularization as the *anchor* and treats all of
parent 1's signals as a **bounded correction** on top of it. The age term has
unit weight over a normalized rank, while the net sum of all other terms is
clamped to `MOD_CAP` (≈0.5). Consequently the corrections can only reorder
deletion among members that are within roughly half the population's age
spread: an old clone is removed before a slightly older but unique and useful
member, yet nothing can survive indefinitely, since a member's age rank keeps
growing until it exceeds any possible protection.

Steps
-----
1. Collect complexity, loss, cost, birth and finiteness for each member.
2. Build tie-aware normalized ranks for age (1 = oldest) and cost (1 = worst),
   so members with identical values are treated identically.
3. Redundancy: hash `(complexity, rounded loss)` at a fine (8 sigdigits) and a
   coarse (5 sigdigits) resolution. The best/newest representative of each
   signature is exempt; the remaining clones get positive (delete-me) pressure.
4. Complexity-space crowding: exact-complexity occupancy plus a `±1` band
   density, both gated by cost rank so that dense-but-good building blocks are
   preserved while dense-and-poor members are cleared.
5. Family crowding: mildly penalize over-represented positive parent IDs
   (nonpositive IDs are sentinels for the initial population and are ignored).
6. Pareto protection: one quality representative per complexity, swept to find
   the non-dominated `(complexity, loss)` front. Fronts points are protected,
   with weaker protection when their loss gain is numerically negligible.
7. Elite protection for the best-cost and best-loss finite members.
8. Protections and penalties are summed, clamped to `[-MOD_CAP, +MOD_CAP]`, and
   added to the age rank. Non-finite members receive an unbounded penalty so
   they are always deleted first. A tiny jitter breaks deterministic cycles.

Assumptions: `exclude_indices` is masked once and never returned; if every slot
is excluded, index `1` is the unavoidable degenerate fallback.
"""
function age_anchored_niche_survival_gen15_4(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = pop.n
    n <= 1 && return 1

    # Mask exclusions once instead of repeatedly scanning the vector.
    excluded = falses(n)
    for idx in exclude_indices
        if 1 <= idx <= n
            excluded[idx] = true
        end
    end
    all(excluded) && return 1

    # How much the quality/diversity corrections may deviate from pure
    # age-regularization (in units of normalized age rank).
    MOD_CAP = 0.50

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Per-member statistics.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    comp = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    lossf = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    costf = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    births = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    broken = falses(n)

    for i in 1:n
        m = pop.members[i]
        comp[i] = compute_complexity(m, options)

        raw_loss = Float64(m.loss)
        raw_cost = Float64(m.cost)
        broken[i] = !isfinite(raw_loss) || !isfinite(raw_cost)

        lossf[i] = isfinite(raw_loss) ? raw_loss : Inf
        costf[i] = isfinite(raw_cost) ? raw_cost : Inf
        births[i] = Float64(m.birth)
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) Tie-aware ranks in [0, 1]: age (1 = oldest), cost (1 = worst).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    denom = Float64(max(1, n - 1))
    age_rank = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    cost_rank = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)

    # Ascending birth => oldest first => rank 1 at the end of the sweep is
    # avoided by assigning the oldest the *largest* rank below.
    age_order = sortperm(births)             # oldest (smallest birth) first
    k = 1
    while k <= n
        j = k
        while j < n && births[age_order[j + 1]] == births[age_order[k]]
            j += 1
        end
        # Average rank within the tie block, then invert so oldest -> 1.0.
        mean_pos = ((k - 1) + (j - 1)) / 2.0
        rank_value = 1.0 - mean_pos / denom
        for pos in k:j
            age_rank[age_order[pos]] = rank_value
        end
        k = j + 1
    end

    cost_order = sortperm(costf)             # best cost first
    k = 1
    while k <= n
        j = k
        while j < n && costf[cost_order[j + 1]] == costf[cost_order[k]]
            j += 1
        end
        rank_value = (((k - 1) + (j - 1)) / 2.0) / denom
        for pos in k:j
            cost_rank[cost_order[pos]] = rank_value
        end
        k = j + 1
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Two-resolution functional redundancy on (complexity, rounded loss).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    fine_sigs = Vector{Tuple{Int,Float64}}(undef, n)
    coarse_sigs = Vector{Tuple{Int,Float64}}(undef, n)
    fine_counts = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()
    coarse_counts = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()
    fine_rep = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()
    coarse_rep = Dict{Tuple{Int,Float64},Int}()

    for i in 1:n
        fine_loss = isfinite(lossf[i]) ? round(lossf[i]; sigdigits=8) : Inf
        coarse_loss = isfinite(lossf[i]) ? round(lossf[i]; sigdigits=5) : Inf
        fine_sigs[i] = (comp[i], fine_loss)
        coarse_sigs[i] = (comp[i], coarse_loss)
        fine_counts[fine_sigs[i]] = get(fine_counts, fine_sigs[i], 0) + 1
        coarse_counts[coarse_sigs[i]] = get(coarse_counts, coarse_sigs[i], 0) + 1
    end

    # Representative = lowest loss, then lowest cost, then newest.
    better_rep(i, old) =
        old == 0 ||
        lossf[i] < lossf[old] ||
        (lossf[i] == lossf[old] && costf[i] < costf[old]) ||
        (lossf[i] == lossf[old] && costf[i] == costf[old] &&
         births[i] > births[old])

    for i in 1:n
        fs = fine_sigs[i]
        better_rep(i, get(fine_rep, fs, 0)) && (fine_rep[fs] = i)
        cs = coarse_sigs[i]
        better_rep(i, get(coarse_rep, cs, 0)) && (coarse_rep[cs] = i)
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) Complexity-space crowding (exact occupancy and +-1 band density).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    comp_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for c in comp
        comp_counts[c] = get(comp_counts, c, 0) + 1
    end

    local_band = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    max_exact_count = 1
    max_band_count = 1
    for i in 1:n
        exact_count = comp_counts[comp[i]]
        band_count =
            get(comp_counts, comp[i] - 1, 0) +
            exact_count +
            get(comp_counts, comp[i] + 1, 0)
        local_band[i] = band_count
        max_exact_count = max(max_exact_count, exact_count)
        max_band_count = max(max_band_count, band_count)
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5) Immediate-family crowding (nonpositive parent IDs are sentinels).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    family_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for i in 1:n
        parent = pop.members[i].parent
        if parent > 0
            family_counts[parent] = get(family_counts, parent, 0) + 1
        end
    end
    family_scale = max(3.0, sqrt(Float64(n)))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6) Pareto front over one quality representative per complexity.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    best_at_complexity = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for i in 1:n
        c = comp[i]
        better_rep(i, get(best_at_complexity, c, 0)) && (best_at_complexity[c] = i)
    end

    frontier_order = collect(values(best_at_complexity))
    sort!(frontier_order; by=i -> comp[i])

    nondom = falses(n)
    frontier_strength = zeros(Float64, n)
    best_loss_so_far = Inf
    for idx in frontier_order
        current_loss = lossf[idx]
        if isfinite(current_loss) && current_loss < best_loss_so_far
            nondom[idx] = true
            if isinf(best_loss_so_far)
                frontier_strength[idx] = 1.0
            else
                improvement = best_loss_so_far - current_loss
                tol = 1.0e-12 + 1.0e-6 * abs(best_loss_so_far)
                # Numerically negligible gains earn only partial protection.
                frontier_strength[idx] = improvement > tol ? 1.0 : 0.35
            end
            best_loss_so_far = current_loss
        end
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7) Finite elites: best cost and best loss (ties favor simpler, newer).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    best_cost_idx = 0
    best_loss_idx = 0
    for i in 1:n
        broken[i] && continue

        if best_cost_idx == 0 ||
           costf[i] < costf[best_cost_idx] ||
           (costf[i] == costf[best_cost_idx] && comp[i] < comp[best_cost_idx]) ||
           (costf[i] == costf[best_cost_idx] && comp[i] == comp[best_cost_idx] &&
            births[i] > births[best_cost_idx])
            best_cost_idx = i
        end

        if best_loss_idx == 0 ||
           lossf[i] < lossf[best_loss_idx] ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[best_loss_idx] && comp[i] < comp[best_loss_idx]) ||
           (lossf[i] == lossf[best_loss_idx] && comp[i] == comp[best_loss_idx] &&
            costf[i] < costf[best_loss_idx])
            best_loss_idx = i
        end
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 8) Score: age anchor + clamped correction. Largest score is deleted.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    best_score = -Inf
    best_choice = 0

    for i in 1:n
        excluded[i] && continue

        # --- delete-me pressures ---
        fine_count = fine_counts[fine_sigs[i]]
        coarse_count = coarse_counts[coarse_sigs[i]]

        fine_duplicate_penalty = 0.0
        if fine_count > 1 && fine_rep[fine_sigs[i]] != i
            # Saturating: a large clone group is not worse than a big one.
            fine_duplicate_penalty = 0.70 + 0.30 * min(1.0, (fine_count - 2) / 3.0)
        end

        coarse_niche_penalty = 0.0
        if coarse_count > 1 && coarse_rep[coarse_sigs[i]] != i
            coarse_niche_penalty = min(1.0, (coarse_count - 1) / 4.0)
        end

        exact_crowding =
            max_exact_count > 1 ?
            (comp_counts[comp[i]] - 1) / Float64(max_exact_count - 1) : 0.0
        band_crowding =
            max_band_count > 1 ?
            (local_band[i] - 1) / Float64(max_band_count - 1) : 0.0

        parent = pop.members[i].parent
        family_count = parent > 0 ? get(family_counts, parent, 1) : 1
        family_crowding = min(1.0, (family_count - 1) / family_scale)

        # Crowding/family pressure acts mainly on low-quality members.
        quality_gate = 0.35 + 0.65 * cost_rank[i]

        modifier =
            0.55 * fine_duplicate_penalty +
            0.18 * coarse_niche_penalty +
            0.30 * cost_rank[i] +
            quality_gate * (0.20 * exact_crowding + 0.15 * band_crowding) +
            0.12 * quality_gate * family_crowding

        # --- keep-me protections (decay with age, so nothing is immortal) ---
        if nondom[i]
            pareto_quality = 0.40 + 0.60 * frontier_strength[i]
            modifier -= 0.55 * pareto_quality * (1.0 - 0.50 * age_rank[i])
        end
        if i == best_cost_idx
            modifier -= 0.45 * (1.0 - 0.40 * age_rank[i])
        end
        if i == best_loss_idx
            modifier -= 0.30 * (1.0 - 0.40 * age_rank[i])
        end

        # Bound the correction so age-regularization remains the backbone.
        modifier = clamp(modifier, -MOD_CAP, MOD_CAP)

        score = age_rank[i] + modifier

        # Invalid members are always the first to go, regardless of the cap.
        broken[i] && (score += 5.0)

        # Tiny jitter only matters for near-exact ties.
        score += 0.004 * rand()

        if score > best_score
            best_score = score
            best_choice = i
        end
    end

    return best_choice == 0 ? 1 : best_choice
end

motif_duplication_graft_encapsulate_gen1.name: motif_duplication_graft_encapsulate_gen15_5
motif_duplication_graft_encapsulate_gen1.code:
"""
    motif_duplication_graft_encapsulate_gen15_5(tree::N, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}

A structural mutation operator that *reuses evolved sub-structure*: it clones an existing
subexpression (a "motif"), optionally re-indexes its variables, optionally wraps it in a unary
operator, and then re-integrates it into the tree either by **binary coupling** or by
**homologous grafting** (in-place replacement of another node).

# Core idea (synthesis of both parents)
Ground-truth laws are built from repeated functional forms applied to different variables
(`0.5*m*(vx^2+vy^2)`, `(x1-x2)^2+(y1-y2)^2`) *and* from nesting an already-discovered inner
quantity inside a new envelope (`x0/sqrt(1-(x1/x2)^2)`, `u/(1+u^2)`). Point mutations must
rediscover each copy / each nesting independently, which is exponentially unlikely.

Parent 1 contributed the *quality controls*: a hard size budget derived from `options.maxsize`,
tiered donor sampling that prefers compound variable-bearing motifs (instead of degenerating into
`insert_random_op` on a bare leaf), degeneracy avoidance for self-couplings, and a bias toward the
canonical symmetric accumulators `+` / `*`.
Parent 2 contributed the *second integration channel*: homologous grafting, which can install a
rich motif where a bare constant/variable leaf sits (a move that pure coupling can never make,
because coupling only ever grows the tree), plus the unary fallback when no binary operator exists.

New in this operator: **unary encapsulation**. Before integration, the motif may be wrapped in a
random unary operator (`sqrt`, `square`, `exp`, `log`, ...). This is the missing move seen in the
`rho_c/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2)` trace, where the search found the inner motif `x1/x2` early but never
managed to build the envelope `sqrt(1 - square(x1/x2))` around it, and instead wasted its budget
on ever-longer rational patchwork.

# Steps
1. If no binary operator exists, fall back to wrapping a random node in a unary operator (parent 2).
2. Roll the integration mode (grafting with prob. 0.3 on non-trivial trees, else coupling) and
   whether to encapsulate the motif in a unary operator (prob. 0.3 when unary ops exist).
3. Sample a donor with tiered preference: (a) compound, variable-bearing subtrees that fit the
   budget, (b) any variable-bearing subtree that fits, (c) any subtree that fits.
4. Remap the clone's feature indices: cyclic shift (block symmetry), targeted single-feature
   substitution (pairwise exchange `x -> y`), or identity (powers / rational self-couplings);
   the identity case is perturbed when donor and target coincide and no encapsulation happens,
   to avoid trivially simplifiable `u + u`.
5. Integrate:
   * **coupling** — new size is `size(tree) + size(motif) + 1`, so the donor budget is
     `maxsize - size(tree) - 1` (minus one more if encapsulating); operator biased to `+`/`*`
     and operand order randomized for non-commutative ops;
   * **grafting** — new size is `size(tree) - size(target) + size(motif)`, so the *target* is
     constrained to be large enough; leaves are preferred (prob. 0.6) whenever they are admissible,
     which is exactly the "fill a placeholder constant with real structure" move.
6. If the coupling budget is exhausted (tree already near `maxsize`), the operator automatically
   falls back to grafting, which can be size-neutral or size-reducing.

# Assumptions
Donor/target may coincide or be nested; all inserted material is deep-copied, so aliasing is
impossible. `options.maxsize` is respected only approximately in the sense of node counts (not
custom complexity maps), which is the same convention the parents used.
"""
function motif_duplication_graft_encapsulate_gen15_5(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    nuna = options.nops[1]
    nbin = options.nops[2]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Step 1: fallback
    # Without a binary operator we cannot couple; degrade to a unary wrap (parent 2 behaviour).
    if nbin == 0
        if nuna > 0
            node = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
            set_node!(
                node,
                constructorof(N)(; op=rand(rng, 1:nuna), children=(copy(node),)),
            )
        end
        return tree
    end

    tree_size = count_nodes(tree)
    maxsize = hasproperty(options, :maxsize) ? options.maxsize : typemax(Int)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
    # Apply an arbitrary index map to every variable leaf of a subtree.
    function _map_features!(node, fmap)
        if node.degree == 0
            node.constant || (node.feature = fmap(node.feature))
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _map_features!(get_child(node, i), fmap)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    # Distinct feature indices appearing in a subtree.
    function _collect_features!(acc::Vector{Int}, node)
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant && !(node.feature in acc)
                push!(acc, node.feature)
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _collect_features!(acc, get_child(node, i))
            end
        end
        return acc
    end

    _has_var(t) = any(n -> n.degree == 0 && !n.constant, t)

    # Tiered donor sampling restricted to a node-count budget (parent 1's motif quality filter).
    function _sample_donor(budget::Int)
        budget < 1 && return nothing
        _fits(t) = count_nodes(t) <= budget
        _tier1(t) = t.degree > 0 && _fits(t) && _has_var(t)
        if count(_tier1, tree) > 0 && rand(rng) < 0.75
            return rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_tier1))
        end
        _tier2(t) = _fits(t) && _has_var(t)
        if count(_tier2, tree) > 0
            return rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_tier2))
        end
        if count(_fits, tree) > 0
            return rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_fits))
        end
        return nothing
    end

    # Feature-space transformation of the cloned motif.
    # `perturb_identity`: force a shift when the identity draw would be degenerate.
    function _remap!(motif, perturb_identity::Bool)
        nfeatures <= 1 && return motif
        r = rand(rng)
        if r < 0.45
            # (a) cyclic shift: replicate the form across a whole variable block
            shift = rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1))
            _map_features!(motif, f -> mod1(f + shift, nfeatures))
        elseif r < 0.80
            # (b) targeted substitution: exchange exactly one feature present in the motif
            feats = _collect_features!(Int[], motif)
            if !isempty(feats)
                src = feats[rand(rng, 1:length(feats))]
                dst = rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1))
                dst >= src && (dst += 1)  # uniform over targets != src
                _map_features!(motif, f -> (f == src ? dst : f))
            end
        else
            # (c) identity: powers (`u*u`) and rational self-couplings (`u/(1+u)`)
            if perturb_identity && rand(rng, Bool)
                shift = rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1))
                _map_features!(motif, f -> mod1(f + shift, nfeatures))
            end
        end
        return motif
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Step 2: mode rolls
    do_graft = tree_size > 3 && rand(rng) < 0.3
    encapsulate = nuna > 0 && rand(rng) < 0.3

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Step 5a: coupling path
    if !do_graft
        budget = maxsize - tree_size - 1 - (encapsulate ? 1 : 0)
        donor = _sample_donor(budget)
        if donor === nothing
            # No admissible motif for growth: fall through to (possibly size-neutral) grafting.
            do_graft = true
        else
            motif = copy(donor)
            # Sometimes couple the donor with itself (powers / rational self-coupling).
            target = rand(rng) < 0.3 ? donor : rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
            self_coupling = target === donor
            _remap!(motif, self_coupling && !encapsulate)

            if encapsulate
                # Build an envelope around the reused motif, e.g. sqrt(u), square(u), exp(u).
                motif = constructorof(N)(; op=rand(rng, 1:nuna), children=(motif,))
            end

            # Bias toward `+` / `*`, the canonical symmetric accumulators.
            binops = options.operators.binops
            pref = Int[]
            for i in 1:nbin
                op = binops[i]
                (op === (+) || op === (*)) && push!(pref, i)
            end
            bin_op = if !isempty(pref) && rand(rng) < 0.6
                pref[rand(rng, 1:length(pref))]
            else
                rand(rng, 1:nbin)
            end

            target_copy = copy(target)
            # Randomize operand order so non-commutative ops explore both arrangements.
            children = rand(rng, Bool) ? (target_copy, motif) : (motif, target_copy)
            set_node!(target, constructorof(N)(; op=bin_op, children=children))
            return tree
        end
    end

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Step 5b: grafting path
    # Any subtree of `tree` trivially satisfies size <= tree_size; also respect maxsize.
    donor = _sample_donor(min(maxsize, tree_size))
    donor === nothing && return tree

    motif = copy(donor)
    _remap!(motif, true)  # a pure identity graft onto an unrelated target is still meaningful
    if encapsulate
        motif = constructorof(N)(; op=rand(rng, 1:nuna), children=(motif,))
    end
    msize = count_nodes(motif)

    # Replacement keeps the tree admissible iff size(target) >= msize - (maxsize - tree_size).
    need = msize - (maxsize - tree_size)
    _ok_target(t) = count_nodes(t) >= need

    target = if need <= 1 && count(t -> t.degree == 0, tree) > 0 && rand(rng) < 0.6
        # Preferred move: install real structure where a bare constant/variable placeholder sits.
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=t -> t.degree == 0))
    elseif count(_ok_target, tree) > 0
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_ok_target))
    else
        return tree  # motif too large for any admissible replacement site
    end

    set_node!(target, motif)
    return tree
end

pareto_aspiration_lineage_selection_gen1.name: pareto_aspiration_lineage_selection_gen15_7
pareto_aspiration_lineage_selection_gen1.code:
"""
    pareto_aspiration_lineage_selection_gen15_7(pop, running_search_statistics, options)

Select a parent from a tournament using a stochastic loss-complexity Pareto ladder.
The operator first removes candidates dominated in both raw loss and expression
complexity. It then orders the surviving frontier from best-fitting to simplest
and samples a loss aspiration level: most selections remain near the best loss,
while occasional broad aspirations preserve useful simple stepping stones.
A relative-loss cliff detector prevents crossing a large fitness discontinuity,
which protects unusually strong discoveries.

Within the admissible portion of the frontier, candidates are scored by
simplicity, fit rank, adaptive complexity-frequency rarity, tournament-local
parent-lineage crowding, and cost as a weak tie-breaker. Rank-based quantities
make the heuristic insensitive to the absolute scale of the benchmark loss.
Non-finite losses are excluded whenever any finite candidate is available.
"""
function pareto_aspiration_lineage_selection_gen15_7(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    tournament_n = min(max(Int(options.tournament_selection_n), 1), length(pop.members))
    sample = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, tournament_n; replace=false)
    n = length(sample)

    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    losses = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    costs = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
    frequencies = zeros(Float64, n)

    for i in 1:n
        member = sample[i]
        complexities[i] = Int(compute_complexity(member, options))

        raw_loss = Float64(member.loss)
        raw_cost = Float64(member.cost)
        losses[i] = isfinite(raw_loss) ? raw_loss : Inf
        costs[i] = isfinite(raw_cost) ? raw_cost : Inf

        size = complexities[i]
        if 0 < size <= length(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies)
            frequency = Float64(
                running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[size]
            )
            frequencies[i] = isfinite(frequency) ? max(frequency, 0.0) : 0.0
        end
    end

    finite_indices = Int[i for i in 1:n if isfinite(losses[i])]

    # If every raw loss is invalid, fall back to rank-based cost, complexity,
    # and rarity rather than allowing NaNs or infinities into later arithmetic.
    if isempty(finite_indices)
        fallback_scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, n)
        denominator = max(n - 1, 1)
        maxsize = max(Int(options.maxsize), 1)
        scaling = max(Float64(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling), 0.0)

        for i in 1:n
            cost_rank = 0
            for j in 1:n
                cost_rank += costs[j] < costs[i]
            end

            rarity_penalty = if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
                1.0 - exp(-min(50.0, scaling * frequencies[i]))
            else
                0.0
            end

            fallback_scores[i] =
                cost_rank / denominator +
                0.25 * clamp(complexities[i] / maxsize, 0.0, 2.0) +
                0.35 * rarity_penalty +
                1.0e-10 * rand()
        end
        return sample[argmin_fast(fallback_scores)]
    end

    # Construct the nondominated frontier in raw-loss/complexity space.
    frontier = Int[]
    for i in finite_indices
        dominated = false
        for j in finite_indices
            i == j && continue

            no_worse =
                losses[j] <= losses[i] && complexities[j] <= complexities[i]
            strictly_better =
                losses[j] < losses[i] || complexities[j] < complexities[i]

            # Cost only resolves exact loss-complexity duplicates.
            duplicate_better =
                losses[j] == losses[i] &&
                complexities[j] == complexities[i] &&
                costs[j] < costs[i]

            if no_worse && (strictly_better || duplicate_better)
                dominated = true
                break
            end
        end
        !dominated && push!(frontier, i)
    end

    # The first rung is the best fit; later rungs trade fit for simplicity.
    sort!(
        frontier;
        by=i -> (losses[i], complexities[i], costs[i], sample[i].birth),
    )
    m = length(frontier)

    pressure = clamp(Float64(options.tournament_selection_p), 0.0, 1.0)
    mode = rand()

    # Sample an aspiration rung. The normal regime is biased toward strong fit,
    # while a small exploration regime deliberately reaches simpler rungs.
    k = if m == 1 || mode < 0.20
        1
    elseif mode < 0.88
        exponent = 1.5 + 2.5 * pressure
        1 + floor(Int, (m - 1) * rand()^exponent)
    else
        1 + floor(Int, (m - 1) * sqrt(rand()))
    end
    k = clamp(k, 1, m)

    # Detect a sharp relative-loss cliff before the sampled aspiration. This
    # avoids discarding an exceptional fit merely to gain a little simplicity.
    if k > 1
        best_loss = losses[frontier[1]]
        scale = max(abs(best_loss), sqrt(eps(Float64)))
        relative_fit = zeros(Float64, k)

        for r in 2:k
            difference = losses[frontier[r]] - best_loss
            if !isfinite(difference)
                relative_fit[r] = 1.0
            elseif difference <= scale
                relative_fit[r] = difference / (difference + scale)
            else
                # Algebraically equivalent form avoids overflow for large gaps.
                relative_fit[r] = 1.0 / (1.0 + scale / difference)
            end
        end

        largest_gap = -Inf
        cliff_before = k
        for r in 2:k
            gap = relative_fit[r] - relative_fit[r - 1]
            if gap > largest_gap
                largest_gap = gap
                cliff_before = r - 1
            end
        end

        total_change = relative_fit[k]
        if total_change > 0.0 &&
           largest_gap > 0.55 * total_change &&
           rand() < 0.75
            k = max(cliff_before, 1)
        end
    end

    admissible = frontier[1:k]
    min_complexity = minimum(complexities[i] for i in admissible)
    max_complexity = maximum(complexities[i] for i in admissible)
    complexity_span = max(max_complexity - min_complexity, 1)
    rank_denominator = max(k - 1, 1)
    lineage_denominator = max(n - 1, 1)
    scaling = max(Float64(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling), 0.0)

    scores = Vector{Float64}(undef, k)
    exploratory = mode >= 0.88

    for r in 1:k
        i = admissible[r]

        simplicity_term =
            (complexities[i] - min_complexity) / complexity_span
        fit_rank_term = (r - 1) / rank_denominator

        rarity_term = if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            # Saturation prevents a single crowded size from overwhelming fit.
            1.0 - exp(-min(50.0, scaling * frequencies[i]))
        else
            0.0
        end

        # Penalize sibling-heavy local niches, but do not group independently
        # generated members whose parent sentinel is non-positive.
        sibling_count = 1
        parent_ref = sample[i].parent
        if parent_ref > 0
            sibling_count = 0
            for j in 1:n
                sibling_count += sample[j].parent == parent_ref
            end
        end
        lineage_term = (sibling_count - 1) / lineage_denominator

        # Cost is intentionally weak because loss and complexity already form
        # the main Pareto objectives.
        cost_rank = 0
        for j in admissible
            cost_rank += costs[j] < costs[i]
        end
        cost_rank_term = cost_rank / rank_denominator

        fit_weight = exploratory ? 0.12 : 0.30
        rarity_weight = exploratory ? 0.90 : 0.45

        scores[r] =
            simplicity_term +
            fit_weight * fit_rank_term +
            rarity_weight * rarity_term +
            0.20 * lineage_term +
            0.08 * cost_rank_term +
            1.0e-10 * rand()
    end

    return sample[admissible[argmin_fast(scores)]]
end

pareto_adaptive_tournament_selection_gen.name: pareto_adaptive_tournament_selection_gen15_9
pareto_adaptive_tournament_selection_gen.code:
"""
    pareto_adaptive_tournament_selection_gen15_9(
        pop::Population{T,L,N},
        running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
        options::AbstractOptions,
    )::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}

Pareto-Adaptive Tournament Selection with Age Regularization for Symbolic Regression.

# Core Idea
Standard tournament selection compresses multi-objective symbolic regression trade-offs
into a single scalar cost with global frequency penalties. This can cause two failure modes:
1. Strictly dominated, bloated expressions can defeat simpler and more accurate models
   purely due to transient complexity-frequency fluctuations.
2. Promising new structural innovations ("young" expressions) are prematurely eliminated
   before their numerical constants can be fully tuned against mature solutions.

This operator implements a multi-objective Pareto-layered tournament that:
- Identifies the local Pareto frontier in (Loss, Complexity) space within the tournament sample.
- Ranks non-dominated expressions ahead of strictly dominated ones.
- Modulates within-rank selection using global adaptive parsimony (frequency scaling) to
  prevent complexity crowding.
- Applies an age-regularization discount to protect newly created expressions, giving them
  an exploration window to refine constants and structural motifs.

# Key Steps & Heuristics
1. **Sample**: Select `tournament_selection_n` individuals randomly without replacement.
2. **Pareto Dominance Assessment**: For each candidate in the sample, compute its dominance
   count: how many other sampled candidates achieve both lower/equal loss and smaller/equal size
   (with at least one strict inequality). Candidates on the sample's Pareto front have `dom_count = 0`.
3. **Adaptive Parsimony & Age Regularization**: For each candidate, compute an adjusted cost
   combining raw cost, complexity-frequency penalization (`adaptive_parsimony_scaling`), and a
   recency bonus (ALPS-inspired) derived from `member.birth`.
4. **Hierarchical Ranking**: Order candidates lexicographically by `(dom_count, adjusted_cost)`:
   Pareto-optimal candidates are preferred first, and ties are broken by frequency/age-adjusted cost.
5. **Probabilistic Selection**: Select the winner using geometric rank-probability weighting
   parameterized by `tournament_selection_p` (or deterministic top-rank if `p == 1.0`).

# What Changed vs. Parent
- **Pareto Dominance Guard**: Prevents strictly suboptimal/bloated solutions from being selected over
  strictly superior solutions.
- **Age-Aware Exploration**: Incorporates relative birth recency to prevent innovation death of young
  trees before constant optimization can mature.
- **Lexicographical Ranking**: Replaces fragile scalar mixing with exact multi-criteria sorting.
"""
function pareto_adaptive_tournament_selection_gen15_9(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Determine sample size bounded by population size
    n_sample = min(options.tournament_selection_n, pop.n)
    if n_sample <= 1
        return copy(pop.members[1])
    end

    # 1. Sample candidate tournament members without replacement
    sample = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, n_sample; replace=false)
    n = length(sample)

    # 2. Extract metrics: losses, complexities, and birth timestamps
    losses = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    sizes = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    births = Vector{Int}(undef, n)

    min_birth = typemax(Int)
    max_birth = typemin(Int)

    for i in 1:n
        member = sample[i]
        loss_val = member.loss
        losses[i] = (isnan(loss_val) || isinf(loss_val)) ? typemax(L) : loss_val
        sizes[i] = compute_complexity(member, options)
        b = member.birth
        births[i] = b
        if b < min_birth
            min_birth = b
        end
        if b > max_birth
            max_birth = b
        end
    end

    # 3. Compute Pareto Dominance Count within the tournament sample
    # dom_counts[i] is the number of sampled members strictly dominating member i
    dom_counts = zeros(Int, n)
    for i in 1:n
        # Disqualify invalid models or expressions exceeding maxsize
        if losses[i] == typemax(L) || sizes[i] > options.maxsize
            dom_counts[i] = n
            continue
        end
        l_i = losses[i]
        s_i = sizes[i]
        for j in 1:n
            if i == j
                continue
            end
            l_j = losses[j]
            s_j = sizes[j]
            # Member j strictly dominates member i if j is no worse in both objectives
            # and strictly better in at least one objective
            if (l_j <= l_i) && (s_j <= s_i) && ((l_j < l_i) || (s_j < s_i))
                dom_counts[i] += 1
            end
        end
    end

    # 4. Compute Adaptive Frequency & Age-Adjusted Cost
    adjusted_costs = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    birth_span = max_birth - min_birth
    age_bonus_scale = L(0.15) # Up to 15% selection advantage for newest structural mutations

    for i in 1:n
        member = sample[i]
        c = member.cost
        if isnan(c) || isinf(c)
            adjusted_costs[i] = typemax(L)
            continue
        end

        # Frequency-based parsimony multiplier
        freq_penalty = if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            sz = sizes[i]
            freq = if (0 < sz <= options.maxsize)
                L(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[sz])
            else
                L(0)
            end
            exp(L(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling) * freq)
        else
            L(1)
        end

        # Recency/Age protection factor: relative_age in [0, 1] (0 = youngest, 1 = oldest)
        age_penalty = if birth_span > 0
            relative_age = L(max_birth - births[i]) / L(birth_span)
            L(1) + age_bonus_scale * relative_age
        else
            L(1)
        end

        adjusted_costs[i] = c * freq_penalty * age_penalty
    end

    # 5. Lexicographical Sorting: Dominance Count first, then Adjusted Cost
    rank_order = collect(1:n)
    sort!(rank_order, by = i -> (dom_counts[i], adjusted_costs[i]))

    # 6. Probabilistic Winner Selection
    p = options.tournament_selection_p
    chosen_idx = if p == 1.0f0 || n == 1
        rank_order[1]
    else
        k = collect(0:(n - 1))
        prob_each = p .* ((1.0f0 - p) .^ k)
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(prob_each, sum(prob_each))
        tournament_winner = StatsBase.sample(weights)
        rank_order[tournament_winner]
    end

    return copy(sample[chosen_idx])
end

duplicate_motif_with_optional_shift_gen1.name: duplicate_motif_with_optional_shift_gen16_2
duplicate_motif_with_optional_shift_gen1.code:
"""
    duplicate_motif_with_optional_shift_gen16_2(tree::N, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG)

Duplicate a randomly selected subtree and couple the two copies with a binary operator.
The duplicate is either left unchanged, encouraging powers and repeated rational motifs, or
given one cyclic feature shift, encouraging symmetric terms across variables.

This streamlined version removes targeted single-feature substitution, unrelated-target
grafting, tree-size heuristics, and the unary fallback. It always performs the core operation
directly at the donor site, concentrating mutations on useful self-couplings and symmetric
motif pairs while requiring fewer random decisions.
"""
function duplicate_motif_with_optional_shift_gen16_2(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # Motif coupling requires a binary operator.
    options.nops[2] == 0 && return tree

    # Apply one consistent feature permutation throughout a copied motif.
    function shift_features!(node, shift::Int)
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant
                node.feature = mod1(node.feature + shift, nfeatures)
            end
        else
            for i in 1:node.degree
                shift_features!(get_child(node, i), shift)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    donor = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
    original = copy(donor)
    duplicate = copy(donor)

    # Identity duplication supports u*u and u/u; shifting supports symmetric analogues.
    if nfeatures > 1 && rand(rng, Bool)
        shift_features!(duplicate, rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1)))
    end

    # Random ordering retains access to both orientations of subtraction and division.
    children = rand(rng, Bool) ? (original, duplicate) : (duplicate, original)
    replacement = constructorof(N)(;
        op=rand(rng, 1:options.nops[2]),
        children=children,
    )
    set_node!(donor, replacement)

    return tree
end

pareto_guarded_age_regularized_survival_.name: pareto_guarded_age_regularized_survival_gen16_1
pareto_guarded_age_regularized_survival_.code:
"""
    pareto_guarded_age_regularized_survival_gen16_1(pop, options; exclude_indices=Int[])

Select a population member for replacement using quality-guarded age regularization.

The operator first orders all eligible members by birth and considers only a small
cohort of the oldest members, preserving the parent's emphasis on turnover and
exploration. Within that cohort, it preferentially removes the member most often
Pareto-dominated in raw loss and expression complexity. Ties favor the oldest
member. A hard age limit falls back to strict oldest-member replacement so that
high-quality individuals cannot become permanently immortal.

Compared with the parent operator, this protects accurate or structurally simple
building blocks from premature deletion when a clearly inferior, similarly old
member is available, while retaining bounded lifetimes and respecting every index
in `exclude_indices`.
"""
function pareto_guarded_age_regularized_survival_gen16_1(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Build the eligible set explicitly so crossover cannot select the same slot twice.
    excluded = falses(pop.n)
    for idx in exclude_indices
        if 1 <= idx <= pop.n
            excluded[idx] = true
        end
    end
    eligible = [i for i in 1:pop.n if !excluded[i]]

    isempty(eligible) &&
        throw(ArgumentError("survival requires at least one non-excluded member"))

    # Oldest members come first; this order also supplies deterministic age tie-breaking.
    sort!(eligible; by=i -> pop.members[i].birth)
    oldest = first(eligible)

    length(eligible) == 1 && return oldest

    # Force eventual turnover after roughly two population generations.
    oldest_birth = pop.members[oldest].birth
    newest_birth = pop.members[last(eligible)].birth
    if newest_birth - oldest_birth >= 2 * pop.n
        return oldest
    end

    # Restrict quality comparisons to an old cohort so youth remains protected.
    cohort_size = min(length(eligible), max(2, options.tournament_selection_n))
    cohort = @view eligible[1:cohort_size]
    losses = [pop.members[idx].loss for idx in cohort]
    complexities = [compute_complexity(pop.members[idx], options) for idx in cohort]

    # Finite losses dominate invalid losses; if both are invalid, complexity decides.
    function dominates(a_loss, a_complexity, b_loss, b_complexity)
        a_finite = isfinite(a_loss)
        b_finite = isfinite(b_loss)

        loss_no_worse =
            a_finite ? (!b_finite || a_loss <= b_loss) : !b_finite
        loss_strictly_better =
            a_finite && (!b_finite || a_loss < b_loss)

        return loss_no_worse &&
               a_complexity <= b_complexity &&
               (loss_strictly_better || a_complexity < b_complexity)
    end

    # Count how many similarly old members dominate each possible victim.
    domination_counts = zeros(Int, cohort_size)
    for victim_pos in 1:cohort_size
        for challenger_pos in 1:cohort_size
            challenger_pos == victim_pos && continue
            if dominates(
                losses[challenger_pos],
                complexities[challenger_pos],
                losses[victim_pos],
                complexities[victim_pos],
            )
                domination_counts[victim_pos] += 1
            end
        end
    end

    # Strict updates preserve the oldest member as the tie-breaker.
    victim_pos = 1
    for pos in 2:cohort_size
        if domination_counts[pos] > domination_counts[victim_pos]
            victim_pos = pos
        end
    end

    return cohort[victim_pos]
end

crowding_suppressed_rare_niche_tournamen.name: crowding_suppressed_rare_niche_tournament_gen16_4
crowding_suppressed_rare_niche_tournamen.code:
"""
    crowding_suppressed_rare_niche_tournament_gen16_4(pop, running_search_statistics, options)

Simplified crowding-suppressed niche tournament.

Core idea (kept from the parent): sample a slightly enlarged tournament pool, score it
with the usual frequency-adjusted cost, demote members that are *redundant copies* of a
better pool member so that a single champion skeleton and its clones cannot monopolise
selection, and occasionally select from the rarest complexity niche instead of the
fittest member so that starved complexity bands (the mid-size building blocks needed to
assemble e.g. `sqrt(x2/(x2 - x1^2/x2))`) get repopulated.

Steps:
 1. Sample `~1.5 * tournament_selection_n` distinct members (enlarged pool so that
    redundancy / niche information exists at all).
 2. Compute complexity and the default adaptive-parsimony-adjusted cost
    (`cost * exp(scaling * normalized_frequency[complexity])`).
 3. Clone suppression: walk the pool from best to worst adjusted cost; count how many
    strictly better members are effectively the same solution (identical complexity and
    loss equal within a relative tolerance) and inflate the score geometrically by
    `clone_penalty^clones`. The best representative of a cluster is never penalised.
 4. With probability `p_rare_niche`, return the pool member whose complexity has the
    smallest `normalized_frequencies` value (ties broken by penalised score); otherwise
    run the standard geometric tournament ladder over the penalised scores.

What was removed / merged relative to the parent, and why it is still sound:
 - The **sibling (shared-parent) partial redundancy term** was dropped: siblings from one
   parent are usually already caught by the "same complexity + same loss" clone test when
   they are truly redundant, and when they are not redundant they are genuinely different
   structures that should not be penalised.
 - The **youth discount** (recency-based cost reduction, plus the birth min/max scan) was
   dropped: it is a very small (<=5%) multiplicative nudge whose anti-stagnation role is
   already covered by clone suppression plus the rare-niche exploration move, so removing
   it costs little and eliminates a whole tunable and pass over the pool.
 - The sign-safe `inflate` closure was folded into a single inline ternary applied only to
   members that actually have clones, so the common (no-redundancy) path is exactly the
   default tournament.
"""
function crowding_suppressed_rare_niche_tournament_gen16_4(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # ---------------- tunables (mild, so we degrade to the default tournament) ----
    pool_scale = 1.5        # pool size relative to tournament_selection_n
    clone_penalty = 1.35    # score inflation per detected better clone
    loss_rtol = 1e-6        # relative tolerance for "the same loss"
    p_rare_niche = 0.10     # probability of the explicit rare-complexity pick

    # ---------------- 1. sample the (enlarged) pool -------------------------------
    n_base = options.tournament_selection_n
    pool_size = min(pop.n, max(n_base, round(Int, pool_scale * n_base)))
    pool = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, pool_size; replace=false)
    n = length(pool)

    # ---------------- 2. base (frequency-adjusted) scores -------------------------
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    scores = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    adaptive_parsimony_scaling = L(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling)
    for i in 1:n
        member = pool[i]
        size = compute_complexity(member, options)
        complexities[i] = size
        if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            frequency = if (0 < size <= options.maxsize)
                L(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[size])
            else
                zero(L)
            end
            scores[i] = member.cost * exp(adaptive_parsimony_scaling * frequency)
        else
            scores[i] = member.cost
        end
    end

    # ---------------- 3. clone suppression ----------------------------------------
    # Process best -> worst so the best representative of each cluster is untouched
    # and each subsequent twin is demoted a bit more.
    order = sortperm(scores)
    penalized = copy(scores)
    for a in 2:n
        i = order[a]
        li = pool[i].loss
        clones = 0
        for b in 1:(a - 1)
            j = order[b]
            lj = pool[j].loss
            # cheap allocation-free proxy for "structurally the same expression"
            if complexities[i] == complexities[j] &&
                abs(li - lj) <= L(loss_rtol) * max(abs(li), abs(lj), eps(L))
                clones += 1
            end
        end
        if clones > 0
            f = L(clone_penalty^clones)
            # sign-safe inflation: "worse" always means a larger penalized score
            penalized[i] = scores[i] > zero(L) ? scores[i] * f : scores[i] / f
        end
    end

    # ---------------- 4a. occasional rare-complexity (niche) pick -----------------
    if rand() < p_rare_niche
        best_idx = 1
        best_freq = Inf
        best_score = penalized[1]
        for i in 1:n
            c = complexities[i]
            f = if (0 < c <= options.maxsize)
                Float64(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[c])
            else
                0.0  # out-of-range sizes count as maximally rare
            end
            if f < best_freq || (f == best_freq && penalized[i] < best_score)
                best_freq = f
                best_score = penalized[i]
                best_idx = i
            end
        end
        return pool[best_idx]
    end

    # ---------------- 4b. standard geometric tournament ladder --------------------
    p = options.tournament_selection_p
    chosen_idx = if p == 1.0
        argmin_fast(penalized)
    else
        k = collect(0:(n - 1))
        prob_each = p * ((1 - p) .^ k)
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(prob_each, sum(prob_each))
        tournament_winner = StatsBase.sample(weights)
        if tournament_winner == 1
            argmin_fast(penalized)
        else
