    bounded_raw = isfinite(raw_nmse) ? raw_nmse / (one_l + raw_nmse) : one_l

    loss_value = shape_term + bounded_raw / L(256)
    return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(max(loss_value, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
end

structure_verified_occupancy_balanced_ni.name: structure_verified_occupancy_balanced_niche_tournament_gen29_1
structure_verified_occupancy_balanced_ni.code:
"""
    structure_verified_occupancy_balanced_niche_tournament_gen29_1(
        pop, running_search_statistics, options
    )

Select a parent with adaptive-parsimony quality, bounded clone crowding, mild
lineage turnover, and quality-gated complexity-niche exploration.

The operator:

 1. Samples an enlarged tournament pool and computes frequency-adjusted costs using
    sign-safe multiplicative penalties.
 2. Orders candidates by quality, preferring newer members when scores tie.
 3. Detects structural copies with `isequal` on expression trees. Exact copies
    contribute both a shared occupancy burden and a rank-directional redundancy
    penalty. Related near-equal candidates receive smaller penalties, while
    unrelated candidates with coincidentally similar complexity and loss receive
    only a soft directional penalty.
 4. Caps both occupancy and directional crowding before combining them. The shared
    component mildly penalizes even the best representative of a clone monopoly,
    fixing the parent's asymmetry where one unpenalized clone could still dominate.
 5. Applies a small recency discount that is strongest for uncrowded structures.
 6. Adapts niche-exploration probability to clone pressure and repeated complexity
    occupancy. Niche moves retain the best representative per complexity, quality
    gate them, then sample using a smooth blend of quality, global rarity, and local
    rarity rather than deterministically choosing the rarest niche.
 7. Otherwise uses the configured geometric tournament ladder.

Compared with the parent, structural verification reduces false clone suppression,
crowding is bounded and partly symmetric, adaptive parsimony is sign-safe, tie
handling favors lineage turnover, and niche selection balances rarity against
quality instead of allowing a single rarity statistic to dominate.
"""
function structure_verified_occupancy_balanced_niche_tournament_gen29_1(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Conservative tunables: shared pressure matters only for strong clone evidence.
    pool_scale = 1.5
    crowding_penalty = 1.30
    directional_weight = 0.70
    shared_weight = 0.30
    crowding_cap = 3.0

    clone_loss_rtol = 1e-6
    lineage_loss_rtol = 1e-2
    unrelated_phenotype_weight = 0.30
    related_phenotype_weight = 0.65
    related_shared_weight = 0.45
    lineage_weight = 0.15

    youth_discount = 0.035
    niche_probability_base = 0.05
    niche_probability_boost = 0.13
    niche_probability_max = 0.18

    # The enlarged pool exposes local clone and complexity occupancy.
    n_base = max(1, options.tournament_selection_n)
    requested_pool_size = max(n_base, round(Int, pool_scale * n_base))
    pool_size = min(pop.n, requested_pool_size)
    pool = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, pool_size; replace=false)
    n = length(pool)

    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    scores = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    adaptive_parsimony_scaling = L(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling)

    for i in 1:n
        member = pool[i]
        complexity = compute_complexity(member, options)
        complexities[i] = complexity

        if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            frequency = if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize
                L(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[complexity])
            else
                zero(L)
            end

            parsimony_factor = exp(adaptive_parsimony_scaling * frequency)

            # A factor above one must worsen either a positive or negative score.
            scores[i] = if member.cost > zero(L)
                member.cost * parsimony_factor
            elseif member.cost < zero(L)
                member.cost / parsimony_factor
            else
                member.cost
            end
        else
            scores[i] = member.cost
        end
    end

    # Newer members become the provisional representative when quality is tied.
    order = sortperm(1:n; by=i -> (scores[i], -pool[i].birth))

    # Directional redundancy preserves a best representative. Shared occupancy also
    # burdens that representative when verified copies monopolize the sampled pool.
    rank_redundancy = zeros(Float64, n)
    shared_occupancy = zeros(Float64, n)

    for a in 2:n
        i = order[a]
        li = pool[i].loss

        for b in 1:(a - 1)
            j = order[b]
            lj = pool[j].loss

            loss_scale = max(abs(li), abs(lj), eps(L))
            loss_delta = abs(li - lj)
            same_complexity = complexities[i] == complexities[j]
            clone_close =
                same_complexity &&
                loss_delta <= L(clone_loss_rtol) * loss_scale

            parent_i = pool[i].parent
            parent_j = pool[j].parent
            related =
                (parent_i != 0 && parent_i == parent_j) ||
                (parent_i != 0 && parent_i == pool[j].ref) ||
                (parent_j != 0 && parent_j == pool[i].ref)

            # Tree equality is substantially stronger evidence than equal scalar loss.
            exact_structure =
                same_complexity && isequal(pool[i].tree, pool[j].tree)

            pair_rank_weight = 0.0
            pair_shared_weight = 0.0

            if exact_structure
                pair_rank_weight = 1.0
                pair_shared_weight = 1.0
            elseif clone_close && related
                # Likely copied or minimally changed relatives.
                pair_rank_weight = related_phenotype_weight
                pair_shared_weight = related_shared_weight
            elseif clone_close
                # Equal loss and size alone can occur for distinct useful structures.
                pair_rank_weight = unrelated_phenotype_weight
            elseif related &&
                abs(complexities[i] - complexities[j]) <= 1 &&
                loss_delta <= L(lineage_loss_rtol) * loss_scale
                pair_rank_weight = lineage_weight
            end

            rank_redundancy[i] += pair_rank_weight

            if pair_shared_weight > 0.0
                shared_occupancy[i] += pair_shared_weight
                shared_occupancy[j] += pair_shared_weight
            end
        end
    end

    birth_min = pool[1].birth
    birth_max = pool[1].birth
    for i in 2:n
        birth = pool[i].birth
        birth < birth_min && (birth_min = birth)
        birth > birth_max && (birth_max = birth)
    end
    birth_span = max(birth_max - birth_min, 1)

    penalized = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    effective_crowding = zeros(Float64, n)
    crowded_mass = 0.0

    for i in 1:n
        directional = min(rank_redundancy[i], crowding_cap)
        shared = min(shared_occupancy[i], crowding_cap)
        redundancy =
            directional_weight * directional + shared_weight * shared
        effective_crowding[i] = redundancy
        crowded_mass += min(redundancy, 1.0)

        recency =
            Float64(pool[i].birth - birth_min) / Float64(birth_span)
        novelty_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + redundancy)

        factor =
            crowding_penalty^redundancy *
            (1.0 - youth_discount * recency * novelty_weight)
        typed_factor = L(factor)

        penalized[i] = if scores[i] > zero(L)
            scores[i] * typed_factor
        elseif scores[i] < zero(L)
            scores[i] / typed_factor
        else
            scores[i]
        end
    end

    # Measure complexity repetition separately from verified structural crowding.
    local_counts = zeros(Int, options.maxsize)
    valid_count = 0
    for complexity in complexities
        if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize
            local_counts[complexity] += 1
            valid_count += 1
        end
    end

    distinct_valid = 0
    for count_at_complexity in local_counts
        count_at_complexity > 0 && (distinct_valid += 1)
    end

    repetition_fraction = if valid_count > 0
        1.0 - distinct_valid / valid_count
    else
        0.0
    end
    crowded_fraction = crowded_mass / n

    # Structural crowding drives most of the adaptation; repeated size alone is weak
    # evidence because many distinct expressions can legitimately share a size.
    crowding_signal =
        0.80 * crowded_fraction + 0.20 * repetition_fraction
    niche_probability = min(
        niche_probability_max,
        niche_probability_base + niche_probability_boost * crowding_signal,
    )

    if rand() < niche_probability
        penalized_order =
            sortperm(1:n; by=i -> (penalized[i], -pool[i].birth))
        seen_complexities = falses(options.maxsize)
        niche_champions = Int[]

        # Retain only the strongest representative of each valid complexity.
        for i in penalized_order
            complexity = complexities[i]
            if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize &&
                !seen_complexities[complexity]
                seen_complexities[complexity] = true
                push!(niche_champions, i)
            end
        end

        if !isempty(niche_champions)
            # Restrict exploration to the better three-fifths of niche champions.
            quality_count =
                max(1, cld(3 * length(niche_champions), 5))
            niche_weights = Vector{Float64}(undef, quality_count)
            frequency_floor = 1.0 / max(pop.n, 1)

            # Adaptive parsimony already supplies rarity pressure when enabled.
            rarity_power =
                options.use_frequency_in_tournament ? 0.35 : 0.50
            rank_denominator = max(quality_count - 1, 1)

            for position in 1:quality_count
                i = niche_champions[position]
                complexity = complexities[i]

                frequency = Float64(
                    running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[
                        complexity
                    ],
                )
                frequency =
                    isfinite(frequency) ? max(frequency, 0.0) : 1.0

                global_rarity =
                    (frequency + frequency_floor)^(-rarity_power)
                local_rarity =
                    Float64(local_counts[complexity])^(-0.35)
                quality_weight = exp(
                    -1.5 * (position - 1) / rank_denominator,
                )

                niche_weights[position] =
                    quality_weight * global_rarity * local_rarity
            end

            selected_position = if quality_count == 1
                1
            else
                weights = StatsBase.Weights(
                    niche_weights,
                    sum(niche_weights),
                )
                StatsBase.sample(weights)
            end

            return pool[niche_champions[selected_position]]
        end
    end

    # Geometric rank selection over the diversity-adjusted scores.
    final_order =
        sortperm(1:n; by=i -> (penalized[i], -pool[i].birth))
    p = clamp(
        Float64(options.tournament_selection_p),
        eps(Float64),
        1.0,
    )

    selected_rank = if p >= 1.0
        1
    else
        ranks = collect(0:(n - 1))
        probabilities = p .* ((1.0 - p) .^ ranks)
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(probabilities, sum(probabilities))
        StatsBase.sample(weights)
    end

    return pool[final_order[selected_rank]]
end

affine_shape_correlation_loss_gen29_8.name: affine_shape_correlation_loss_gen29_8
affine_shape_correlation_loss_gen29_8.code:
"""
    affine_shape_correlation_loss_gen29_8(tree, dataset, options)

Single-pass affine-invariant shape loss with a small bounded raw-error tie-breaker.

Core idea (kept from the parent): rank expressions primarily by the *shape* of their
prediction, i.e. the normalized RMSE that remains after the best affine calibration
`a * prediction + b` is applied, and add a tiny bounded raw-error term so that among
affine-equivalent candidates the one with correctly tuned constants wins (and only the
true target achieves zero loss).

Steps:
 1. Evaluate the tree; bail out with `Inf` on failure or non-finite values.
 2. One streaming pass accumulates Welford moments (`mean`, `m2_p`, `m2_y`, `cov_py`)
    plus the plain sum of squared raw residuals.
 3. Shape term = `sqrt(1 - r^2)` (the affine-residual normalized RMSE), clamped to
    `[0, 1]`.
 4. Raw term = `r/(1+r)` with `r = SSE / m2_y`, a saturating tie-breaker weighted by
    `1/256` so it never overrides shape discovery.

Simplifications relative to the parent:
 * The whole second pass over the data is removed: the affine residual is recovered
   analytically from the first-pass moments as `1 - cov^2/(var_p*var_y)`. This halves
   the data traffic; the loss of precision only matters for candidates that are already
   correlated to within machine epsilon, and those are separated by the raw term anyway.
 * Kahan compensation and the raw-overflow flag are dropped; plain summation plus a
   single `isfinite` check on the accumulated sums is sufficient, and an overflowing
   raw sum simply saturates the bounded term to 1.
 * The dedicated constant-target branch (with its own normalized-MSE loop) and the
   scale-relative variability thresholds are folded into the common path: a constant
   target gives shape term 0 so the ordering is decided monotonically by the raw term,
   and a constant prediction gives shape term 1 (only the mean can be reproduced).
"""
function affine_shape_correlation_loss_gen29_8(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = dataset.n
    if n <= 0 || length(prediction) != n || length(dataset.y) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    zero_l = zero(L)
    one_l = one(L)
    n_l = L(n)

    # Single streaming pass: Welford moments for the affine fit plus raw SSE.
    mean_p = zero_l
    mean_y = zero_l
    m2_p = zero_l
    m2_y = zero_l
    cov_py = zero_l
    raw_sum = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        if !(isfinite(p) && isfinite(y))
            return L(Inf)
        end

        # Raw (uncalibrated) squared error, used only as a tie-breaker later.
        d = p - y
        raw_sum += d * d

        k = L(i)
        delta_p = p - mean_p
        delta_y = y - mean_y

        mean_p += delta_p / k
        mean_y += delta_y / k

        # Covariance update uses the freshly updated target mean.
        cov_py += delta_p * (y - mean_y)
        m2_p += delta_p * (p - mean_p)
        m2_y += delta_y * (y - mean_y)
    end

    if !(isfinite(mean_p) && isfinite(mean_y) &&
         isfinite(m2_p) && isfinite(m2_y) && isfinite(cov_py))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Welford sums can be microscopically negative after roundoff.
    m2_p = max(m2_p, zero_l)
    m2_y = max(m2_y, zero_l)

    # Shape term: normalized RMSE left after the optimal affine calibration.
    shape_term = if m2_y <= zero_l
        # Constant target: affine shape carries no information, ordering falls to raw.
        zero_l
    elseif m2_p <= zero_l
        # Constant prediction can only reproduce the target mean => NMSE == 1.
        one_l
    else
        r2 = (cov_py * cov_py) / (m2_p * m2_y)
        sqrt(clamp(one_l - r2, zero_l, one_l))
    end

    # Bounded raw-error tie-breaker, scale-free via the target's total variation
    # (falling back to a magnitude-based scale when the target is constant).
    denom = m2_y > zero_l ? m2_y : n_l * max(one_l, mean_y * mean_y)
    ratio = raw_sum / denom
    bounded_raw = (isfinite(ratio) && ratio > zero_l) ? ratio / (one_l + ratio) : zero_l
    if !isfinite(ratio)
        # Overflowed / non-finite raw error saturates the bounded term.
        bounded_raw = one_l
    end

    loss_value = shape_term + bounded_raw / L(256)
    return isfinite(loss_value) ? L(max(loss_value, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
end

pareto_niche_age_cost_survival_gen30_0_g.name: pareto_niche_age_cost_survival_gen30_0_gen29_9
pareto_niche_age_cost_survival_gen30_0_g.code:
"""
Synthesizes rank-based age/cost regularization (parent 1) with Pareto-frontier
protection and complexity-niche desaturation (parent 2) into a single
multiplicative scoring scheme.

Motivation: Pure age+cost ranking (parent 1) is robust and scale-free but
blind to structural diversity — it can happily evict a rare, non-dominated
stepping-stone expression just because it is old and mediocre, which stalls
progress on the Pareto front (visible in the trace: many evals spent
re-discovering similar high-complexity, low-improvement expressions instead
of protecting cheap non-dominated forms like `x0*(x2+x1/x3)`). Parent 2's
raw score mixture (age_factor * congestion_factor * pareto_factor) captures
this diversity protection well, but combines unnormalized age with harsh
absolute pareto/congestion multipliers that can dominate age signal
unpredictably across runs with different population age spreads.

This operator keeps parent 1's normalized [0,1] rank scheme for age and cost
(stable across problems/population sizes) as the *base* score, and then
modulates that base multiplicatively by parent 2's Pareto-protection and
niche-congestion factors — preserving age-regularization's turnover
guarantee while still steering removals away from valuable non-dominated
members and away from thinly populated complexity niches, and toward
crowded niches and dominated members. Non-finite individuals are purged
immediately (oldest first), exactly as in parent 2, since they carry zero
evolutionary value.
"""
function pareto_niche_age_cost_survival_gen30_0_gen29_9(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    n = pop.n
    eligible = [i for i in 1:n if !(i in exclude_indices)]
    @assert !isempty(eligible) "No eligible members to replace"

    # --- Step 1: finiteness check (purge NaN/Inf members first, oldest-first tie-break) ---
    is_finite_member = Vector{Bool}(undef, n)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        loss_val = pop.members[i].loss
        cost_val = pop.members[i].cost
        is_finite_member[i] = isfinite(loss_val) && isfinite(cost_val)
    end
    nonfinite_eligible = [i for i in eligible if !is_finite_member[i]]
    if !isempty(nonfinite_eligible)
        # Among non-finite eligible members, remove the oldest (smallest birth) first.
        births_nf = [pop.members[i].birth for i in nonfinite_eligible]
        return nonfinite_eligible[argmin_fast(births_nf)]
    end

    # --- Step 2: complexity, niche congestion, and Pareto dominance over whole population ---
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    max_c = 0
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        c = compute_complexity(pop.members[i], options)
        complexities[i] = c
        if c > max_c
            max_c = c
        end
    end
    niche_counts = zeros(Int, max_c)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        c = complexities[i]
        if c >= 1 && c <= max_c
            niche_counts[c] += 1
        end
    end

    is_dominated = falses(n)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        if !is_finite_member[i]
            is_dominated[i] = true
            continue
        end
        c_i = complexities[i]
        loss_i = pop.members[i].loss
        for j in 1:n
            if i == j || !is_finite_member[j]
                continue
            end
            c_j = complexities[j]
            loss_j = pop.members[j].loss
            if (c_j <= c_i && loss_j < loss_i) || (c_j < c_i && loss_j <= loss_i)
                is_dominated[i] = true
                break
            end
        end
    end

    # --- Step 3: rank-based age & cost scores among eligible (finite) members ---
    births = [pop.members[i].birth for i in eligible]
    costs = [pop.members[i].cost for i in eligible]
    m = length(eligible)

    age_order = sortperm(births)  # ascending birth -> first is oldest
    age_rank = similar(age_order, Float64)
    for (r, idx) in enumerate(age_order)
        age_rank[idx] = (m - r + 1) / m  # oldest -> 1.0
    end

    cost_order = sortperm(costs)  # ascending cost -> last is worst
    cost_rank = similar(cost_order, Float64)
    for (r, idx) in enumerate(cost_order)
        cost_rank[idx] = r / m  # worst -> 1.0
    end

    age_weight = 0.65  # age remains the dominant signal, cost breaks ties
    base_score = age_weight .* age_rank .+ (1 - age_weight) .* cost_rank

    # --- Step 4: modulate base score by Pareto protection and niche congestion ---
    best_local = -1
    best_score = -Inf
    for (local_idx, global_idx) in enumerate(eligible)
        c_i = complexities[global_idx]
        niche_count = (c_i >= 1 && c_i <= max_c) ? niche_counts[c_i] : 1
        # Congestion factor: mildly favors thinning out overcrowded complexity bins.
        congestion_factor = 1.0 + 0.5 * log(Float64(niche_count))
        # Pareto factor: non-dominated members get a protective discount, dominated
        # members get a modest push toward removal, without overwhelming age/cost rank.
        pareto_factor = is_dominated[global_idx] ? 1.2 : 0.6

        score = base_score[local_idx] * congestion_factor * pareto_factor

        if score > best_score
            best_score = score
            best_local = local_idx
        end
    end

    return eligible[best_local]
end

motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen2.name: motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen29_0
motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen2.code:
"""
    motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen29_0(tree::N, dataset, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}

Advanced motif-duplication mutation operator that discovers multi-variable symmetries, rational
saturation kinetics, and linear basis-expansion terms.

# Core Idea
Physical, biological, and mathematical systems are governed by repeated structural motifs across
variables (e.g. Euclidean distances `(x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2`, kinetic energies `0.5*m*(vx^2 + vy^2)`),
rational saturation/feedback laws (e.g. Michaelis-Menten `u/(1+u)`, relativistic factors, harmonic
resistors `1/(1/r1 + 1/r2)`), and linear combination expansions (`w1*f(x1) + w2*f(x2)`).
Standard point mutations cannot build these multi-node correlated structures in a single step.
This operator clones an evolved subexpression ("motif"), applies intelligent symmetry feature
remapping (cyclic shift or targeted feature substitution), and couples it into the expression
using one of three principled templates:
1. **Rational Saturation & Harmonic Coupling**: `target / (1 + motif)` or `1 / (target + motif)`
2. **Coefficient-Scaled Accumulation**: `target + (1.0 * motif)`, inserting an optimizable constant
   so PySR's constant optimizer can immediately fit the relative weight of the duplicated basis.
3. **Plain / Difference Accumulation**: `target ⊕ motif` with biased operators (`+`, `*`, `-`).

# Algorithmic Steps
1. **Guard & Operator Lookup**: Verify binary operators exist; cache indices for `+`, `*`, `/`, `-`.
2. **Dynamic Budget Sizing**: Compute maximum available node headroom `maxsize - tree_size - 1`.
3. **Donor Sampling**: Prefer compound, variable-bearing subtrees; fall back to any fitting subtree.
4. **Target Selection with Self-Coupling Bias**: Bias target selection (45% self-coupling `target === donor`,
   55% uniform tree sampling) to accelerate in-place symmetrization and saturation.
5. **Dual-Mode Feature Remapping**:
   - *Targeted Feature Substitution* (50%): Replace all occurrences of a specific variable in the motif
     with an alternative variable (allows non-cyclic coordinate swaps like `x1 -> x3`).
   - *Cyclic Shift* (50%): Shift all variable indices cyclically `f -> mod1(f + k, nfeatures)`.
6. **Adaptive Coupling Template Dispatch**:
   - If headroom >= 3 and `/`, `+` exist: 30% rational saturation `target / (1 + motif)` or harmonic `1 / (target + motif)`.
   - If headroom >= 3 and `+`, `*` exist: 25% scaled accumulation `target + 1.0 * motif` (ready for constant optimizer).
   - Otherwise: Plain accumulation `target ⊕ motif` biased toward canonical operations (`+`, `*`, `-`).
7. **In-place Splice**: Replace `target` with the new coupled subtree via `set_node!`.

# Improvements vs. Parent (`motif_duplication_rational_coupling_simple_gen24_2`)
- **Added Coefficient-Scaled Coupling (`target + c * motif`)**: Embeds a constant multiplier node
  allowing the downstream constant optimizer (BFGS/Nelder-Mead) to immediately tune the weight of
  the new symmetric term, accelerating convergence on linear combinations and potentials.
- **Added Harmonic/Inverse Coupling (`1 / (target + motif)`)**: Expands rational capabilities to
  parallel resistances, reduced masses, and inverse potential kernels.
- **Added Targeted Feature Substitution**: Complements cyclic shifts by allowing single-variable
  replacements (crucial when equations involve non-contiguous or sparse feature subsets).
- **Dynamic Headroom Budgeting**: Evaluates template cost dynamically rather than discarding large
  motifs under a rigid worst-case 3-node penalty.
- **Biased Self-Coupling**: Samples `target = donor` with 45% probability, vastly improving the
  discovery rate of self-saturating kinetics `u/(1+u)` and direct expansions `x^2 -> x^2 + y^2`.
"""
function motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen29_0(
    tree::N,
    dataset,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 1: Guard & Op Lookup
    options.nops[2] == 0 && return tree

    binops = options.operators.binops
    nbin = options.nops[2]
    idx_add = findfirst(op -> op === (+), binops)
    idx_mul = findfirst(op -> op === (*), binops)
    idx_div = findfirst(op -> op === (/), binops)
    idx_sub = findfirst(op -> op === (-), binops)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 2: Dynamic Budget
    maxsize = hasproperty(options, :maxsize) ? options.maxsize : typemax(Int)
    tree_size = count_nodes(tree)
    max_budget = maxsize - tree_size - 1  # Minimum overhead for binary coupling is 1 node
    max_budget < 1 && return tree

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 3: Donor Sampling
    _fits(t) = count_nodes(t) <= max_budget
    _good(t) = t.degree > 0 && _fits(t) && any(n -> n.degree == 0 && !n.constant, t)

    donor = if count(_good, tree) > 0
        # Prefer compound, variable-bearing subtrees (meaningful symmetry carriers)
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_good))
    elseif count(_fits, tree) > 0
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_fits))
    else
        return tree
    end

    motif = copy(donor)
    s_donor = count_nodes(donor)
    spare = maxsize - tree_size - s_donor  # Extra node headroom available for complex coupling templates

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 4: Target Selection
    # Biasing target selection toward donor increases the frequency of in-place self-symmetrization
    # (e.g. x^2 -> x^2 + y^2) and self-referential saturation (e.g. u -> u / (1 + u)).
    target = (rand(rng) < 0.45) ? donor : rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
    self_coupling = target === donor

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 5: Feature Remapping
    function _collect_features!(node, feats::Vector{Int})
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant && !(node.feature in feats)
                push!(feats, node.feature)
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _collect_features!(get_child(node, i), feats)
            end
        end
        return feats
    end

    function _shift_features!(node, shift::Int, nfeats::Int)
        if node.degree == 0
            node.constant || (node.feature = mod1(node.feature + shift, nfeats))
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _shift_features!(get_child(node, i), shift, nfeats)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    function _substitute_feature!(node, src::Int, dst::Int)
        if node.degree == 0
            if !node.constant && node.feature == src
                node.feature = dst
            end
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _substitute_feature!(get_child(node, i), src, dst)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    if nfeatures > 1
        # Always remap if plain self-coupling would result in trivial u ⊕ u redundancy
        must_remap = self_coupling && (spare < 3 || rand(rng) > 0.4)
        if must_remap || rand(rng) < 0.55
            motif_feats = _collect_features!(motif, Int[])
            if !isempty(motif_feats)
                if rand(rng) < 0.50
                    # Strategy A: Targeted single-feature substitution (replaces x_i with x_j)
                    f_src = rand(rng, motif_feats)
                    candidates = [f for f in 1:nfeatures if f != f_src]
                    if !isempty(candidates)
                        f_dst = rand(rng, candidates)
                        _substitute_feature!(motif, f_src, f_dst)
                    end
                else
                    # Strategy B: Cyclic coordinate shift (isotropic multidimensional shift)
                    _shift_features!(motif, rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1)), nfeatures)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 6: Coupling Template
    target_copy = copy(target)

    # Determine template feasibility based on spare node capacity
    can_rational = (idx_div !== nothing) && (idx_add !== nothing) && (spare >= 3)
    can_scaled = (idx_add !== nothing) && (idx_mul !== nothing) && (spare >= 3)

    r_template = rand(rng)
    new_node = if can_rational && (r_template < 0.30)
        # Template 1: Rational saturation / Harmonic attenuation
        c = constructorof(N)(T; val=one(T))
        if rand(rng) < 0.70
            # Michaelis-Menten / Padé / Relativistic saturation: target / (1 + motif)
            den = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_add, children=(c, motif))
            constructorof(N)(; op=idx_div, children=(target_copy, den))
        else
            # Harmonic / Parallel interaction: 1 / (target + motif)
            sum_node = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_add, children=(target_copy, motif))
            constructorof(N)(; op=idx_div, children=(c, sum_node))
        end
    elseif can_scaled && (r_template < 0.55)
        # Template 2: Coefficient-scaled accumulation target + (1.0 * motif)
        # Constant optimizer can directly tune the coefficient of the duplicated symmetry motif
        c = constructorof(N)(T; val=one(T))
        scaled_motif = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_mul, children=(c, motif))
        op_accum = (idx_sub !== nothing && rand(rng) < 0.25) ? idx_sub : idx_add
        constructorof(N)(; op=op_accum, children=(target_copy, scaled_motif))
    else
        # Template 3: Plain binary coupling target ⊕ motif
        pref = Int[]
        idx_add !== nothing && push!(pref, idx_add)
        idx_mul !== nothing && push!(pref, idx_mul)
        idx_sub !== nothing && push!(pref, idx_sub)

        bin_op = if !isempty(pref) && rand(rng) < 0.80
            pref[rand(rng, 1:length(pref))]
        else
            rand(rng, 1:nbin)
        end
        # Randomize operand order so non-commutative operators explore both arrangements
        children = rand(rng, Bool) ? (target_copy, motif) : (motif, target_copy)
        constructorof(N)(; op=bin_op, children=children)
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 7: In-place Splice
    set_node!(target, new_node)
    return tree
end

# 4-argument convenience method
function motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen29_0(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    return motif_duplication_adaptive_coupling_gen29_0(tree, nothing, options, nfeatures, rng)
end

newton_constant_step_gen29_2.name: newton_constant_step_gen29_2
newton_constant_step_gen29_2.code:
"""
    newton_constant_step_gen29_2(tree, dataset, options, nfeatures, rng)

A data-aware constant-tuning mutation that replaces PySR's usual "randomly
rescale a constant" move with a single Gauss-Newton / least-squares step
computed directly from the training data. The idea: for a randomly chosen
constant leaf with current value `c0`, we estimate (via finite differences)
how the *whole tree's* prediction changes as that one constant is perturbed,
then solve the 1-D weighted least-squares problem that finds the value of the
constant that best explains the residual `y - pred`, under a local-linearity
assumption. This lets constants "snap" toward good values in one mutation
instead of relying on many small random nudges, which is especially useful
for tricky rational/relativistic-looking formulas (e.g. Feynman-style
equations with denominators like `1 + x0/(x1*x2^2)*(1-cos(x3))`) where a
poorly-placed constant dominates the loss and random rescaling struggles to
find the right magnitude/sign efficiently.

Steps:
1. Bail out early if the tree has no constants, or if the dataset has no `y`.
2. Pick a random constant leaf node.
3. Evaluate the tree's predictions at the current constant value (`pred0`).
4. Perturb the constant by a small relative (or absolute, if near zero) step
   `eps`, re-evaluate to get `pred1`, and restore the original value.
5. Form the finite-difference sensitivity `B = (pred1 - pred0) / eps`, i.e.
   d(pred)/d(constant) at each data point.
6. Solve the scalar weighted least-squares problem
   `delta = sum(w .* B .* residual) / sum(w .* B.^2)`
   where `residual = y - pred0`, giving the locally-optimal update to the
   constant (a single Gauss-Newton step for this one parameter).
7. Guard against non-finite/degenerate cases (e.g. B ≈ 0 everywhere, NaNs
   from eval_tree_array) by falling back to the unmodified tree.
8. Clip the step size to avoid wild jumps (helps stability far from the
   linear regime) and write the updated constant back into the node.
"""
function newton_constant_step_gen29_2(
    tree::N,
    dataset,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # Nothing to do without constants or without a scalar target to fit against
    if !has_constants(tree) || dataset.y === nothing
        return tree
    end

    # Pick a random constant leaf to tune
    node = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=t -> (t.degree == 0 && t.constant)))
    c0 = node.val

    # Baseline prediction with the current constant value
    pred0, ok0 = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options.operators)
    if !ok0 || any(!isfinite, pred0)
        return tree
    end

    # Choose a small perturbation, scaled to the constant's own magnitude
    eps = abs(c0) > T(1e-6) ? c0 * T(1e-3) : T(1e-3)
    node.val = c0 + eps
    pred1, ok1 = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options.operators)
    node.val = c0  # restore immediately, regardless of what follows

    if !ok1 || any(!isfinite, pred1)
        return tree
    end

    # Finite-difference sensitivity of the tree's output w.r.t. this constant
    B = (pred1 .- pred0) ./ eps
    residual = dataset.y .- pred0

    # Optionally weight the least-squares fit by per-sample weights if present
    w = dataset.weights === nothing ? one(T) : dataset.weights

    numer = sum(w .* B .* residual)
    denom = sum(w .* B .* B)

    # Guard against degenerate/non-finite updates (e.g. constant has no
    # local effect on the output, so B is ~0 everywhere)
    if !isfinite(numer) || !isfinite(denom) || denom < T(1e-12)
        return tree
    end

    delta = numer / denom

    # Clip the update to avoid overshooting far outside the local-linear regime
    max_step = max(abs(c0), one(T)) * T(10)
    delta = clamp(delta, -max_step, max_step)

    new_val = c0 + delta
    # Only accept the new value if it's finite; otherwise keep the original
    node.val = isfinite(new_val) ? new_val : c0

    return tree
end

motif_duplication_rational_coupling_lore.name: motif_duplication_rational_coupling_lorentz_gen25_gen29_3
motif_duplication_rational_coupling_lore.code:
"""
    motif_duplication_rational_coupling_lorentz_gen25_gen29_3(tree::N, options, nfeatures::Int, rng::AbstractRNG) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}

Motif-duplication mutation that clones an existing subexpression ("motif") and couples it back
into the tree either as a plain accumulation, a self-referential saturating ratio
(`target / (1 + motif)`), or — new in this version — a self-referential **quadratic-root**
ratio (`target / sqrt(1 - motif^2)`).

# Motivation for the change
Tracing a real search (Feynman II.13.23, `x0/sqrt(1-x1^2/x2^2)`) shows the Pareto front getting
permanently stuck on `x0/cos(x1/x2)` and elaborations thereof: `1/cos(u)` is a decent local
surrogate for `1/sqrt(1-u^2)` near `u≈0` (both start `1 + u^2/2 + ...`), but the two forms are not
connected by any single point mutation or by the parent's `target/(1+motif)` template, so the
search spends its whole budget polishing the wrong functional family. Lorentz-factor-style laws
(`rho/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2)`, thin-lens and resistor correction terms, relativistic Doppler/aberration
formulas) all share the same "divide by sqrt(1 - (something)^2)" skeleton. This mutation gives
evolution direct machinery to build that skeleton by squaring a duplicated motif under a `-` and
a `sqrt`, instead of relying on `cos`/`exp` surrogates to be slowly reshaped into it.

# Steps
1. Guard: need at least one binary operator; compute remaining node `slack` for the whole tree.
2. Look up `+`, `*`, `/`, `-` indices and a unary `sqrt` index (if present) once.
3. Pick a coupling mode:
   - `:sqrt_square` (prob. 0.20, needs `sqrt`,`-`,`*`,`/` and enough slack): builds
     `target / sqrt(1 - motif*motif)`.
   - `:add_recip` (prob. 0.25 otherwise, needs `+`,`/`): builds `target / (1 + motif)`.
   - `:plain` (remaining probability): splices `target ⊕ motif` with `⊕` biased toward `+`/`*`.
4. Each mode has its own conservative node budget, since `:sqrt_square` duplicates the motif
   *twice* (it appears squared) plus needs 5 extra structural nodes, `:add_recip` duplicates it
   once plus 3 extra nodes, and `:plain` duplicates it once plus 1 extra node. If the chosen fancy
   template doesn't fit, gracefully degrade to `:plain` rather than aborting the mutation.
5. Donor sampling (two tiers, unchanged in spirit): prefer compound, variable-bearing subtrees
   that fit the mode's budget; otherwise fall back to any fitting subtree.
6. Feature remapping: a single cyclic shift applied to the motif template *before* any duplication
   (so a squared motif stays internally consistent, e.g. genuinely `(v/c)^2` rather than two
   differently-shifted copies), with prob. 0.5, and always applied when `:plain` self-coupling
   would otherwise produce a trivial `u ⊕ u`.
7. Coupling: assemble the template for the chosen mode and splice it in at `target`.

# What changed vs. the parent
- **New `:sqrt_square` template** `target / sqrt(1 - motif^2)`, directly reachable only via
  duplication (the motif must appear identically twice), giving evolution a shortcut to
  relativistic/Lorentz-style laws that the old `target/(1+motif)` template could not express.
- **Per-mode budgets** replace the parent's single conservative budget, since the new template's
  worst-case node cost (duplicate motif twice) is materially larger than the additive-rational
  template's.
- **Graceful degradation**: if the sampled fancy mode doesn't fit the remaining size budget, the
  mutation falls back to `:plain` instead of bailing out entirely, so the mutation still does
  useful work on tightly-sized trees.
- Feature shifting is applied once to a template subtree before any duplication, guaranteeing
  squared/duplicated copies are mutually consistent.
"""
function motif_duplication_rational_coupling_lorentz_gen25_gen29_3(
    tree::N,
    options,
    nfeatures::Int,
    rng::AbstractRNG,
) where {T,N<:AbstractExpressionNode{T}}
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 1: guard
    options.nops[2] == 0 && return tree

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 2: operator lookup
    binops = options.operators.binops
    nbin = options.nops[2]
    idx_add = findfirst(op -> op === (+), binops)
    idx_mul = findfirst(op -> op === (*), binops)
    idx_div = findfirst(op -> op === (/), binops)
    idx_sub = findfirst(op -> op === (-), binops)
    idx_sqrt = options.nops[1] > 0 ? findfirst(op -> op === sqrt, options.operators.unaops) : nothing

    maxsize = hasproperty(options, :maxsize) ? options.maxsize : typemax(Int)
    slack = maxsize - count_nodes(tree)
    slack < 2 && return tree

    can_sqrt_mode = idx_sqrt !== nothing && idx_sub !== nothing && idx_mul !== nothing && idx_div !== nothing
    can_add_mode = idx_div !== nothing && idx_add !== nothing

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 3: mode selection
    r = rand(rng)
    mode = if can_sqrt_mode && r < 0.20 && slack >= 6
        :sqrt_square
    elseif can_add_mode && r < 0.45
        :add_recip
    else
        :plain
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 4: per-mode budget
    # extra_cost = worst-case count of newly-introduced structural nodes (ops/consts, excluding
    # the target copy, which is size-neutral since it replaces the original target node).
    # motif_mult = number of independent motif copies the template needs.
    extra_cost, motif_mult = if mode === :sqrt_square
        (5, 2)   # div + sqrt + sub + const + mul; motif appears squared (two copies)
    elseif mode === :add_recip
        (3, 1)   # div + add + const; motif appears once
    else
        (1, 1)   # single new binary op; motif appears once
    end

    budget = fld(slack - extra_cost, motif_mult)
    if budget < 1
        # Fancy template doesn't fit in the remaining size budget: degrade to plain coupling.
        mode = :plain
        budget = slack - 1
        budget < 1 && return tree
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 5: donor (two tiers)
    _fits(t) = count_nodes(t) <= budget
    _good(t) = t.degree > 0 && _fits(t) && any(n -> n.degree == 0 && !n.constant, t)

    donor = if count(_good, tree) > 0
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_good))
    elseif count(_fits, tree) > 0
        rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree, filter=_fits))
    else
        return tree  # nothing fits the budget
    end

    target = rand(rng, NodeSampler(; tree))
    self_coupling = target === donor

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 6: cyclic feature shift
    function _shift_features!(node, shift)
        if node.degree == 0
            node.constant || (node.feature = mod1(node.feature + shift, nfeatures))
        else
            for i in 1:(node.degree)
                _shift_features!(get_child(node, i), shift)
            end
        end
        return node
    end

    motif_template = copy(donor)
    # Only the plain mode risks a trivial `u ⊕ u`; the ratio templates are meaningful even
    # when the motif duplicates the target (e.g. self-saturating `v/sqrt(1-v^2)`-type forms).
    must_shift = self_coupling && mode === :plain
    if nfeatures > 1 && (must_shift || rand(rng) < 0.5)
        _shift_features!(motif_template, rand(rng, 1:(nfeatures - 1)))
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Step 7: coupling
    target_copy = copy(target)

    new_node = if mode === :sqrt_square
        # Self-referential quadratic-root saturation: target / sqrt(1 - motif^2)
        # Two independent copies of the (already feature-shifted) template give a
        # structurally-honest square, matching Lorentz-factor / lens / resistor correction laws.
        motif1 = copy(motif_template)
        motif2 = copy(motif_template)
        one_c = constructorof(N)(T; val=one(T))
        sq = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_mul, children=(motif1, motif2))
        inner = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_sub, children=(one_c, sq))
        den = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_sqrt, children=(inner,))
        constructorof(N)(; op=idx_div, children=(target_copy, den))
    elseif mode === :add_recip
        # Self-referential saturation / correction factor: target / (1 + motif)
        c = constructorof(N)(T; val=one(T))
        den = constructorof(N)(; op=idx_add, children=(c, motif_template))
        constructorof(N)(; op=idx_div, children=(target_copy, den))
    else
        # Plain coupling, biased toward the canonical accumulators `+` and `*`
        pref = Int[]
        idx_add !== nothing && push!(pref, idx_add)
        idx_mul !== nothing && push!(pref, idx_mul)
        bin_op = if !isempty(pref) && rand(rng) < 0.65
            pref[rand(rng, 1:length(pref))]
        else
            rand(rng, 1:nbin)
        end
        # Randomize operand order so non-commutative operators explore both arrangements
        children = rand(rng, Bool) ? (target_copy, motif_template) : (motif_template, target_copy)
        constructorof(N)(; op=bin_op, children=children)
    end

    set_node!(target, new_node)
    return tree
end

pareto_shielded_sampled_age_survival_gen.name: pareto_shielded_sampled_age_survival_gen27_0_gen29_4
pareto_shielded_sampled_age_survival_gen.code:
"""
    pareto_shielded_sampled_age_survival_gen27_0_gen29_4(pop::Population{T,L,N}, options::AbstractOptions; exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[])::Int where {T,L,N}

Synthesizes the two parents: cheap per-complexity Pareto shielding + sampled
age pressure (parent 2's efficiency) combined with parent 1's richer scoring
model (non-finite purge, niche-congestion desaturation, graded Pareto
discount/penalty) instead of a hard-binary shield and full O(n) / O(n^2) scans.

# Synthesis rationale
* Parent 1's exhaustive O(n^2) pairwise dominance check is expensive and its
  full-population scan runs every generation. We keep its *scoring idea*
  (age × congestion × Pareto-factor, with non-finite members purged first)
  but replace the exact dominance test with parent 2's cheap O(n) proxy:
  the lowest-cost member at each complexity value is treated as
  "non-dominated" (shielded), which is a fast, good approximation of the
  Pareto frontier.
* Parent 2's sampling strategy (draw `tournament_selection_n` random slots)
  is reused to keep the operator O(tournament_selection_n) per call instead
  of O(n), but instead of picking the *oldest* sampled slot outright, we
  score each sampled slot with parent 1's composite formula so that
  congestion and Pareto-protection still shape which of the sampled
  candidates is culled — not just raw age.
* A single relaxed full-population fallback (same scoring, exclusion-only)
  guarantees a valid return when the random sample is unlucky or entirely
  excluded/shielded, mirroring parent 2's single-fallback simplicity.

# Steps
1. One O(n) pass: compute complexity, finiteness, per-complexity population
   counts (congestion), per-complexity cheapest-cost index (Pareto shield),
   and global birth range (for age normalization).
2. Draw `n_sample = clamp(tournament_selection_n, 2, n)` random candidates;
   score each with the composite formula and keep the highest-scoring,
   non-excluded one.
3. If nothing valid was sampled, fall back to a full scan using the same
   scoring formula, respecting only `exclude_indices` (shield relaxed).
4. Last-resort fallback: first non-excluded index, else 1.
"""
function pareto_shielded_sampled_age_survival_gen27_0_gen29_4(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    options::AbstractOptions;
    exclude_indices::Vector{Int}=Int[],
)::Int where {T,L,N}
    n = pop.n
    if n == 0
        return 1
    end

    # ---- Step 1: single O(n) pass gathering complexity/finiteness/congestion/shield/age stats ----
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    is_finite_member = Vector{Bool}(undef, n)

    min_birth = pop.members[1].birth
    max_birth = pop.members[1].birth

    # Track cheapest-cost member per complexity value (Pareto shield proxy).
    best_idx_at_c = Dict{Int,Int}()
    best_cost_at_c = Dict{Int,L}()
    niche_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        c = compute_complexity(pop.members[i], options)
        complexities[i] = c

        b = pop.members[i].birth
        if b < min_birth
            min_birth = b
        end
        if b > max_birth
            max_birth = b
        end

        niche_counts[c] = get(niche_counts, c, 0) + 1

        loss_val = pop.members[i].loss
        cost_val = pop.members[i].cost
        finite_i = isfinite(loss_val) && isfinite(cost_val)
        is_finite_member[i] = finite_i

        if finite_i
            prev_cost = get(best_cost_at_c, c, typemax(L))
            if cost_val < prev_cost
                best_cost_at_c[c] = cost_val
                best_idx_at_c[c] = i
            end
        end
    end

    shielded = falses(n)
    for (_, idx) in best_idx_at_c
        shielded[idx] = true
    end

    birth_range = Float64(max_birth - min_birth + 1)

    # ---- Composite score helper (higher = more replaceable) ----
    function replacement_score(i::Int)
        @inbounds if !is_finite_member[i]
            # Non-finite individuals are purged first; among them, oldest first.
            return 1e9 + Float64(max_birth - pop.members[i].birth + 1)
        else
            age_factor = Float64(max_birth - pop.members[i].birth + 1) / birth_range
            c_i = complexities[i]
            niche_count = get(niche_counts, c_i, 1)
            congestion_factor = 1.0 + log(Float64(niche_count))
            # Graded Pareto protection: shielded (cheapest-at-complexity) members
            # get a strong survival discount; others get accelerated pressure.
            pareto_factor = shielded[i] ? 0.2 : 1.5
            return age_factor * congestion_factor * pareto_factor
        end
    end

    # ---- Step 2: sampled scoring over a small random pool (cheap, allocation-light) ----
    n_sample = clamp(options.tournament_selection_n, 2, n)
    best_candidate_idx = -1
    best_candidate_score = -Inf

    @inbounds for _ in 1:n_sample
        i = rand(1:n)
        (i in exclude_indices) && continue
        score = replacement_score(i)
        if score > best_candidate_score
            best_candidate_score = score
            best_candidate_idx = i
        end
    end

    # ---- Step 3: fallback — full scan with same scoring, shield relaxed implicitly ----
    if best_candidate_idx == -1
        @inbounds for i in 1:n
            (i in exclude_indices) && continue
            score = replacement_score(i)
            if score > best_candidate_score
                best_candidate_score = score
                best_candidate_idx = i
            end
        end
    end

    # ---- Step 4: last-resort fallback ----
    if best_candidate_idx == -1
        for i in 1:n
            if !(i in exclude_indices)
                return i
            end
        end
        return 1
    end

    return best_candidate_idx
end

structural_signature_quality_gated_niche.name: structural_signature_quality_gated_niche_tournament_gen29_5
structural_signature_quality_gated_niche.code:
"""
    structural_signature_quality_gated_niche_tournament_gen29_5(
        pop, running_search_statistics, options
    )

Crowding-aware tournament selection that fuses the clone/lineage suppression and
quality-gated niche repopulation of the parent operators with an explicit
structural-identity signal, aimed at the failure mode seen on tasks like
feynman_II_13_23: the Pareto front repeatedly refines the *same* rational-function
skeleton (e.g. `x0 + (... / (x2*(C/x1)+C))`) for many complexities in a row instead
of trying a structurally different decomposition. That stagnation happens because
loss+complexity proximity alone under-detects "the same idea wearing different
constants," so redundant descendants keep winning tournaments and starve novel
structures.

Synthesis and steps:

 1. Sample an enlarged tournament pool and compute the usual
    adaptive-parsimony-adjusted costs (as in both parents).
 2. For every pair (worse vs. better), first check an exact structural signature
    (a hash of the printed expression tree). Identical signatures are treated as
    guaranteed duplicates and receive the strongest crowding weight, since they are
    the *same* expression modulo evaluation noise. Failing that, fall back to the
    original same-complexity/near-equal-loss phenotype proxy, and finally to a small
    fractional penalty for close parent/child/sibling lineage with similar
    complexity and loss. This layered check catches redundant re-derivations that
    the loss/complexity heuristic alone misses, while still not punishing honestly
    different descendants.
 3. Apply a mild youth discount (attenuated by crowding) so fresh, non-redundant
    structures are nudged forward without letting fresh clones dodge suppression.
 4. Adapt the niche-exploration probability to observed pool crowding, as before,
    but make the quality-gated niche choice favor rarity more aggressively (rarity
    weighted by frequency^2 among the best two-thirds of complexity champions) so
    starved complexity bands are repopulated more decisively once genuine crowding
    (including structural duplication) is detected.
 5. Otherwise, apply the standard geometric tournament ladder over the
    diversity-adjusted scores.

Assumptions: `string(member.tree)` gives a stable textual representation whose hash
is a cheap, conservative proxy for exact structural identity (differing only in
which constants attached to which nodes would still usually differ in string form,
so this signal is intentionally strict and used only as the strongest crowding
tier, not a replacement for the softer proxies).
"""
function structural_signature_quality_gated_niche_tournament_gen29_5(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}
    # Mild tunables: exact structural duplicates dominate crowding evidence,
    # phenotype/lineage proxies are secondary, youth and niche moves are nudges.
    pool_scale = 1.5
    crowding_penalty = 1.35
    exact_duplicate_weight = 1.5
    lineage_weight = 0.25
    clone_loss_rtol = 1e-6
    lineage_loss_rtol = 1e-2
    youth_discount = 0.03
    niche_probability_base = 0.08
    niche_probability_boost = 0.12
    niche_probability_max = 0.20
    rarity_power = 2.0

    # Sample a larger pool so local crowding and niche occupancy are observable.
    n_base = options.tournament_selection_n
    pool_size = min(pop.n, max(n_base, round(Int, pool_scale * n_base)))
    pool = StatsBase.sample(pop.members, pool_size; replace=false)
    n = length(pool)

    # Compute complexity, structural signature, and the adaptive-parsimony score.
    complexities = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    signatures = Vector{UInt64}(undef, n)
    scores = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    adaptive_parsimony_scaling = L(options.adaptive_parsimony_scaling)

    for i in 1:n
        member = pool[i]
        complexity = compute_complexity(member, options)
        complexities[i] = complexity
        # Cheap structural fingerprint: hash of the printed expression tree.
        signatures[i] = hash(string(member.tree))

        if options.use_frequency_in_tournament
            frequency = if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize
                L(running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[complexity])
            else
                zero(L)
            end
            scores[i] =
                member.cost * exp(adaptive_parsimony_scaling * frequency)
        else
            scores[i] = member.cost
        end
    end

    # Better representatives establish the local crowding baseline.
    order = sortperm(scores)
    crowding = zeros(Float64, n)

    for a in 2:n
        i = order[a]
        li = pool[i].loss
        scale_i = max(abs(li), eps(L))
        weight = 0.0

        for b in 1:(a - 1)
            j = order[b]
            lj = pool[j].loss

            if signatures[i] == signatures[j]
                # Same printed structure: near-certain redundant re-derivation.
                weight += exact_duplicate_weight
                continue
            end

            loss_scale = max(scale_i, abs(lj))
            same_phenotype =
                complexities[i] == complexities[j] &&
                abs(li - lj) <= L(clone_loss_rtol) * loss_scale

            if same_phenotype
                # Strong evidence that the later member is redundant.
                weight += 1.0
                continue
            end

            parent_i = pool[i].parent
            parent_j = pool[j].parent
            related =
                (parent_i != 0 && parent_i == parent_j) ||
                (parent_i != 0 && parent_i == pool[j].ref) ||
                (parent_j != 0 && parent_j == pool[i].ref)

            # Shared ancestry is penalized only when phenotype is also close.
            if related &&
                abs(complexities[i] - complexities[j]) <= 1 &&
                abs(li - lj) <= L(lineage_loss_rtol) * loss_scale
                weight += lineage_weight
            end
        end

        crowding[i] = weight
    end

    # Find the age range once; recency is used only as a mild novelty preference.
    birth_min = pool[1].birth
    birth_max = pool[1].birth
    for i in 2:n
        birth = pool[i].birth
        birth < birth_min && (birth_min = birth)
        birth > birth_max && (birth_max = birth)
    end
    birth_span = max(birth_max - birth_min, 1)

    penalized = Vector{L}(undef, n)
    crowded_count = 0

    for i in 1:n
        redundancy = crowding[i]
        redundancy > 0.0 && (crowded_count += 1)

        recency = (pool[i].birth - birth_min) / birth_span
        novelty_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + redundancy)

        # Clone/lineage penalties dominate; youth matters most for uncrowded forms.
        factor =
            crowding_penalty^redundancy *
            (1.0 - youth_discount * recency * novelty_weight)
        typed_factor = L(factor)

        # Sign-safe adjustment: larger factors always make the score less fit.
        penalized[i] = if scores[i] > zero(L)
            scores[i] * typed_factor
        elseif scores[i] < zero(L)
            scores[i] / typed_factor
        else
            scores[i]
        end
    end

    # Increase explicit niche exploration when the sampled pool shows monopoly,
    # whether due to structural duplication or phenotype/lineage crowding.
    crowded_fraction = crowded_count / n
    niche_probability = min(
        niche_probability_max,
        niche_probability_base +
        niche_probability_boost * crowded_fraction,
    )

    if rand() < niche_probability
        # Keep one best representative per valid complexity niche.
        penalized_order = sortperm(penalized)
        seen_complexities = falses(options.maxsize)
        niche_champions = Int[]

        for i in penalized_order
            complexity = complexities[i]
            if 0 < complexity <= options.maxsize &&
                !seen_complexities[complexity]
                seen_complexities[complexity] = true
                push!(niche_champions, i)
            end
        end

        if !isempty(niche_champions)
            # Quality gate: consider the better two-thirds of niche champions,
            # but weight rarity super-linearly so genuinely starved bands win
            # decisively once real crowding has been detected.
            quality_count = max(1, cld(2 * length(niche_champions), 3))
            best_idx = niche_champions[1]
            best_frequency = Float64(
                running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[
                    complexities[best_idx]
                ],
            )
            best_rarity_score = best_frequency^rarity_power
            best_score = penalized[best_idx]

            for position in 2:quality_count
                i = niche_champions[position]
                frequency = Float64(
                    running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[
                        complexities[i]
                    ],
                )
                rarity_score = frequency^rarity_power

                if rarity_score < best_rarity_score ||
                    (rarity_score == best_rarity_score && penalized[i] < best_score)
                    best_idx = i
                    best_frequency = frequency
                    best_rarity_score = rarity_score
                    best_score = penalized[i]
                end
            end

            return pool[best_idx]
        end
    end

    # Standard geometric tournament ladder over diversity-adjusted scores.
    p = options.tournament_selection_p
    chosen_idx = if p == 1.0
        argmin_fast(penalized)
    else
        ranks = collect(0:(n - 1))
        probabilities = p * ((1 - p) .^ ranks)
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(probabilities, sum(probabilities))
        selected_rank = StatsBase.sample(weights)

        if selected_rank == 1
            argmin_fast(penalized)
        else
            bottomk_fast(penalized, selected_rank)[2][end]
        end
    end

    return pool[chosen_idx]
end

"""
    standardized_angular_shape_calibration_loss_gen29_7(tree, dataset, options)

Evaluate functional alignment via standardized Euclidean coordinate geometry with
directional correlation enforcement and non-saturating calibration coupling.

# Core Idea & Geometric Formulation
1. **Cancellation-Free Standardized Shape Metric**:
   Instead of computing correlation via variance-covariance differences (which suffer
   from catastrophic cancellation when `r ≈ 1` due to subtracting two nearly equal
   floats), we evaluate the standardized difference `u_i - v_i` directly, where
   `u = (p - mean_p) / std_p` and `v = (y - mean_y) / std_y`. The squared Euclidean
   distance `d_u^2 = (1/n) sum((u_i - v_i)^2)` identically equals `2 * (1 - r)`.
   Because this is an exact sum of non-negative squares, it computes the residual
   shape error to full machine precision without numerical cancellation.

2. **Directional Correlation & Smooth Anti-Correlation Penalty**:
   Standard affine least-squares assigns zero loss to inverted shapes (`r = -1`).
   This loss enforces positive alignment:
   - When `r > 0` (`d_u^2 < 2`), shape error is `sqrt(d_u^2 * (1 - d_u^2 / 4)) = sqrt(1 - r^2)`.
   - When `r <= 0` (`d_u^2 >= 2`), shape error transitions with C1 smoothness to
     `1.0 + 0.125 * (d_u^2 - 2)^2`, penalizing anti-correlated predictions and
     preventing sign-inversion local minima.

3. **Sublinear Calibration Coupling for Constant Optimization**:
   The raw calibration error is coupled via the smooth sublinear map
   `C = E_raw / sqrt(1 + E_raw^2)`. At `E_raw = 0`, this has a unit derivative
   `dC/dE = 1.0`, ensuring BFGS / gradient descent receives full, non-vanishing
   gradient signals to calibrate constants, unlike quadratic penalties whose
   gradients vanish near zero.

4. **Two-Pass Compensated Accumulation**:
   Pass 1 computes stable Welford moments and relative variability thresholds.
   Pass 2 computes standardized shape residuals and normalized raw errors using
   Neumaier summation for high numerical accuracy.

# Improvements Over Parent
- Replaces unconstrained affine regression with directional standardized geometry,
  eliminating sign-inversion traps where anti-correlated trees (`r = -1`) scored 0.
- Replaces explicit slope/intercept residual evaluation with cancellation-free
  standardized coordinates `(u_i - v_i)^2 = 2(1-r)`.
- Replaces the heavily suppressed quadratic calibration `1/256 * (raw / (1 + raw))`
  with a sublinear calibration `1/16 * (E_raw / sqrt(1 + E_raw^2))` that maintains
  well-scaled non-zero gradients for constant optimization.
- Employs C1 smooth boundary transitions and Neumaier summation.
- Retains zero parsimony penalty inside the loss operator.
"""
function standardized_angular_shape_calibration_loss_gen29_7(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = dataset.n
    if n <= 0 || length(prediction) != n || length(dataset.y) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    zero_l = zero(L)
    one_l = one(L)
    two_l = L(2)
    quarter_l = L(0.25)
    eighth_l = L(0.125)
    calib_weight = one_l / L(16)
    n_l = L(n)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Pass 1: Welford statistics for target and prediction
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    mean_p = zero_l
    mean_y = zero_l
    m2_p = zero_l
    m2_y = zero_l
    max_abs_p = zero_l
    max_abs_y = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        if !(isfinite(p) && isfinite(y))
            return L(Inf)
        end

        max_abs_p = max(max_abs_p, abs(p))
        max_abs_y = max(max_abs_y, abs(y))

        k = L(i)
        delta_p = p - mean_p
        delta_y = y - mean_y

        mean_p += delta_p / k
        mean_y += delta_y / k

        m2_p += delta_p * (p - mean_p)
        m2_y += delta_y * (y - mean_y)
    end

    if !(isfinite(mean_p) && isfinite(mean_y) && isfinite(m2_p) && isfinite(m2_y))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    m2_p = max(m2_p, zero_l)
    m2_y = max(m2_y, zero_l)

    std_p = sqrt(m2_p / n_l)
    std_y = sqrt(m2_y / n_l)

    # Relative variability thresholds
    rel_tol = sqrt(eps(L))
    target_is_variable = std_y > rel_tol * max(one_l, max_abs_y)
    pred_is_variable = std_p > rel_tol * max(one_l, max_abs_p)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Case A: Constant Target
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    if !target_is_variable
        target_scale = max(one_l, max_abs_y)
        inv_scale = one_l / target_scale
        raw_sum = zero_l
        raw_c = zero_l

        @inbounds for i in 1:n
            p = L(prediction[i])
            y = L(dataset.y[i])
            diff = (p - y) * inv_scale
            term = diff * diff

            if !isfinite(term)
                return L(Inf)
            end

            # Neumaier compensated summation
            t = raw_sum + term
            if abs(raw_sum) >= abs(term)
                raw_c += (raw_sum - t) + term
            else
                raw_c += (term - t) + raw_sum
            end
            raw_sum = t
        end

        raw_mse = max(zero_l, (raw_sum + raw_c) / n_l)
        raw_rmse = sqrt(raw_mse)
        calib = raw_rmse / sqrt(one_l + raw_mse)
        return isfinite(calib) ? L(max(calib, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Case B: Constant Prediction (with variable target)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    inv_std_y = one_l / std_y
    if !pred_is_variable
        raw_sum = zero_l
        raw_c = zero_l

        @inbounds for i in 1:n
            p = L(prediction[i])
            y = L(dataset.y[i])
            norm_res = (p - y) * inv_std_y
            term = norm_res * norm_res

            if !isfinite(term)
                return L(Inf)
            end

            t = raw_sum + term
            if abs(raw_sum) >= abs(term)
                raw_c += (raw_sum - t) + term
            else
                raw_c += (term - t) + raw_sum
            end
            raw_sum = t
        end

        raw_mse = max(zero_l, (raw_sum + raw_c) / n_l)
        raw_rmse = sqrt(raw_mse)
        calib = raw_rmse / sqrt(one_l + raw_mse)
        # Uncorrelated baseline shape error is 1.0
        loss_val = one_l + calib_weight * calib
        return isfinite(loss_val) ? L(max(loss_val, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
    end

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Pass 2: Standardized Shape Discrepancy & Raw Error (both variable)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    inv_std_p = one_l / std_p

    shape_sum = zero_l
    shape_c = zero_l
    raw_sum = zero_l
    raw_c = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        # Standardized coordinates: u_i and v_i have zero mean and unit variance
        u_i = (p - mean_p) * inv_std_p
        v_i = (y - mean_y) * inv_std_y
        diff_u = u_i - v_i
        term_shape = diff_u * diff_u

        # Scale-normalized raw residual
        norm_raw = (p - y) * inv_std_y
        term_raw = norm_raw * norm_raw

        if !(isfinite(term_shape) && isfinite(term_raw))
            return L(Inf)
        end

        # Neumaier summation for shape metric
        t_s = shape_sum + term_shape
        if abs(shape_sum) >= abs(term_shape)
            shape_c += (shape_sum - t_s) + term_shape
        else
            shape_c += (term_shape - t_s) + shape_sum
        end
        shape_sum = t_s

        # Neumaier summation for raw calibration
        t_r = raw_sum + term_raw
        if abs(raw_sum) >= abs(term_raw)
            raw_c += (raw_sum - t_r) + term_raw
        else
            raw_c += (term_raw - t_r) + raw_sum
        end
        raw_sum = t_r
    end

    # d_u_sq = (1/n) sum((u_i - v_i)^2) = 2 * (1 - r)
    d_u_sq = max(zero_l, (shape_sum + shape_c) / n_l)

    # Directional shape metric with C1 smooth anti-correlation penalty
    shape_loss = if d_u_sq < two_l
        # Positive correlation (r > 0): 1 - r^2 = d_u_sq * (1 - d_u_sq / 4)
        sq_val = max(zero_l, d_u_sq * (one_l - quarter_l * d_u_sq))
        sqrt(sq_val)
    else
        # Negative or zero correlation (r <= 0): smooth C1 penalty starting at 1.0
        delta = d_u_sq - two_l
        one_l + eighth_l * delta * delta
    end

    # Raw calibration coupling with unit gradient near zero
    raw_mse = max(zero_l, (raw_sum + raw_c) / n_l)
    raw_rmse = sqrt(raw_mse)
    calib_loss = raw_rmse / sqrt(one_l + raw_mse)

    # Combined loss
    total_loss = shape_loss + calib_weight * calib_loss

    return isfinite(total_loss) ? L(max(total_loss, zero_l)) : L(Inf)
end

"""
    novelty_weighted_quality_gated_niche_tournament_gen19_gen30_0(
        pop, running_search_statistics, options
    )

Crowding-aware tournament selection that refines the previous clone/lineage
crowding model with an explicit structural-identity check, so that
same-complexity/same-loss "convergent" solutions (different expressions that
happen to fit similarly well) are no longer punished as harshly as true
duplicates.

Motivation (seen in trace): search repeatedly re-derives variations of the
same rational-function motif and stalls, apparently because members that
reach similar loss/complexity via genuinely different structures (e.g. a
`sin`-based vs a `cos`-based rewrite) were being crowded out identically to
exact clones. This removes a useful source of structural novelty just when it
matters most for escaping a local structural basin.

Changes vs. parent (`..._gen18_4`):

 1. For every pool member we also compute a cheap structural signature
    (the printed form of its expression tree). Two members are only treated
    as *true clones* if their signature matches exactly; same
    complexity/loss without signature equality is now labeled a *convergent
    pair* and receives a lighter, separate penalty weight, distinct from both
    the lineage penalty and the full clone penalty.
 2. Lineage-relation penalty weight is trimmed slightly since some of its
    former job (catching near-identical descendants) is now handled more
    precisely by the signature check.
 3. Niche exploration, youth discount, adaptive niche probability, and the
    final geometric tournament ladder are kept structurally the same as the
    parent, since those parts are not implicated by the observed stagnation.

always worsen a score, and factors below one always improve it.

function novelty_weighted_quality_gated_niche_tournament_gen19_gen30_0(
    pop::Population{T,L,N},
    running_search_statistics::RunningSearchStatistics,
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::PopMember{T,L,N} where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE,N}

    # lineage relations are lighter nudges; youth is the lightest nudge.

    exact_clone_weight = 1.0
    convergent_form_weight = 0.45
    lineage_weight = 0.2

            else
                zero(L)
            end
            scores[i] =
                member.cost * exp(adaptive_parsimony_scaling * frequency)
        else
            scores[i] = member.cost
        end
    end

    # Better representatives establish the local crowding baseline.
    order = sortperm(scores)
    crowding = zeros(Float64, n)

    for a in 2:n
        i = order[a]
        li = pool[i].loss
        scale_i = max(abs(li), eps(L))
        weight = 0.0

        for b in 1:(a - 1)

            same_complexity_loss =
                complexities[i] == complexities[j] &&
                abs(li - lj) <= L(clone_loss_rtol) * loss_scale

                    weight += exact_clone_weight

                    # occupies the same performance slot, but should not be
                    # suppressed as aggressively as an exact clone.

    birth_max = pool[1].birth
    for i in 2:n

        else

        end
    end

    crowded_fraction = crowded_count / n
    niche_probability = min(
        niche_probability_max,
        niche_probability_base +
        niche_probability_boost * crowded_fraction,

        seen_complexities = falses(options.maxsize)
        niche_champions = Int[]

            )
            best_score = penalized[best_idx]

            for position in 2:quality_count
                i = niche_champions[position]
                frequency = Float64(
                    running_search_statistics.normalized_frequencies[
                        complexities[i]
                    ],
                )

                if frequency < best_frequency ||
                    (frequency == best_frequency && penalized[i] < best_score)
                    best_idx = i
                    best_frequency = frequency
                    best_score = penalized[i]
                end
            end

            return pool[best_idx]
        end
    end

    # Standard geometric tournament ladder over diversity-adjusted scores.
    p = options.tournament_selection_p
    chosen_idx = if p == 1.0
        argmin_fast(penalized)
    else
        ranks = collect(0:(n - 1))
        probabilities = p * ((1 - p) .^ ranks)
        weights = StatsBase.Weights(probabilities, sum(probabilities))
        selected_rank = StatsBase.sample(weights)

        if selected_rank == 1
            argmin_fast(penalized)
        else
            bottomk_fast(penalized, selected_rank)[2][end]
        end
    end

    return pool[chosen_idx]
end

streamlined_affine_angular_loss_gen30_5.name: streamlined_affine_angular_loss_gen30_5
streamlined_affine_angular_loss_gen30_5.code:
"""
    streamlined_affine_angular_loss_gen30_5(tree, dataset, options)

A streamlined two-pass loss operator that evaluates functional shape via optimal affine
calibration `a * prediction + b` and uses a small, bounded raw-error term to prefer exact
calibrated constants.

### Core Idea & Steps:
1. **Pass 1 (Moments)**: Accumulates means, sample variances, and cross-covariance using
   Welford's algorithm in a single clean loop.
2. **Affine Calibration**: Solves for the optimal least-squares slope `a = cov(p, y) / var(p)`
   and intercept `b = mean_y - a * mean_p`.
3. **Pass 2 (Direct Residuals)**: Directly evaluates the affine fitted residual `(a*p + b - y)^2`
   and raw residual `(p - y)^2`. Evaluating fitted residuals directly avoids catastrophic
   subtractive cancellation when correlation is near 1.
4. **Composition**: Computes normalized affine RMSE (shape error in [0, 1]) and adds a small,
   bounded raw NMSE penalty (`raw_nmse / (1 + raw_nmse) * (1/256)`) as a calibration tie-breaker.

### Simplifications from Parent:
- Removed Kahan-compensated summation and its associated state/branching overhead across both
  passes, dramatically improving evaluation throughput.
- Replaced custom scale-relative variability heuristic thresholds and `max_abs` tracking with
  standard machine-epsilon variance guards.
- Consolidated overflow handling and constant-target fallback into streamlined, branchless logic.
"""
function streamlined_affine_angular_loss_gen30_5(
    tree::Union{AbstractExpression{T},AbstractExpressionNode{T}},
    dataset::Dataset{T,L},
    options::AbstractOptions,
)::L where {T<:DATA_TYPE,L<:LOSS_TYPE}
    prediction, completed = eval_tree_array(tree, dataset.X, options)
    if !completed || isnothing(prediction)
        return L(Inf)
    end

    n = dataset.n
    if n <= 0 || length(prediction) != n || length(dataset.y) != n
        return L(Inf)
    end

    zero_l = zero(L)
    one_l = one(L)
    n_l = L(n)
    eps_l = eps(L)

    # Pass 1: Stable Welford accumulation of sample means, variances, and covariance
    mean_p = zero_l
    mean_y = zero_l
    var_p = zero_l
    var_y = zero_l
    cov_py = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        if !(isfinite(p) && isfinite(y))
            return L(Inf)
        end

        k = L(i)
        dp = p - mean_p
        dy = y - mean_y

        mean_p += dp / k
        mean_y += dy / k

        var_p += dp * (p - mean_p)
        var_y += dy * (y - mean_y)
        cov_py += dp * (y - mean_y)
    end

    if !(isfinite(mean_p) && isfinite(mean_y) && isfinite(var_p) && isfinite(var_y) && isfinite(cov_py))
        return L(Inf)
    end

    # Fallback for constant target: scale-normalized bounded RMSE
    if var_y <= eps_l
        raw_sse = zero_l
        @inbounds for i in 1:n
            diff = L(prediction[i]) - L(dataset.y[i])
            raw_sse += diff * diff
        end
        raw_mse = raw_sse / n_l
        target_scale = max(one_l, mean_y * mean_y)
        loss = sqrt(raw_mse / (target_scale + raw_mse))
        return isfinite(loss) ? L(loss) : L(Inf)
    end

    # Optimal affine calibration coefficients (a * p + b)
    slope = zero_l
    intercept = mean_y
    if var_p > eps_l
        slope = cov_py / var_p
        intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_p
        if !(isfinite(slope) && isfinite(intercept))
            slope = zero_l
            intercept = mean_y
        end
    end

    # Pass 2: Direct accumulation of affine fitted residuals and raw residuals
    affine_sse = zero_l
    raw_sse = zero_l

    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        p = L(prediction[i])
        y = L(dataset.y[i])

        raw_res = p - y
        raw_sse += raw_res * raw_res

        fitted = muladd(slope, p, intercept)
        aff_res = fitted - y
        affine_sse += aff_res * aff_res
    end
